sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Preface

sentences.zh: 夫文以化成，惟聖之高義；

translations.literal: As for wen (writing and culture), by it transformation is accomplished; this alone is the lofty principle of the sages;
translations.idiomatic: Writing is what shapes civilization through moral transformation—the supreme teaching of the sages.

sentences.zh: 行而不遠，前史之格言。

translations.literal: If it does not travel far it cannot endure—a maxim the older histories never cease to cite.
translations.idiomatic: What fails to spread far will not last—a truth the histories hammer home again and again.

sentences.zh: 是以溫洛禎圖，綠字元其丕業；

translations.literal: Therefore there were auspicious charts at the Luo, and green characters inaugurated their great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the prophetic charts drawn from the Luo and the mystic green script that founded their mighty reign.

sentences.zh: 苑山靈篆，金簡成其帝載。

translations.literal: On Yuan Mountain, spirit seal-script; on golden slips were completed the records of their emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-seal writing on Mount Yuan, imperial deeds engraved on golden slips—the lore that crowned their rule.

sentences.zh: 既而書契之道聿興，鐘石之文逾廣，移風俗于王化，崇孝敬于人倫，經緯乾坤，彌綸中外，故知文之時義大哉遠矣！

translations.literal: Thereupon the way of writing and signing flourished; script on bells and stones grew ever broader; it shifted customs toward royal transformation and exalted filial reverence within human relations; it ordered heaven and earth and embraced what lies within and beyond—thus one knows how vast and far-reaching is the timely significance of wen!
translations.idiomatic: Then came the full flowering of written records; inscriptions on bells and stones multiplied; literature reshaped folkways under royal civilizing influence and upheld filial duty within the bonds of kin; it structured heaven and earth and spanned all within the realm and beyond—so we see how immense, how enduring, is the meaning of letters in their age.

sentences.zh: 洎姬曆雲季，歌頌滋繁，荀宋之流，導源自遠，總金羈而齊騖，揚玉軑而並馳，言泉會於九流，交律詣於六變。

translations.literal: Down to the closing age of the Zhou calendar, songs and eulogies multiplied; the line of Xun and Song guided the source from afar; bridled alike they raced together, raising jade axles as they galloped side by side; springs of language converged in the nine currents; patterned verse attained the six transformations.
translations.idiomatic: By the twilight of Zhou rule, hymns and praise poetry had grown lush; masters such as Xun Qing and Song Yu carried that tradition from remote antiquity—writers who coursed together like matched teams, whose eloquence poured into every school of thought and whose regulated verse mastered every tonal shift.

sentences.zh: 自時已降，軌躅同趨，西都賈馬，耀靈蛇于掌握，東漢班張，發雕龍於綈槧，俱標稱首，咸推雄伯。

translations.literal: From that time downward their tracks converged; in the Western Capital Jia Yi and Sima Xiangru made the divine serpent glitter in the palm; in Eastern Han Ban Gu and Zhang Heng unleashed the carved dragon on bamboo slips; all were reckoned foremost and alike hailed as champions.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward writers trod the same path: at Chang'an, Jia Yi and Sima Xiangru wielded prose like the luminous serpent in legend; in Later Han, Ban Gu and Zhang Heng carved draconic brilliance onto their drafts—each claimed the summit of renown and won universal acclaim as a literary lord.

sentences.zh: 逮乎當塗基命，文宗鬱起，三祖葉其高韻，七子分其麗則，《翰林》總其菁華，《典論》詳其澡絢，彬蔚之美，競爽當年。

translations.literal: When the Wei house assumed the mandate, literary masters rose in splendor; the Three Ancestors lent their lofty tones, the Seven Masters shared their polished norms; the "Hanlin" gathered their finest blossoms, the Dianlun expounded their polished brilliance—the lush splendor of their style vied in brilliance through those years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei inherited Heaven's charge, a galaxy of writers arose: its founding rulers set the pitch of high style, the Seven Masters of Jian'an each refined its grace; the Hanlin anthology distilled their essence, Cao Pi's Dianlun anatomized their craft—never had lettered beauty flourished so fiercely in one generation.

sentences.zh: 獨彼陳王，思風遒舉，備乎典奧，懸諸日月。

translations.literal: Only Prince Chen of that age—his thinking wind rose forcefully; complete in canonical depth, it hangs beside sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Chen set his genius soaring—fully steeped in the canon, a brilliance that stands beside sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 及金行纂極，文雅斯盛，張載擅銘山之美，陸機挺焚研之奇，潘夏連輝，頡頏名輩，並綜采繁縟，杼軸清英，窮廣內之青編，緝平臺之麗曲，嘉聲茂跡，陳諸別傳。

translations.literal: When the Jin house (metal phase) assumed the throne, letters flourished ever more; Zhang Zai excelled in the beauty of mountain inscriptions, Lu Ji displayed the marvel of burning inkstones to polish verse; Pan Yue and Xia Tong shone in succession, neck-and-neck with celebrated peers; together they wove lush ornament and spun pure brilliance, exhausting the blue-bound archives within the palace and compiling the lovely songs of the Ping Terrace—their fair reputations and splendid deeds are recorded in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin took the mandate, literature bloomed: Zhang Zai memorialized mountains with unmatched grace; Lu Ji wrung marvels from inkstones half consumed by flame; Pan Yue and Xia Tong matched radiance with the greatest names of their day; each lavishly embroidered yet kept the shuttle bright, mining the imperial stacks for lore and weaving Ping Terrace songs—their fuller stories appear in separate traditions.

sentences.zh: 至於吉甫、太沖，江右之才傑；

translations.literal: As for Jifu (Ying Zhen) and Taichong (Zuo Si)—outstanding talents of Jiangyou;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Ying Zhen (Jifu) and Zuo Si (Taichong)—stars among the writers south of the river;

sentences.zh: 曹毗、庾闡，中興之時秀。

translations.literal: Cao Pi and Yu Chan—the timely elite of the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: and Cao Pi together with Yu Chan—the finest Eastern Jin had to offer at its revival.

sentences.zh: 信乃金相玉潤，林薈川沖，埒美前修，垂裕來葉。

translations.literal: Truly they were gold in appearance and jade in luster, forest gathered and stream deep—rivaling the excellence of earlier masters and laying up blessings for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: They truly combined bronze resonance with polished jade—learning broad as a grove, depth like a river—matching the old masters and leaving an inheritance for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 今撰其鴻筆之彥，著之《文苑》云。

translations.literal: Now I compile those eminent exemplars of the great brush and present them in this "Garden of Letters."
translations.idiomatic: Here we gather the foremost wielders of the brush and set them down under the heading "Literary Garden."

sentences.zh: 應貞

translations.literal: Ying Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen

sentences.zh: 應貞，字吉甫，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之子也。

translations.literal: Ying Zhen, style Jifu, was a man of Nandun in Runan, son of Wei Palace Attendant Ying Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen, courtesy name Jifu, came from Nandun in Runan and was the son of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自漢至魏，世以文章顯，軒冕相襲，為郡盛族。

translations.literal: From Han down to Wei, generation after generation they showed distinction in letters; high caps and carriage canopies succeeded one another—they were a great clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For generations from Han through Wei the family had risen on literary talent; rank followed rank until they stood among the commandery's greatest houses.

sentences.zh: 貞善談論，以才學稱。

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled in discourse and was famed for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen excelled at debate and was celebrated for his erudition.

sentences.zh: 夏侯玄有盛名，貞詣玄，玄甚重之。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xuan had a great reputation; Zhen visited Xuan, and Xuan thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan's fame was immense; when Ying Zhen called on him, Xuan treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 舉高第，頻曆顯位。

translations.literal: He was nominated in the highest grade and repeatedly passed through eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked at the top of his cohort and rose through a series of prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍大將軍，以為參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was General Who Guards the Army, he appointed him Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu still held the title General Who Guards the Army, he named Ying Zhen army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When [Wu] ascended the throne, [Zhen] was promoted to Palace Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Ying Zhen became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝于華林園宴射，貞賦詩最美。

translations.literal: When the emperor feasted and shot at Hualin Garden, Zhen's poem was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: During an archery banquet at Hualin Garden, Ying Zhen's poem outshone every other.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：悠悠太上，人之厥初。

translations.literal: Its words said: far, far back in highest antiquity was man's primal origin.
translations.idiomatic: The poem begins: from remotest antiquity came mankind's earliest beginnings.

sentences.zh: 皇極肇建，彝倫攸敷。

translations.literal: The imperial pole was first established, and the constant norms were thereby spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The royal center was first established, and the enduring norms of human conduct were laid out.

sentences.zh: 五德更運，應錄受符。

translations.literal: The five virtues turned in succession; matching Heaven's register, he received the mandate tally.
translations.idiomatic: The succession of the Five Virtues turned, and Heaven's register matched as the mandate token was received.

sentences.zh: 陶唐既謝，天曆在虞。

translations.literal: After Tao Tang had declined, Heaven's calendar rested with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao of Tao Tang passed from the stage, Heaven's succession passed to Shun of Yu.

sentences.zh: 于時上帝，乃顧惟眷。

translations.literal: At that time the Lord on High then turned His gaze with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Lord on High turned His gaze and showed His favor.

sentences.zh: 光我晉祚，應期納禪。

translations.literal: He brightened our Jin fortune and, responding to the appointed season, received the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: He brightened the house of Jin and, at the appointed time, received the abdication of the throne.

sentences.zh: 位以龍飛，文以豹變。

translations.literal: The throne was taken by dragon-flight, and culture was renewed by leopard-transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was taken like a dragon soaring, and culture was renewed like a leopard changing its spots.

sentences.zh: 玄澤滂流，仁風潛扇。

translations.literal: Dark beneficence poured in torrents, and a benevolent wind secretly fanned abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Dark beneficence poured forth in abundance, and a humane breeze quietly stirred.

sentences.zh: 區內宅心，方隅回面。

translations.literal: Within the realm hearts made their home, and at the four corners faces turned back.
translations.idiomatic: All within the realm gave their hearts, and from every quarter faces turned toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 天垂其象，地耀其文。

translations.literal: Heaven hung its emblems, and earth shone its patterned brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven displayed its signs, and earth gleamed with its patterned brilliance.

sentences.zh: 鳳鳴朝陽，龍翔景雲。

translations.literal: The phoenix cried toward the morning sun, and the dragon soared amid glorious clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix sang facing the morning sun, and the dragon soared amid glorious clouds.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾重穎，蓂莢載芬。

translations.literal: Fine grain bore double ears, and lucky pods spread their fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent grain bore double heads, and auspicious pods spread their fragrance.

sentences.zh: 率土咸寧，人胥悅欣。

translations.literal: All the earth alike was tranquil, and every man was pleased and glad.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven was at peace, and every man rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 恢恢皇度，穆穆聖容。

translations.literal: Vast, vast was the imperial measure, and solemn, solemn the sage countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial way was broad and far-reaching, and the sage sovereign's bearing was grave and serene.

sentences.zh: 言思其允，貌思其恭。

translations.literal: In speech he thought of sincerity, and in appearance he thought of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In speech he sought truthfulness, and in demeanor he sought reverence.

sentences.zh: 在視斯明。

translations.literal: In what he looked upon, thus he was luminous.
translations.idiomatic: In what he saw, he was luminous.

sentences.zh: 在聽斯聰。

translations.literal: In what he heard, thus he was penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: In what he heard, he was penetrating.

sentences.zh: 登庸以德，明試以功。

translations.literal: He promoted the worthy by virtue and clearly tested men by merit.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted men by virtue and clearly tested them by merit.

sentences.zh: 其恭惟何？

translations.literal: His reverence—what was it?
translations.idiomatic: What was the nature of his reverence?

sentences.zh: 昧旦丕顯。

translations.literal: Before dawn he was greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn he was already at work, making his virtue brilliantly plain.

sentences.zh: 無義不經，無理不踐。

translations.literal: No righteousness went unexpounded, and no right principle went untrodden.
translations.idiomatic: No principle of righteousness went unuttered, and no right path went unfollowed.

sentences.zh: 行舍其華，言去其辯。

translations.literal: In conduct he set aside ornament, and in speech he put away empty argument.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct he set aside mere ornament, and in speech he put away empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 遊心至虛，同規易簡。

translations.literal: His mind wandered to utmost emptiness, and all followed the same rule of ease and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His heart rested in utmost emptiness, and all followed the same rule of ease and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 六府孔修，九有來踐。

translations.literal: The six treasuries were greatly ordered, and the nine domains came to tread his rule.
translations.idiomatic: The six treasuries were fully ordered, and the nine regions all came to follow his rule.

sentences.zh: 澤罔不被，化莫不加。

translations.literal: His bounty was nowhere unspread, and his transforming influence was nowhere not applied.
translations.idiomatic: His bounty reached everywhere, and his transforming power touched all.

sentences.zh: 聲教南暨，西漸流沙。

translations.literal: His voice and teaching reached southward and penetrated westward even to the Flowing Sands.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing influence spread to the south and westward even to the Flowing Sands.

sentences.zh: 幽人肆險，遠國忘遐；

translations.literal: Recluses left their fastnesses, and distant states forgot their remoteness;
translations.idiomatic: Recluses abandoned their strongholds, and distant lands forgot how far away they were;

sentences.zh: 越常重譯，充牣皇家。

translations.literal: Yuechang came with repeated interpreters and filled the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Yuechang sent envoys through repeated interpreters, thronging the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 峨峨列辟，赫赫武臣。

translations.literal: Towering, towering stood the arrayed lords, and blazing, blazing the martial ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords stood towering in rank, and martial ministers shone in splendor.

sentences.zh: 內和五品，外威四賓。

translations.literal: Within he harmonized the five ranks of kin, and without he awed the four frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Within he harmonized the five grades of kin, and without he overawed the four frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 順時貢職，入覲天人。

translations.literal: Following the seasons they paid tribute and duty and entered to behold Heaven's son.
translations.idiomatic: At the proper seasons they paid tribute and came to court to behold the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 備言錫命，羽蓋硃輪。

translations.literal: Edicts of appointment were fully bestowed, with feathered canopies and vermilion wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts of appointment were lavishly bestowed, with feathered canopies and vermilion wheels marking their honors.

sentences.zh: 貽宴好會，不常厥數。

translations.literal: He granted banquets and friendly gatherings without fixing their number.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished feasts and cordial gatherings without counting how often.

sentences.zh: 神心所授，不言而喻。

translations.literal: What the divine mind imparted was understood without words being spoken.
translations.idiomatic: What the divine heart conveyed needed no words to make it understood.

sentences.zh: 于時肆射，弓矢斯具。

translations.literal: At that time came the shooting display, and bows and arrows were there prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the archery display, with bows and arrows all ready.

sentences.zh: 發彼互的，有酒斯飫。

translations.literal: They loosed arrows at those layered targets, and where there was wine there was feasting.
translations.idiomatic: They loosed arrows at the layered targets, and wine was there for all to enjoy.

sentences.zh: 文武之道，厥猷未墜。

translations.literal: The way of civil and martial affairs had not yet fallen from its grand design.
translations.idiomatic: The way of wen and wu had not yet fallen from practice.

sentences.zh: 在昔先王，射御茲器。

translations.literal: In ancient times the former kings practiced archery and charioteering with these implements.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the former kings practiced archery and charioteering with such gear.

sentences.zh: 示武懼荒，過則有失。

translations.literal: They displayed martial readiness to fear dissipation, for excess then brought failure.
translations.idiomatic: They showed martial readiness to guard against decadence, for excess brings failure.

sentences.zh: 凡厥羣后，無懈於位。

translations.literal: For all those assembled lords, let there be no slackening in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Let all the assembled lords never slacken in their duties.

sentences.zh: 初置太子中庶子官，貞與護軍長史孔恂俱為之。

translations.literal: When the office of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent was first created, Zhen and Army-Guards Chief Clerk Kong Xun were both appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's junior mentorate was first established, Ying Zhen and Kong Xun, chief clerk of the Army Guard, were the first to hold the post.

sentences.zh: 後遷散騎常侍，以儒學與太尉荀顗撰定新禮，未施行。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; on the basis of ru learning he together with Grand Commandant Xun Yi compiled the new ritual code, but it was not put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He later became a cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, as a Confucian scholar, helped Grand Commandant Xun Yi draft a new ritual code that never came into force.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年卒，文集行於世。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, he died; his collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi, he died, leaving a literary collection that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弟純。

translations.literal: Younger brother Chun.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ying Chun:

sentences.zh: 純子紹，永嘉中，至黃門郎，為東海王越所害。

translations.literal: Chun's son Shao, in the Yongjia era, reached the post of Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gates and was killed by the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Chun's son Ying Shao rose to palace attendant under the Yellow Gates in the Yongjia years and was put to death by Sima Yue, the Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 純弟秀，秀子詹，自有傳。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Xiu; Xiu's son Zhan—each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Chun's brother Ying Xiu and Xiu's son Ying Zhan are biographed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 成公綏

translations.literal: Cheng Gongshui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui

sentences.zh: 成公綏，字子安，東郡白馬人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Gongshui, style Zi'an, was a man of Baima in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui, courtesy name Zi'an, came from Baima in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰敏，博涉經傳。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive, and he read widely in the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was precocious and devoured the classics and their exegesis.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，不營資產，家貧歲饑，常晏如也。

translations.literal: By nature he had few desires and did not pursue property; his household was poor and the harvest failed year after year, yet he was always serene.
translations.idiomatic: Content with little, he acquired no lands or fortune; even when famine gnawed his household he remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 少有俊才，詞賦甚麗，閑默自守，不求聞達。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; his ci and fu were very beautiful; quietly he kept to himself and sought neither fame nor advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted from youth, he wrote rhapsodies of striking polish yet lived in quiet retirement, courting neither renown nor office.

sentences.zh: 時有孝烏，每集其廬舍，綏謂有反哺之德，以為祥禽，乃作賦美之，文多不載。

translations.literal: At that time there was a filial crow that always roosted on his cottage; Sui said it had the virtue of bringing food back to its parents, deemed it an auspicious bird, and composed a fu praising it—the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: A crow famed for filial devotion nested habitually on his roof; Cheng judged it an auspicious creature embodying the virtue of feeding one's parents in old age and wrote a rhapsody in its praise (most of which is omitted here).

sentences.zh: 又以「賦者貴能分賦物理，敷演無方，天地之盛，可以致思矣。

translations.literal: He also said, "In fu pieces one prizes the ability to analyze the categories of things and unfold principles without fixed pattern; the fullness of heaven and earth may thereby be brought within contemplation.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that "a true fu must dissect the nature of things and expound principle without rigid formula—the grandeur of heaven and earth becomes thinkable through such writing.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古人未之有賦，豈獨以至麗無文，難以辭贊；

translations.literal: Surveying the ancients, none had composed a fu on it—is it only because its supreme beauty lacked patterned wording and was hard to praise in phrases?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no one had attempted such a piece—perhaps because beauty too overwhelming defies eloquence;

sentences.zh: 不然，何其闕哉？」

translations.literal: If not, why was it lacking?"
translations.idiomatic: or else why should the tradition have stayed silent?"

sentences.zh: 遂為《天地賦》曰：惟自然之初載兮，道虛無而玄清，太素紛以溷淆兮，始有物而混成，何元一之芒昧兮，廓開闢而著形。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the "Fu on Heaven and Earth," which says: Only at nature's first bearing—ah!—the Way was empty and void, dark and pure; Grand Simplicity in confusion and mixture—ah!—then there were things and blended completion; how the primal One was dim and obscure—ah!—broadly opening and establishing, forms appeared.
translations.idiomatic: With that he composed his "Rhapsody on Heaven and Earth," opening: In nature's first dawn the Way lay empty, dark, and still; Grand Simplicity churned in confusion till matter blended into form; how dim the primal One—then space opened wide and shapes took hold.

sentences.zh: 爾乃清濁剖分，玄黃判離。

translations.literal: Then pure and turbid were cut apart; dark and yellow were separated.
translations.idiomatic: Then pure and turbid split apart, dark and yellow drew clear of each other.

sentences.zh: 太極既殊，是生兩儀，星辰煥列，日月重規，天動以尊，地靜以卑，昏明迭照，或盈或虧，陰陽協氣而代謝，寒暑隨時而推移。

translations.literal: The Supreme Pole already distinct—therefrom the Two Forms were born; stars and constellations blaze in array, sun and moon double their circles; heaven moves thereby to be honored, earth is still thereby to be low; dusk and dawn alternate in shining, now full now waning; yin and yang harmonize qi and replace each other, cold and heat follow the seasons and shift.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Supreme Pole stood apart, the Two Forms arose; stars blazed in ranks, sun and moon wheeled in paired orbits; heaven moved and gained honor, earth rested and kept humility; light and dark took turns, fullness and waning followed in turn; yin and yang breathed together in ceaseless exchange, cold and heat advanced with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 三才殊性，五行異位，千變萬化，繁育庶類，授之以形，稟之以氣。

translations.literal: The three powers have distinct natures, the five phases occupy different positions; a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations breed and multiply the myriad kinds—granting them form, endowing them with qi.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers bore distinct natures, the five phases took separate stations; through endless change the myriad creatures multiplied, each granted a body, each endowed with breath.

sentences.zh: 色表文采，聲有音律，覆載無方，流形品物。

translations.literal: Color displays patterned splendor, sound has pitch and measure; covering and bearing have no fixed direction, flowing forms sort the classes of things.
translations.idiomatic: Colors showed their patterned splendor, sounds obeyed pitch and measure; heaven and earth enfolded all without limit, shaping every kind of thing.

sentences.zh: 鼓以雷霆，潤以慶雲，八風翱翔，六氣氤氳。

translations.literal: Beaten with thunder and lightning, moistened with auspicious clouds; the eight winds soar and wheel, the six qi blend and suffuse.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder drummed the sky, auspicious clouds brought rain; the eight winds swept on broad wings, the six vapors mingled and rose.

sentences.zh: 蚑行蠕動，方聚類分，鱗殊族別，羽毛異群，各含精而熔冶，咸受范于陶鈞，何滋育之罔極兮，偉造化之至神！

translations.literal: Crawling legs and writhing motion, in squares gather and by kind divide; scales differ in clans, feathers and down differ in flocks; each holds essence and is smelted and refined, all receive pattern from the potter's wheel—ah, how nurturing has no bound!—how grand the utmost divinity of creation-and-transformation!
translations.idiomatic: Crawling things and writhing creatures gathered by kind and clan; scaled tribes parted, feathered flocks divided; each held its essence refined, each took shape from the cosmic wheel—how boundless the nurture, how wondrous the godlike art of creation!

sentences.zh: 若天懸象成文，列宿有章，三辰燭耀，五緯重光，河漢委蛇而帶天，虹蜺偃蹇於昊蒼，望舒彌節於九道，義和正轡于中黃，眾星回而環極，招搖運而指方，白獸峙據於參伐，青龍垂尾于心房，玄龜匿首於女虛，硃鳥奮翼于注張，帝皇正坐于紫宮，輔臣列位於文昌，垣屏駱驛而珠連，三台差池而雁翔，軒轅華布而曲列，攝提鼎峙而相望。

translations.literal: As for heaven: suspended images form patterns, the arrayed lodges have design; the three luminaries candle and shine, the five cords double their light; the River and Han wind sinuous and belt the sky, rainbows recline and linger in vast azure; Wang Shu slows his pace along the nine paths, Yi He straightens reins at central yellow; the host of stars wheel and encircle the pole, Twinkling Indicator moves and points direction; the White Beast stands firm at Shen and Fa, the Azure Dragon trails its tail at Heart and Room, the Black Tortoise hides its head at Woman and Void, the Vermilion Bird spreads wings at Lightning and Spread; the August Emperor sits upright in the Purple Palace, assisting ministers range their places at Literary Glory; wall-screens run continuous like pearls strung, the Three Terraces stagger like wild geese in flight, Chariot Pivot blooms in curved array, Bootstrap stars stand like tripods facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hung signs that wrote their text: constellations marched in ordered ranks, the three luminaries burned bright, the five planets doubled their gleam; the Milky Way coiled like a sash across the sky, rainbows arched through the azure vault; Wang Shu slowed the moon along its nine paths, Yi He reined the sun at the yellow center; stars wheeled around the pole, the Twinkling Indicator swung and marked the quarters; the White Tiger held Shen and Fa, the Azure Dragon trailed Heart and Room, the Black Tortoise crouched at Woman and Void, the Vermilion Bird spread wings at Lightning and Spread; the celestial emperor sat enthroned in the Purple Palace, his ministers ranked in Literary Glory; palace walls linked like strung pearls, the Three Terraces staggered like flying geese, the Chariot Pivot bloomed in curving lines, the Bootstrap stars stood like facing tripods.

sentences.zh: 若乃徵瑞表祥，災變呈異，交會薄蝕，抱暈帶珥，流逆犯曆，譴悟象事，蓬容著而妖害生，老人形而主受喜，天矢黃而國吉祥，彗孛發而世所忌。

translations.literal: As for omens of fortune displaying auspice, calamitous changes presenting strangeness: conjunctions, near-approaches, thin eclipses, halos embraced and pendants at the ear; streaming, retrograde, calendar-violating offenses, warnings and awakenings in image-affairs; bushy forms appear and demonic harm is born, the Old Man takes shape and the ruler receives joy; the Sky Arrow turns yellow and the state is auspicious and fortunate, comets and broom-stars rise and the age dreads them.
translations.idiomatic: Omens of blessing and signs of disaster alike appeared: conjunctions and near-eclipses, halos ringed with ear-pendants; stars streamed backward and breached the calendar, heaven's images warned and admonished; bushy stars foretold harm, the Old Man star promised joy to the throne; the Sky Arrow glowed yellow for the state's good fortune, comets and broom-stars rose—and ages dreaded them.

sentences.zh: 爾乃旁觀四極，俯察地理，川瀆浩汗而分流，山嶽磊落而羅峙，滄海沆漭而四周，懸圃隆崇而特起，昆吾嘉於南極，燭龍曜於北址，扶桑高於萬仞，尋木長於千里，昆侖鎮于陰隅，赤縣據於辰巳。

translations.literal: Then viewing the four extremities on every side, looking down to survey earthly patterns: rivers and channels vast and branching divide their flow, mountains and peaks piled and jumbled stand ranged; the blue sea billows and surges on every side, the Hanging Garden rises lofty and stands apart; Kunwu is splendid at the southern pole, Torch Dragon shines at the northern foothills; Fusang towers above ten thousand ren, Xunmu grows long for a thousand li; Kunlun guards the yin corner, the Red Territory occupies chen and si.
translations.idiomatic: Then I surveyed the four quarters and looked down on earth's lay: rivers poured in vast division, mountains stood piled in ranks; the blue sea surged on every side, the Hanging Garden rose alone in grandeur; Kunwu shone at the southern pole, the Torch Dragon blazed in the northern foothills; Fusang towered beyond measure, Xunmu stretched a thousand li; Kunlun anchored the dark corner, the Red Territory held the southeast.

sentences.zh: 於是八十一域，區分方別；

translations.literal: Thereupon eighty-one regions, divided by direction and distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus eighty-one domains were marked and set apart by quarter;

sentences.zh: 風乖俗異，險斷阻絕，萬國羅布，九州並列。

translations.literal: winds diverge and customs differ, peril cuts off and barriers block; ten thousand states spread like a net, the nine provinces stand side by side.
translations.idiomatic: winds shifted and customs changed, barriers cut off the perilous ways; myriad states spread like a net, the nine provinces stood in row.

sentences.zh: 青冀白壤，荊衡塗泥，海岱赤埴，華梁青黎，兗帶河洛，揚有江淮。

translations.literal: Qing and Ji have white soil, Jing and Heng have mud for coating; Hai and Dai have red clay, Hua and Liang have green and black; Yan girds the He and Luo, Yang has the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Ji bore white earth, Jing and Heng clay and mud; Hai and Dai red soil, Hua and Liang green and black loam; Yan embraced the He and Luo, Yang held the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 辯方正土，經略建邦，王圻九服，列國一同，連城比邑，深池高墉，康衢交路，四達五通。

translations.literal: Discerning directions and rectifying soil, planning borders and establishing states; the royal domain and nine domains, the arrayed states unified as one; linked cities compare with towns, deep moats and high walls; broad avenues cross roads, four reach and five connect.
translations.idiomatic: They measured the quarters, laid out the land, and founded realms; the royal domain and nine domains stood as one, states ranked in unity; cities linked with towns, deep moats and high walls rose; broad crossroads met, roads running four ways and five.

sentences.zh: 東至陽穀，西極泰濛，南暨丹砲，北盡空同。

translations.literal: East reaching Yang Valley, west extending to Tai Meng, south reaching Dan Pao, north ending at Kongtong.
translations.idiomatic: East to Yang Valley, west to Tai Meng, south to Dan Pao, north to Kongtong.

sentences.zh: 遐方外區，絕域殊鄰，人首蛇軀，烏翼龍身，衣毛被羽，或介或鱗，棲林浮水，若獸若人，居於大荒之外，處於巨海之濱。

translations.literal: Distant regions beyond the outer zones, extreme territories with strange neighbors: human heads and serpent bodies, bird wings and dragon forms; clothed in fur and draped in feathers, some armored some scaled; dwelling in forests and floating on water, like beasts yet like men—they live beyond the Great Waste, they dwell on the shores of the vast sea.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the far marches, in lands of alien neighbors, lived beings with human heads and serpent bodies, bird wings and dragon forms; clad in fur or feather, armored in shell or scale; dwelling in forests, floating on waters, half beast and half man—they lived past the Great Waste, on the shores of the outer sea.

sentences.zh: 於是六合混一而同宅，宇宙結體而括囊，渾元運流而無窮，陰陽循度而率常，回動糾紛而乾乾，天道不息而自強。

translations.literal: Thereupon the six harmonies blend as one and share one dwelling; cosmos and universe knit their bodies and enfold like a sack; primordial unity moves and flows without end, yin and yang follow measure and lead the constant; turning motion tangles and strives—qian qian; heaven's Way never ceases and strengthens itself.
translations.idiomatic: Then the six directions merged in one dwelling, the universe bound its body like a folded sack; primordial unity flowed without end, yin and yang kept their measured course; ceaseless turning strove ever onward—heaven's Way never rested, ever renewed its strength.

sentences.zh: 統群生而載育，人托命於所系，尊太一於上皇，奉萬神於五帝，故萬物之所宗，必敬天而事地。

translations.literal: Governing all life and bearing and nurturing, humans entrust their lives to what they depend on; honoring Grand Unity at the Supreme August, serving the myriad spirits at the Five Emperors—therefore what the myriad things revere must revere heaven and serve earth.
translations.idiomatic: It sustains all life and nurtures every kind; humanity hangs its fate on what binds it; it honors Grand Unity on high, serves the myriad spirits through the Five Emperors—thus all that lives must revere heaven and serve earth.

sentences.zh: 若乃共工赫怒，天柱摧折，東南俄其既傾，西北豁而中裂，斷鰲足而續毀，煉玉石而補缺。

translations.literal: As for Gong Gong in blazing rage, the heaven-pillar was shattered and broken; the southeast suddenly already tilted, the northwest gaped and split at the center; cutting off the ao's legs yet further ruin, smelting jade and stone to mend the gap.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong Gong raged in fury, the pillar of heaven snapped; the southeast suddenly tilted, the northwest split open; they severed the ao's legs yet ruin continued, smelted jade and stone to patch the breach.

sentences.zh: 豈斯事之有征，將言者之虛設？

translations.literal: Are these matters truly attested, or are the speakers' words empty invention?
translations.idiomatic: Were these events truly witnessed—or mere inventions of storytellers?

sentences.zh: 何陰陽之難測，偉二儀之奓闊！

translations.literal: How yin and yang are hard to fathom—how grand the vast expanse of the Two Forms!
translations.idiomatic: How unfathomable yin and yang—how vast and grand the Two Forms!

sentences.zh: 坤厚德以載物，乾資始而至大，俯盡鑒於有形，仰蔽視于所蓋，遊萬物而極思，故一言於天外。

translations.literal: Kun with thick virtue bears the myriad things; qian with beginning-to-endowment reaches the greatest; bending down, fully mirror all that has form; lifting up, cover and view what is roofed; roaming the myriad things to the utmost in thought—therefore one word beyond heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Kun bears all things in deep virtue; qian begins all and reaches the greatest; gazing down I mirrored every formed thing, looking up I saw only what heaven covers; roaming all creation to the limit of thought—thus one word beyond the sky.

sentences.zh: 綏雅好音律，嘗當暑承風而嘯，泠然成曲，因為《嘯賦》曰：逸羣公子，體奇好異，敖世忘榮，絕棄人事，希高慕古，長想遠思，將登箕山以抗節，浮滄海以遊志。

translations.literal: Sui was refined and fond of pitch and temperament; once in summer heat he received the wind and whistled—cool and clear it formed a melody; thereupon he composed the "Fu on Whistling," which says: A free-roaming lord's son, in body strange and loving the unusual, disdaining the age and forgetting glory, utterly abandoning human affairs, hoping for heights and admiring antiquity, long pondering and far thinking—about to ascend Mount Ji to uphold integrity, float the blue sea to roam his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui loved music deeply; one sweltering day he whistled into the breeze until cool, pure tones shaped themselves into melody—and thus arose his "Rhapsody on Whistling," which begins: A free-spirited noble son, strange in body and hungry for the unusual, scorned the world's honors and cast off its affairs, reached toward the ancients and brooded on distant things, ready to climb Mount Ji to keep his integrity, to drift the blue sea and roam where his spirit led.

sentences.zh: 於是延友生，集同好，精性命之至機，研道德之玄奧，湣流俗之未悟，獨超然而先覺，狹世路之厄僻，仰天衢而高蹈，邈跨俗而遺身，乃慷慨而長嘯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he extended to student-friends, gathered kindred spirits; refined the utmost pivot of nature and life, studied the dark profundity of the Way and virtue; pitied the vulgar stream not yet awakened, alone transcendent and first aware; the narrow world's path cramped and remote—lifting eyes to heaven's highway and treading high; far crossing the vulgar and leaving the body behind—then expansively and long he whistled.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned friends and gathered like-minded souls, probed the deepest springs of life and nature, plumbed the hidden depths of the Way; pitying a world still unawakened, he alone rose first to understanding; finding the world's road cramped and mean, he lifted his gaze to heaven's broad way and strode aloft; leaving the vulgar far behind and his bodily self behind with it—he gave a long, impassioned whistle.

sentences.zh: 于時曜靈俄景，流光濛汜，逍遙攜手，躊躇步趾，發妙聲於丹脣，激哀音於皓齒，響抑揚而潛轉，氣沖鬱而熛起，協黃宮於清角，雜商羽於流征，飄浮雲於泰清，集長風於萬里。

translations.literal: At that time the shining spirit suddenly set its light, flowing radiance misted at the ford; free and easy, hand in hand, hesitant in step and toe; issuing wondrous sound from cinnabar lips, stirring mournful tones from white teeth; sound suppressed and raised, secretly turning; qi surged dense and flamed up; harmonizing yellow bell with clear jue, mixing shang and yu with flowing zhi; floating clouds drift in Supreme Clarity, gathering the long wind from ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the sun sank low, light pooled in misty twilight; roaming hand in hand, pacing with lingering steps, he drew wonder from crimson lips, grief from gleaming teeth; tones rose and fell in hidden turns, breath surged dense as flame; yellow bell met clear jue, shang and yu blended with flowing zhi; clouds drifted through highest heaven, the long wind gathered from a thousand miles.

sentences.zh: 曲既終而響絕，餘遺玩而未已，良自然之至音，非絲竹之所擬。

translations.literal: The tune already ended yet the sound ceased, the remnant lingered for savoring and did not stop—truly nature's utmost tone, not what silk and bamboo can match.
translations.idiomatic: Though the tune had ended and sound fell silent, the lingering echo invited endless savor—truly nature's own supreme music, beyond anything silk strings or bamboo pipes could rival.

sentences.zh: 是故聲不假器，用不借物，近取諸身，役心御氣。

translations.literal: Therefore sound borrows no instrument, use borrows no object; taking near from the body itself, employing mind to command qi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus sound needs no instrument, art borrows no thing; it draws from the body itself, mind commanding breath.

sentences.zh: 動脣有曲，發口成音，觸類感物，因歌隨吟。

translations.literal: Moving lips there is melody, opening mouth there is tone; touching categories and moved by things, following song and along with chant.
translations.idiomatic: Lips move and melody forms, mouth opens and tone is born; stirred by things of every kind, it follows song and flows with chant.

sentences.zh: 大而不洿，細而不沈，清激切於竽笙，優潤和瑟琴，玄妙足以通神悟靈，精微足以窮幽測深，收激楚之哀荒，節北里之奢淫，濟洪災於炎旱，反亢陽于重陰。

translations.literal: Great yet not muddy, fine yet not sunk; clear and piercing, cutting past yu and sheng; graceful and moist, harmonizing with se and qin; dark mystery sufficient to penetrate spirit and awaken soul, subtle refinement sufficient to exhaust the hidden and fathom the deep; restraining the mournful desolation of Exciting Chu, moderating the extravagant licentiousness of North Lane; relieving great calamity in scorching drought, returning excessive yang within heavy yin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand yet never turbid, delicate yet never drowned; clear and piercing beyond reed and pipe, graceful and mellow as zither and lute; subtle enough to pierce the spirit and awaken the soul, fine enough to probe the hidden depths; it curbed the wild grief of Exciting Chu, tempered the lavish excess of North Lane; eased great disaster in burning drought, turned scorching yang back within heavy yin.

sentences.zh: 引唱萬變，曲用無方，和樂怡懌，悲傷摧藏。

translations.literal: Leading chant in ten thousand changes, tune's use has no fixed method; harmonious music brings joy and ease, grief and sorrow crush and hide.
translations.idiomatic: Its leading tones shifted in endless ways, its melodies obeyed no fixed rule; harmony brought joy and ease, sorrow crushed the heart and hid it away.

sentences.zh: 時幽散而將絕，中矯曆而慷慨，徐婉約而優遊，紛繁騖而激揚。

translations.literal: At times dark and scattered, about to end; at the center stern and forceful, expansive and impassioned; slowly gentle and restrained yet leisurely roaming; tangled and rushing, swift and rousing.
translations.idiomatic: Now dim and scattered, nearly dying away; now stern at the center, bold and impassioned; now gently restrained and leisurely roaming; now tangled, rushing, swift and rousing.

sentences.zh: 情既思而能反，心雖哀而不傷。

translations.literal: Feeling already thought yet able to return; heart though mournful yet not wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling pondered yet could turn back; the heart mourned yet was not broken.

sentences.zh: 總八音之至和，固極樂而無荒。

translations.literal: Gathering the eight sounds' utmost harmony, solidly utmost joy without dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering the eight tones in perfect harmony, it held supreme joy without excess.

sentences.zh: 若乃登高臺以臨遠，披文軒而騁望，喟仰抃而抗首，嘈長引而憀亮。

translations.literal: As for ascending a high terrace to overlook the distance, parting patterned rails and galloping the gaze; sighing, lifting face and tossing head, noisy long-drawn notes clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: When he climbed a high terrace to gaze afar, opened patterned rails and let his sight run free, sighing he lifted his face and threw back his head, drawing long, bright, resonant notes.

sentences.zh: 或舒肆而自反，或徘徊而復放，或冉弱而柔撓，或澎濞而奔壯。

translations.literal: Sometimes expansive and self-returning, sometimes lingering and again releasing; sometimes gradually weakening and softly yielding, sometimes surging and billowing, rushing and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Now broad and free, then folding back on itself; now lingering, then releasing again; now soft and yielding, now surging, billowing, bold and rushing.

sentences.zh: 橫鬱嗚而滔涸，洌繚眺而清昶。

translations.literal: Crosswise dense and moaning, overflowing and drying; clear and winding, gazing far, bright and open.
translations.idiomatic: It moaned dense and crosswise, flooded and ebbed; ran clear and winding, bright and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 逸氣奮湧，繽紛交錯，烈烈飆揚，啾啾響作。

translations.literal: Free qi surged and welled, riotous colors crossed and tangled; fiercely the gale rose, chirping sounds arose.
translations.idiomatic: Free breath surged and welled, colors of sound crossed and tangled; gales rose fierce and bright, chirping echoes answered.

sentences.zh: 奏胡馬之長思，回寒風乎北朔，又似鴻雁之將雛，群鳴號乎沙漠。

translations.literal: Playing the long longing of frontier horses, turning the cold wind at northern frontier; again like wild geese about to rear their young, flocks crying and calling in the desert.
translations.idiomatic: It played the long yearning of frontier horses, turned the cold wind of the northern frontier; then seemed wild geese brooding over their young, flocks crying across the desert.

sentences.zh: 故能因形創聲，隨事造曲，應物無窮，機發響速，怫鬱沖流，參譚雲屬，若離若合，將絕復續。

translations.literal: Therefore able to follow form and create sound, follow affairs and fashion tunes; responding to things without end, trigger released and sound swift; sullen and surging in rushing flow, mixed and layered like clouds joined; as if parting as if joining, about to end yet again continuing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it shaped sound from form, fashioned melody from circumstance, answered things without limit, sprang forth swift as thought; surging, dense, and flowing, layered like joining clouds—now parting, now meeting, nearly ending, then continuing again.

sentences.zh: 飛廉鼓於幽隧，猛獸應于中谷；

translations.literal: Fei Lian drums in the dark tunnel, fierce beasts respond in the middle valley;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Lian drummed in dark ravines, fierce beasts answered in the hollow vale;

sentences.zh: 南箕動於穹蒼，清飆振于喬木；

translations.literal: the Southern Sieve moves in the vaulted azure, clear gales vibrate on tall trees;
translations.idiomatic: the Southern Sieve stirred in the vaulted sky, clear winds shook the tall trees;

sentences.zh: 散滯積而播揚，蕩埃靄之溷濁，變陰陽於至和，移淫風之穢俗。

translations.literal: scattering stagnation and accumulation and broadcasting them abroad, washing the dust and haze of turbid murk; transforming yin and yang into utmost harmony, shifting the foul customs of decadent winds.
translations.idiomatic: scattering what had stagnated and spreading it abroad, cleansing murky dust and haze; turning yin and yang toward perfect harmony, shifting the foul customs of decadent times.

sentences.zh: 若乃遊崇岡，陵景山，臨岩側，望流川，坐磐石，漱清泉，藉皋蘭之猗靡，廕修竹之蟬蜎，乃吟詠而發歎，聲驛驛而響連，舒蓄思之悱憤，奮久結之纏綿，心滌蕩而無累，志離俗而飄然。

translations.literal: As for roaming lofty ridges, ascending scenic mountains, facing cliff-sides, gazing at flowing streams; sitting on bedrock boulders, rinsing with clear springs; resting on orchids' luxuriant spread, shaded by tall bamboo's cicada-curl; then chanting and singing and issuing sighs, sound continuous and echoes linked; releasing stored thought's pent frustration, rousing long-knotted entanglement; heart washed clear without burden, ambition leaving the vulgar and drifting free.
translations.idiomatic: When he roamed high ridges, climbed scenic peaks, stood by cliff-sides and gazed on flowing streams; sat on bedrock, rinsed with clear springs; rested on spreading orchids, shaded by tall bamboo's graceful bend—then chanting he sighed aloud, sound running on in linked echoes; he released pent thoughts long stored, roused feelings knotted through the years; his heart washed clear and unburdened, his spirit left the vulgar world and drifted free.

sentences.zh: 若夫假像金革，擬則陶匏，眾聲繁奏，若笳若簫；

translations.literal: As for borrowing the image of metal and hide, modeling on pottery and gourd; the many sounds densely performed, like qiang like xiao;
translations.idiomatic: It could mimic metal drums and hide, take pottery and gourd for model; many voices sounded together, like qiang or xiao;

sentences.zh: 磞硠震隱，訇礚𥕡嘈。

translations.literal: booming and rumbling, shaking and hidden; thunderous crashing, roaring and noisy.
translations.idiomatic: booming, rumbling, shaking and rolling; thunderous, crashing, roaring and loud.

sentences.zh: 發徵則隆冬熙烝，騁羽則嚴霜夏凋，動商則秋霖春降，奏角則谷風鳴條。

translations.literal: Issuing zhi then deep winter grows warm and steamy; unleashing yu then harsh frost in summer withers; moving shang then autumn rains fall in spring; playing jue then valley winds sing through branches.
translations.idiomatic: Strike the zhi note and deep winter turns warm; release yu and harsh frost withers summer; move shang and autumn rains fall in spring; play jue and valley winds sing through the branches.

sentences.zh: 音均不恆，曲無定制，行而不流，止而不滯，隨口吻而發揚，假芳氣而遠逝，音要妙而流響，聲激嚁而清厲。

translations.literal: Pitch and balance not constant, tune without fixed pattern; moving yet not flowing, stopping yet not stagnant; following mouth and lips and issuing abroad, borrowing fragrant qi and departing far; tone subtle-wondrous and flowing in echo, sound piercing-clear and pure and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch held no constant measure, melody no fixed form; it moved without spilling, stopped without stagnating; rose with the lips' breath, rode fragrant air into the distance; tones subtle and wondrous, echoes flowing on; sound piercing, clear, and keen.

sentences.zh: 信自然之極麗，羌殊尤而絕世，越《韶》《夏》與《咸池》，何徒取異乎《鄭》《衛》！

translations.literal: Truly nature's utmost beauty—how singular and surpassing, unmatched in the age; transcending "Shao," "Xia," and "Xianchi"—why merely take difference from "Zheng" and "Wei"!
translations.idiomatic: Truly nature's supreme beauty, singular and unmatched in the age; it surpassed Shao, Xia, and Xianchi—how could it be compared merely with the music of Zheng and Wei!

sentences.zh: 于時綿駒結舌而喪精，王豹杜口而失色，虞公輟聲而止歌，寧子斂手而歎息，鐘期棄琴而改聽，尼父忘味而不食，百獸率儛而拤足，鳳皇來儀而拊翼。

translations.literal: At that time Mian Ju bit his tongue and lost his spirit, Wang Bao shut his mouth and lost his color; the Duke of Yu stopped his voice and ceased his song, Ningzi folded his hands and sighed; Zhong Qi cast aside his qin and changed what he listened to, Master Ni forgot flavor and did not eat; the hundred beasts led in dance and stamped their feet, the phoenix came in ritual and beat its wings.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mian Ju bit his tongue and lost his wits, Wang Bao fell silent and pale; the Duke of Yu stopped singing, Ningzi sighed and folded his hands; Zhong Qi laid down his zither and turned to listen anew, Confucius forgot his meal; the hundred beasts danced and stamped their feet, the phoenix came in ritual and beat its wings.

sentences.zh: 乃知長嘯之奇妙，此音聲之至極。

translations.literal: Then one knows the wondrous subtlety of long whistling—this is the utmost extreme of sound and voice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows the marvel of long whistling—this is the supreme limit of music and sound.

sentences.zh: 張華雅重綏，每見其文，歎伏以為絕倫，薦之太常，徵為博士。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua deeply esteemed Sui; whenever he saw his writings he sighed and submitted, deeming them without peer—he recommended him to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, who summoned him as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua admired him deeply; each essay left Zhang convinced no one could rival Cheng, so he nominated him to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, who appointed him court erudite.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書郎，轉丞，遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Palace Secretary, transferred to assistant director, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Writers.
translations.idiomatic: He served as palace secretary, moved up to assistant director, then advanced to gentleman of the palace writers.

sentences.zh: 每與華受詔並為詩賦，又與賈充等參定法律。

translations.literal: Whenever he received edicts together with Hua they jointly composed shi and fu; he also joined Jia Chong and others in revising the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He often drafted verse and rhapsodies alongside Zhang Hua by imperial order and helped Jia Chong and colleagues codify the law.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年卒，年四十三，所著詩賦雜筆十餘卷行於世。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi he died, at age forty-three; what he wrote—poetry, fu, and miscellaneous brush-notes in more than ten fascicles—circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taishi, he died at forty-three; over ten fascicles of poetry, rhapsodies, and assorted prose circulated after him.

sentences.zh: 左思，字太沖，齊國臨淄人也。

translations.literal: Zuo Si, style Taichong, was a man of Linzi in the kingdom of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si, courtesy name Taichong, hailed from Linzi in the old kingdom of Qi.

sentences.zh: 其先齊之公族有左右公子，因為氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors were among the ducal kin of Qi; there were Left and Right Young Lords, and from this they took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: The clan descended from Qi nobility—the ancient titles "Left and Right Young Lord" supplied their surname.

sentences.zh: 家世儒學。

translations.literal: For generations the household practiced ru learning.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had pursued Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 父雍，起小吏，以能擢授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Yong rose from petty clerk and by ability was promoted and appointed Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo Yong began as a petty clerk and won promotion on merit to palace assistant censor.

sentences.zh: 思小學鐘、胡書及鼓琴，並不成。

translations.literal: Si in youth studied Zhong and Hu calligraphy and playing the zither—none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zuo studied calligraphy after Zhong Yao and Hu Zhao and took up the zither—he mastered neither.

sentences.zh: 雍謂友人曰：「思所曉解，不及我少時。」

translations.literal: Yong said to a friend, "What Si understands does not match me in my youth."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yong told a friend, "The boy grasps less than I did at his age."

sentences.zh: 思遂感激勤學，兼善陰陽之術。

translations.literal: Si thereupon was stirred and studied diligently; he also became adept in yin-yang arts.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by those words, Zuo threw himself into study and learned the yin-yang traditions besides.

sentences.zh: 貌寢，口訥，而辭藻壯麗。

translations.literal: His appearance was homely, his speech halting, yet his phrasing was magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Plain of face and slow of tongue, he nevertheless wrote with towering brilliance.

sentences.zh: 不好交遊，惟以閒居為事。

translations.literal: He did not enjoy socializing; he took only quiet retirement as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He avoided society and preferred the quiet of home.

sentences.zh: 造《齊都賦》，一年乃成。

translations.literal: He composed the "Fu on the Qi Capital"; one year then it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a "Rhapsody on the Qi Capital" that took a year to complete.

sentences.zh: 復欲賦三都，會妹芬入宮，移家京師，乃詣著作郎張載，訪岷邛之事。

translations.literal: He again wished to compose a fu on the three capitals; it happened that his younger sister Fen entered the palace, and he moved the household to the capital—thereupon he visited Editorial Director Zhang Zai and inquired into affairs of Min and Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: He next planned his "Three Capitals" rhapsody; when his sister Zuo Fen entered the harem the family relocated to Luoyang, and Zuo called on Editorial Director Zhang Zai to gather material on Shu Min and Qiong.

sentences.zh: 遂構思十年，門庭籓溷，皆著筆紙，遇得一句，即便疏之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he conceived it for ten years; gate, courtyard, fence, and privy all had brush and paper—whenever he obtained a line he at once wrote it down.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded on the work a full decade; brush and paper littered gate, yard, fence, and latrine—every stray couplet was recorded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自以所見不博，求為秘書郎。

translations.literal: He himself thought what he had seen was not broad; he sought appointment as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling his reading still too narrow, he secured a post as palace secretary for access to the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 及賦成，時人未之重。

translations.literal: When the fu was finished, people of the time did not yet esteem it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rhapsody was done, contemporaries still shrugged it off.

sentences.zh: 思自以其作不謝班張，恐以人廢言，安定皇甫謐有高譽，思造而示之。

translations.literal: Si himself thought his work did not yield to Ban and Zhang; he feared people would discard the words because of the man—Huangfu Mi of Anding had a lofty reputation, and Si visited and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo believed his work matched Ban Gu and Zhang Heng yet feared dismissal on account of his homely looks, so he brought the manuscript to the renowned Huangfu Mi of Anding.

sentences.zh: 謐稱善，為其賦序。

translations.literal: Mi praised it as good and composed a preface to his fu.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu praised it and supplied a preface.

sentences.zh: 張載為注《魏都》，劉逵注《吳》《蜀》而序之曰：「觀中古以來為賦者多矣，相如《子虛》擅名于前，班固《兩都》理勝其辭，張衡《二京》文過其意。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai annotated the "Wei Capital"; Liu Kui annotated the "Wu" and "Shu" sections and prefaced them, saying, "Since middle antiquity many have composed fu: Xiangru's 'Sir Vacuous' monopolized fame early; Ban Gu's 'Two Capitals' had principle surpassing its phrasing; Zhang Heng's 'Two Capitals' had pattern exceeding its ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai glossed the Wei section; Liu Kui annotated Wu and Shu and wrote a preface: "Fu writers crowd the middle ages—Sima Xiangru's 'Sir Vacuous' claimed first glory; Ban Gu's twin capitals privilege argument over diction; Zhang Heng's pair favors ornament over thought.

sentences.zh: 至若此賦，擬議數家，傅辭會義，抑多精緻，非夫研核者不能練其旨，非夫博物者不能統其異。

translations.literal: As for this fu, it models several masters, spreads phrasing and joins meanings—indeed much is refined; unless one examines closely one cannot master its aim; unless one broadly knows things one cannot unite its differences.
translations.idiomatic: This piece, however, distills many models and weaves diction with doctrine at rare finesse—only a painstaking reader grasps its argument, only a scholar of wide learning commands its diversity.

sentences.zh: 世咸貴遠而賤近，莫肯用心於明物。

translations.literal: The age all esteems the distant and despises the near; none is willing to apply mind to clarifying things.
translations.idiomatic: People honor the remote past and scorn the present, unwilling to labor over factual truth.

sentences.zh: 斯文吾有異焉，故聊以餘思為其引詁，亦猶胡廣之於《官箴》，蔡邕之於《典引》也。」

translations.literal: On this text I have a different view; therefore briefly with remaining thought I supply its introduction and gloss—it is also like Hu Guang with regard to the 'Official Admonition,' Cai Yong with regard to the 'Canon Introduction.'"
translations.idiomatic: I take a different view of this text, so I lend what wit remains to introduce and gloss it—much as Hu Guang annotated the "Official Admonitions" or Cai Yong the "Canon Preface."

sentences.zh: 陳留衛權又為思賦作《略解》，序曰：「余觀《三都》之賦，言不苟華，必經典要，品物殊類，稟之圖籍；

translations.literal: Wei Quan of Chenliu further composed for Si's fu a "Brief Explication," prefacing it: "I have viewed the fu 'Three Capitals': its words do not recklessly flower—they must pass through canonical essentials; the categories of things are diverse classes, received from charts and records;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Quan of Chenliu also wrote a "Brief Explication" for Zuo's work, opening: "Reading the 'Three Capitals,' one finds no idle flourish—every line rests on canonical authority; each thing catalogued comes straight from the atlases and histories.

sentences.zh: 辭義瑰瑋，良可貴也。

translations.literal: its phrasing and meaning are rare and grand—truly to be prized.
translations.idiomatic: The language is splendid and the sense monumental—work of real worth.

sentences.zh: 有晉征士故太子中庶子安定皇甫謐，西州之逸士，耽籍樂道，高尚其事，覽斯文而慷慨，為之都序。

translations.literal: There is Jin reclusive scholar, former Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Huangfu Mi of Anding, a retired gentleman of the western provinces who delighted in texts and rejoiced in the Way, holding his pursuits lofty—reading this refined writing he grew impassioned and composed for it a general preface.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Huangfu Mi of Anding—once junior mentor to the crown prince—western gentleman lost in books and the Way, lofty in purpose, read these lines with beating heart and supplied the overarching preface.

sentences.zh: 中書著作郎安平張載、中書郎濟南劉逵，並以經學洽博，才章美茂，咸皆悅玩，為之訓詁；

translations.literal: Gentleman Compiler Zhang Zai of Anping and Gentleman of the Palace Writers Liu Kui of Jinan—both by classical learning were broadly versed, their talent and pattern rich and lush—all alike delighted in it and played with it, producing glosses for it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai of Anping and Liu Kui of Jinan—court compilers steeped in the classics, gifted stylists—each delighted in the text and drafted scholarly commentary;

sentences.zh: 其山川土域，草木鳥獸，奇怪珍異，僉皆研精所由，紛散其義矣。

translations.literal: as to its mountains and rivers, soil and regions, plants and trees, birds and beasts, strange and precious marvels—all alike investigated with refinement whence they came, scattering and unfolding their meanings.
translations.idiomatic: every landscape, soil, plant, beast, and curiosity they traced to source, unpacking sense after sense.

sentences.zh: 余嘉其文，不能默已，聊藉二子之遺忘，又為之《略解》，祗增煩重，覽者闕焉。」

translations.literal: I admire its pattern and cannot be silent; briefly borrowing where those two sons left gaps, I again composed for it a "Brief Explication"—only adding annoyance and burden; let readers omit it."
translations.idiomatic: I admire the piece too deeply to stay mute; picking up where Zhang and Liu left off I added this "Brief Explication"—knowing it only piles dutiful clutter on readers who may skip it."

sentences.zh: 自是之後，盛重于時，文多不載。

translations.literal: From this time onward it was greatly esteemed in its age—much of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: After that the work commanded enormous esteem (most of the prose is omitted here).

sentences.zh: 司空張華見而歎曰：「班張之流也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua saw it and sighed, saying, "Of the class of Ban and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Hua exclaimed, "This belongs with Ban Gu and Zhang Heng.

sentences.zh: 使讀之者盡而有餘，久而更新。」

translations.literal: It causes those who read it to exhaust yet still have surplus; long enduring yet anew."
translations.idiomatic: Readers finish yet feel there is more; revisit after years and it still feels fresh."

sentences.zh: 於是豪貴之家競相傳寫，洛陽為之紙貴。

translations.literal: Thereupon houses of the mighty and noble vied to copy and circulate it; Luoyang for this reason had costly paper.
translations.idiomatic: Noble households scrambled to copy it until Luoyang ran short of paper—a story still told today.

sentences.zh: 初，陸機入洛，欲為此賦，聞思作之，撫掌而笑，與弟雲書曰：「此間有傖父，欲作《三都賦》，須其成，當以覆酒甕耳。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Ji entered Luoyang he wished to compose this fu; hearing Si was composing it, he clapped his hands and laughed, writing to his younger brother Yun: "Here there is a boorish fellow who wishes to compose the 'Fu on the Three Capitals'; wait until it is finished—we shall use it to cover wine jars."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji first reached Luoyang he meant to write his own "Three Capitals"; learning Zuo was at work he laughed aloud and wrote Lu Yun: "Some rustic here thinks he can compose that rhapsody—when he's done we'll line the wine jars with it."

sentences.zh: 及思賦出，機絕歎伏，以為不能加也，遂輟筆焉。

translations.literal: When Si's fu appeared, Ji utterly sighed and submitted, thinking he could not surpass it—thereupon he stopped his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zuo's piece appeared, Lu Ji conceded outright that he could not better it and abandoned his own draft.

sentences.zh: 秘書監賈謐請講《漢書》，謐誅，退居宜春裏，專意典籍。

translations.literal: Palace Library Supervisor Jia Mi invited him to lecture on the Han History; when Mi was executed, [Si] retired to live in Yichun Ward and devoted intent attention to classical writings.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi, director of the palace library, asked him to lecture on the Han History; after Jia's execution Zuo withdrew to Yichun Ward and buried himself in books.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏命為記室督，辭疾，不就。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, ordered him to be Recorder-in-Chief; he declined citing illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, offered him chief recorder; Zuo pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 及張方縱暴都邑，舉家適冀州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fang wantonly ravaged the capital region, he moved the whole household to Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fang terrorized the capital the entire family fled north into Ji province.

sentences.zh: 數歲，以疾終。

translations.literal: After several years he ended by illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness a few years later.

sentences.zh: 趙至

translations.literal: Zhao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi

sentences.zh: 趙至，字景真，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhi, style Jingzhen, was a man of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi, courtesy name Jingzhen, was a native of Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 寓居洛陽。

translations.literal: He dwelled sojourning in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 緱氏令初到官，至年十三，與母同觀。

translations.literal: When the magistrate of Goushi first arrived at his post, Zhi was thirteen years old and together with his mother watched.
translations.idiomatic: When the new magistrate of Goushi took office, thirteen-year-old Zhao went with his mother to watch the procession.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「汝先世本非微賤，世亂流離，遂為士伍耳。

translations.literal: His mother said, "Your ancestors were originally not lowly; age disorder scattering separation—thereupon they became common soldiers, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Our forebears were never humble folk; war uprooted the clan until they sank into the ranks—that is all.

sentences.zh: 爾後能如此不？」

translations.literal: Can you afterward be like this or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you rise above this life or not?"

sentences.zh: 至感母言，詣師受業。

translations.literal: Zhi was moved by his mother's words and went to a teacher to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Moved deeply, Zhao sought out a tutor.

sentences.zh: 聞父耕叱牛聲，投書而泣。

translations.literal: Hearing his father's plowing shout at the ox, he cast aside his book and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard his father shouting at the ox in the field he dropped his primer and wept.

sentences.zh: 師怪問之，至曰：「我小未能榮養，使老父不免勤苦。」

translations.literal: The teacher wondered and asked him; Zhi said, "I am young and unable yet to honor and support [them], causing my aged father not to avoid toil and bitterness."
translations.idiomatic: His teacher asked why; Zhao answered, "I am too young to earn honor or keep my parents fed—the old man still toils because of me."

sentences.zh: 師甚異之。

translations.literal: The teacher greatly considered him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 年十四，詣洛陽，遊太學，遇嵇康于學寫石經，徘徊視之，不能去，而請問姓名。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he went to Luoyang and roamed the Imperial Academy; he encountered Ji Kang at the academy copying the stone classics—hovering he gazed, unable to leave, and requested to ask his name.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the capital and the Imperial Academy, where he found Ji Kang transcribing the stone classics; Zhao circled, unable to tear himself away, and begged the stranger's name.

sentences.zh: 康曰：「年少何以問邪？」

translations.literal: Kang said, "Youth—why do you ask?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang said, "What is a boy like you doing asking?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「觀君風器非常，所以問耳。」

translations.literal: [Zhi] said, "Observing your air and bearing is not ordinary—therefore I ask, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: "Your bearing is like no other—that is why I asked."

sentences.zh: 康異而告之。

translations.literal: Kang considered it strange and told him [his name].
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang, intrigued, told him who he was.

sentences.zh: 後乃亡到山陽，求康不得而還。

translations.literal: Afterward he fled to Shanyang, sought Kang but did not find him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He later ran away to Shanyang hoping to find Ji Kang but failed and trudged home.

sentences.zh: 又將遠學，母禁之，至遂陽狂，走三五里，輒追得之。

translations.literal: Again he was about to study far away; his mother forbade him—Zhi thereupon feigned madness, ran five or three li, and each time was pursued and caught.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to leave for distant study his mother forbade it, so he feigned madness and bolted a few miles—each time she ran him down.

sentences.zh: 年十六，遊鄴，復與康相遇，隨康還山陽，改名浚，字允元。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he roamed Ye; again he encountered Kang and followed Kang back to Shanyang—he changed his name to Jun, style Yuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he wandered to Ye, met Ji Kang again, followed him home to Shanyang, and adopted the name Zhao Jun, courtesy name Yuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 康每曰：「卿頭小而銳，童子白黑分明，有白起之風矣。」

translations.literal: Kang often said, "Your head is small and keen; as a boy black and white were distinct in your eyes—you have the air of Bai Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang used to tell him, "That sharp little head of yours, those bright eyes even as a boy—you have something of Bai Qi about you."

sentences.zh: 及康卒，至詣魏興見太守張嗣宗，甚被優遇。

translations.literal: When Kang died, Zhi went to Wei Xing and visited Administrator Zhang Sizong and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji Kang's execution Zhao traveled to Wei Xing and called on Prefect Zhang Sizong, who treated him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗遷江夏相，隨到溳川，欲因入吳，而嗣宗卒，乃向遼西而占戶焉。

translations.literal: Sizong was transferred to be minister of Jiangxia; [Zhi] followed him to Yun River, intending thereby to enter Wu, but Sizong died—thereupon he headed toward Liaoxi and registered his household there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang rose to governor of Jiangxia, Zhao followed him to the Yun basin hoping to cross into Wu; Zhang died before they could go, so Zhao drifted to Liaoxi and settled his household register there.

sentences.zh: 初，至與康兄子蕃友善，及將遠適，乃與蕃書敘離，並陳其志曰：

translations.literal: Earlier Zhi had been friendly with Kang's elder brother's son Fan; when he was about to go far away he wrote Fan a letter narrating parting and stating his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He had long befriended Ji Kang's nephew Ji Fan; before leaving for good he sent Fan a farewell letter laying bare his purpose:

sentences.zh: 梁生適越，登嶽長謠。

translations.literal: Liang Sheng went to Yue, climbed the mountain and sang long.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong set out for Yue and poured out a long song from the heights.

sentences.zh: 夫以嘉遁之舉，猶懷戀恨，況乎不得已者哉！

translations.literal: Now as for the act of fine withdrawal, they still cherished fond regret—how much more when one has no choice!
translations.idiomatic: Even those who withdraw in noble ease still feel the ache of parting—how much more one who goes against his will!

sentences.zh: 惟別之後，離群獨逝，背榮宴，辭倫好，經迥路，造沙漠。

translations.literal: Since parting, leaving the flock I go alone, turning my back on honored feasting, bidding farewell to worthy fellowship, traversing winding roads, reaching the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Since we parted I have traveled alone, leaving feasts and friends behind, crossing twisting roads until I stand at the desert's edge.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴戒旦，則飄爾晨征；

translations.literal: At cockcrow warning dawn, then lightly I set out at morning;
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow I rise and fare forth at dawn;

sentences.zh: 日薄西山，則馬首靡托。

translations.literal: The sun draws near western mountains, then my horse's head has nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: when the sun sinks west, my horse has nowhere to halt.

sentences.zh: 尋曆曲阻，則沈思紆結；

translations.literal: Soon traversing winding barriers, then deep thought knots and coils;
translations.idiomatic: On winding passes my thoughts knot tight;

sentences.zh: 登高遠眺，則山川攸隔。

translations.literal: Climbing high and gazing far, then mountains and rivers are sundered.
translations.idiomatic: from lofty vistas mountains and rivers stretch infinitely between us.

sentences.zh: 或乃回風狂厲，白日寢光，徙倚交錯，陵隰相望，徘徊九皋之內，慷慨重阜之顛，進無所由，退無所據，涉澤求蹊，披榛覓路，嘯詠溝渠，良不可度。

translations.literal: Sometimes whirling wind is fierce and violent, the white sun hides its light; I linger and lean crisscrossing, hills and marshes facing one another; I pace within the nine marshes, pour forth feeling on heavy knolls' crests; advancing there is no path, retreating there is no foothold; crossing swamps seeking tracks, parting brambles seeking roads—whistling and chanting in ditches and channels—truly cannot be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes wild winds howl and daylight dies; I wander lost among hills and bogs, pacing the reedy flats and brooding on high ridges—no way forward, no place to turn back. I wade marshes for a trail, hack through brambles for a road, and whistle verses in muddy channels where none may pass.

sentences.zh: 斯亦行路之艱難，然非吾心之所懼也。

translations.literal: This too is the hardship of travel on the road—yet it is not what my heart fears.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the trials of the road—but they are not what I dread.

sentences.zh: 至若蘭芷傾頓，桂林移殖，根萌未樹而牙淺弦急，每恐風波潛駭，危機密發，此所以怵惕於長衢也。

translations.literal: As for orchids and angelica overturned, cassia trees transplanted—roots and sprouts not yet set while the bow is shallow-drawn and the string tight—each time I fear hidden shock of wind and waves, peril's moment secretly arising; this is why I am fearful and wary on the long highway.
translations.idiomatic: What I dread is orchid and cassia uprooted and replanted—roots not yet firm while the bow is taut—lest hidden storms strike and danger burst forth without warning. That is why I tremble on this long road.

sentences.zh: 又北土之性，難以托根，投人夜光，鮮不按劍。

translations.literal: Moreover the nature of northern soil is hard to take root in; casting a luminous gem before others, few do not lay hand to sword.
translations.idiomatic: The northern lands are hard soil for transplanting; show a luminous pearl to strangers and few will not reach for their swords.

sentences.zh: 今將殖橘柚于玄朔，蒂華藕于修陵，表龍章於裸壤，奏《韶》《武》於聾俗，固難以取貴矣。

translations.literal: Now I am about to plant orange and pomelo in dark northlands, set lotus stems and flowers on Xiu Mound, display dragon emblems on bare soil, perform "Shao" and "Wu" for deaf custom—truly hard to win esteem.
translations.idiomatic: I go to plant oranges in the far north, set lotus on barren hills, display dragon insignia on naked earth, and play the "Shao" and "Wu" hymns to deaf ears—how can such gifts win honor?

sentences.zh: 夫物不我貴則莫之與，莫之與則傷之者至矣。

translations.literal: Now if things do not prize me then none will join with me; if none join with me then those who wound will arrive in full.
translations.idiomatic: When the world does not value you, none will stand with you; and when none stand with you, injury is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 飄颻遠遊之士，托身無人之鄉，總轡遐路，則有前言之難；

translations.literal: A drifting far-wandering gentleman, lodging his person in a land without men, gathering reins on distant roads—then there is the hardship of words already spoken;
translations.idiomatic: A wanderer adrift in empty country, reins in hand on endless roads, faces the hardship foretold by sages;

sentences.zh: 懸鞍陋宇，則有後慮之戒；

translations.literal: hanging saddle in a mean dwelling—then there is the warning of later concern;
translations.idiomatic: and stabling his horse in a wretched inn, the warning of troubles yet to come.

sentences.zh: 朝霞啟暉，則身疲而遄征；

translations.literal: morning rosy clouds open radiance—then the body is weary yet hastens on campaign;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn's first light his weary body presses on;

sentences.zh: 太陽戢曜，則情劬而夕惕；

translations.literal: the great sun sheathes its brilliance—then feeling is toiled and evening-cautious;
translations.idiomatic: at sunset his heart labors and he keeps vigil through the night.

sentences.zh: 肆目平隰，則寥廓而無睹；

translations.literal: releasing the eye over level lowlands—then vast emptiness and nothing seen;
translations.idiomatic: He scans the flat plains and sees only emptiness;

sentences.zh: 極聽修原，則掩寂而無聞。

translations.literal: listening to the limit on long plains—then muffled silence and nothing heard.
translations.idiomatic: he listens across the open steppe and hears only silence.

sentences.zh: 籲其悲矣！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 心傷瘁矣！

translations.literal: The heart is wounded and worn!
translations.idiomatic: The heart is wounded to exhaustion!

sentences.zh: 然後知步驟之士不足為貴也。

translations.literal: Only then does one know that gentlemen of measured pace are not worth esteeming.
translations.idiomatic: Only then does one see that men content with small steps are no fit measure of worth.

sentences.zh: 顧景中原，憤中雲踴，哀物悼世，激情風厲。

translations.literal: Turning sight to the central plains, rage within surges like clouds; grieving things and mourning the age, fierce feeling blazes like wind.
translations.idiomatic: I look back toward the heartland and rage boils within; grieving for the world, my passion rises fierce as a gale.

sentences.zh: 龍嘯大野，獸睇六合，猛志紛紜，雄心四據。

translations.literal: A dragon roars across the great wilds, beasts gaze upon the six quarters; fierce intent tangles in profusion, bold heart seizes the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: My spirit roars like a dragon across the wilds and surveys the realm; fierce purpose swarms and bold ambition grips all four quarters.

sentences.zh: 思躡雲梯，橫奮八極，披艱掃穢，蕩海夷嶽，蹴昆侖使西倒，蹋太山令東覆，平滌九區，恢維宇宙，斯吾之鄙願也。

translations.literal: I think to tread the cloud ladder, stride across and strive through the eight extremities, part hardship and sweep defilement, level seas and flatten mountains, kick Kunlun to make it fall westward, tread Mount Tai to make it overturn eastward, level and cleanse the nine regions, restore and sustain the cosmos—this is my humble wish.
translations.idiomatic: I dream of climbing heaven's ladder and ranging the eight extremes—cutting through hardship, cleansing corruption, flattening seas and mountains, kicking Kunlun westward and toppling Tai eastward, purging the nine provinces and ordering the universe. That is my humble ambition.

sentences.zh: 時不我與，垂翼遠逝，鋒距靡加，六翮摧屈，自非知命，孰能不憤悒者哉！

translations.literal: The age does not grant me its time; wings droop as I go far away; talons and spurs cannot be applied, six pinions are broken and bent—if not one who knows fate, who could fail to be angry and depressed!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hour is not mine: wings folded, I fly into exile; talons blunted, pinions broken—who but one resigned to fate could bear such bitterness!

sentences.zh: 吾子殖根芳苑，濯秀清流，晞葉華崖，飛藻雲肆，俯據潛龍之渚，仰廕游鳳之林，榮曜眩其前，豔色餌其後，良疇交其左，聲名馳其右，翱翔倫黨之間，弄姿帷房之裹，從容顧眄，綽有餘裕，俯仰吟嘯，自以為得志矣，豈能與吾曹同大丈夫之憂樂哉！

translations.literal: My lord plants roots in fragrant gardens, washes splendor in clear streams, dries leaves on flowery cliffs, lets ornament fly in cloud's expanse; below he occupies the ford of hidden dragons, above he is shaded by the grove of roaming phoenixes—glory dazzles before him, gorgeous color lures behind him, fine companions meet at his left, fame races at his right; soaring among kindred fellows, displaying grace within curtain chambers, at ease in glance and look, ample in surplus ease, bowing and rising in chant and whistle—he takes himself to have attained his aim—how could he share with men like us a great man's cares and joys!
translations.idiomatic: You have rooted yourself in fragrant gardens, bathed in clear streams, flourished on sunny cliffs, and let your talents soar among the clouds. Below lies the dragon's ford; above, the phoenix's grove—glory dazzles before you, beauty tempts behind, fine friends at your left, fame racing at your right. You glide among peers and preen within curtained chambers, serene and at ease, chanting and whistling as though life were complete—how could you share a great man's joys and sorrows with men like us!

sentences.zh: 去矣嵇生，遠離隔矣！
