translations.literal: Gone is Master Ji, far parted and sundered!
translations.idiomatic: Farewell, Xi Kang—how far we are sundered!

sentences.zh: 煢煢飄寄，臨沙漠矣！

translations.literal: Alone and drifting, lodged, facing the desert!
translations.idiomatic: Alone I drift, adrift at the desert's edge!

sentences.zh: 悠悠三千，路難涉矣！

translations.literal: Vast and long, three thousand—hard the road to cross!
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand leagues stretch before me—how hard the road to cross!

sentences.zh: 攜手之期，邈無日矣！

translations.literal: The time of joined hands—remote, no day!
translations.idiomatic: The day we might join hands again seems endlessly far!

sentences.zh: 思心彌結，誰云釋矣！

translations.literal: Thinking heart ever more bound—who says it is released!
translations.idiomatic: My thoughts bind ever tighter—who says they can be loosed!

sentences.zh: 無金玉爾音而有遐心。

translations.literal: Without gold and jade is your message, yet there is a far-reaching heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though no precious word comes from you, my heart reaches far to you.

sentences.zh: 身雖胡越，意存斷金。

translations.literal: Though body is Hu and Yue apart, intent remains severing-gold.
translations.idiomatic: Though our bodies stand as far apart as north and south, our bond remains unbreakable as sworn gold.

sentences.zh: 各敬爾儀，敦履璞沈，繁華流蕩，君子弗欽。

translations.literal: Each respect your deportment, earnestly tread submerged uncut jade—flowery splendor drifting in dissipation, the gentleman does not esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Guard your conduct, keep your uncut jade hidden in depth; the gentleman does not prize gaudy dissipation.

sentences.zh: 臨紙意結，知復何云。

translations.literal: Facing the paper, intent knots—knowing again what to say.
translations.idiomatic: Facing this page my thoughts knot tight—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 至身長七尺四寸，論議精辯，有從橫才氣。

translations.literal: Zhi's body was seven chi four cun in height; in discourse and debate he was refined and acute and had the talent-air of vertical-horizontal persuaders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stood seven feet four inches tall; his speech was sharp and incisive in the manner of a wandering strategist.

sentences.zh: 遼西舉郡計吏，到洛，與父相遇。

translations.literal: Liaoxi nominated him commandery accounting clerk; arriving at Luoyang he encountered his father.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi recommended him as chief clerk for fiscal reporting; in Luoyang he unexpectedly met his father.

sentences.zh: 時母已亡，父欲令其宦立，弗之告，仍戒以不歸，至乃還遼西。

translations.literal: At that time his mother had already died; his father wished to cause him to establish himself through office and did not inform him of this, still enjoining him not to return—Zhi thereupon returned to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had died without his knowledge—his father hid the news so Zhao could establish a career and forbade him to come home; Zhao therefore turned back toward Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 幽州三辟部從事，斷九獄，見稱精審。

translations.literal: Youzhou thrice summoned him as staff attendant to the ministry; he adjudicated nine cases and was praised as rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou repeatedly appointed him section aide; he closed nine criminal cases and earned praise for meticulous judgment.

sentences.zh: 太康中，以良吏赴洛，方知母亡。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era, because he was a good official he went to Luoyang—only then did he learn his mother had died.
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang he qualified as an exemplary official and was summoned to court—only then did he learn his mother was gone.

sentences.zh: 初，至自恥士伍，欲以宦學立名，期於榮養。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhi himself was ashamed of being a common soldier and wished by office and learning to establish a name, aiming at honored support.
translations.idiomatic: Once ashamed of his commoner's station, he had hoped office and scholarship would win honor enough to support his parents in style.

sentences.zh: 既而其志不就，號憤慟哭，歐血而卒，時年三十七。

translations.literal: But thereafter his aim was not realized; he wailed in rage and wept in grief, vomited blood and died—at that time age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When that dream collapsed he howled and wept until blood burst from his throat; he died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 鄒湛

translations.literal: Zou Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan

sentences.zh: 鄒湛，字潤甫，南陽新野人也。

translations.literal: Zou Zhan, style Runfu, was a man of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan, courtesy name Runfu, hailed from Xinye in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父軌，魏左將軍。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Left General of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zou Gui had served Wei as Left General.

sentences.zh: 湛少以才學知名，仕魏曆通事郎、太學博士。

translations.literal: In youth Zhan was famed for talent and learning; serving Wei he passed through Communicator Gentleman and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated young for breadth of learning, he served Wei as communicator gentleman and erudite at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，轉尚書郎、廷尉平、征南從事中郎，深為羊祜所器重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Justice Evaluation, and Staff Officer on the South Expedition—he was deeply prized by Yang Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he moved through masters-of-writing posts, justice reviewer, and aide on the southern campaign—Yang Hu esteemed him greatly.

sentences.zh: 入為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then called in as junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太康中，拜散騎常侍，出補渤海太守，轉太傅楊駿長史，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, went out to fill the post of governor of Bohai, transferred to be chief clerk to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then governor of Bohai, later chief secretary to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, and finally palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 駿誅，以僚佐免官。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, by being a subordinate staff member he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's fall cost him his post as a member of the discredited staff.

sentences.zh: 尋起為散騎常侍、國子祭酒，轉少府。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer of the National University, and transferred to Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reinstated as cavalier attendant and libationer of the Imperial College, then moved to head the Lesser Treasury.

sentences.zh: 元康末卒，所著詩及論事議二十五首，為時所重。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Yuankang; his writings—poetry and discussion pieces on affairs in twenty-five pieces—were valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the close of Yuankang; twenty-five poems and policy essays won wide respect.

sentences.zh: 初，湛嘗夢見一人，自稱甄舒仲，餘無所言，如此非一。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhan once dreamed of a man who called himself Zhen Shuzhong—otherwise nothing was said; it was so not once.
translations.idiomatic: Zou repeatedly dreamed of a figure calling himself Zhen Shuzhong who said nothing more—the dream returned again and again.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃悟曰：「吾宅西有積土敗瓦，其中必有死人。

translations.literal: After a long time he at last understood, saying, "West of my residence there is piled earth and ruined tile—inside there must be a dead person.
translations.idiomatic: At length he understood: "West of my house lie rubble piles—someone lies buried beneath them.

sentences.zh: 甄舒仲者，予舍西土瓦中人也。」

translations.literal: As for Zhen Shuzhong—he is a person among the earth and tile west of my house."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Shuzhong" is the restless soul beneath the rubble west of my gate."

sentences.zh: 檢之，果然，厚加斂葬。

translations.literal: Investigating it, it was indeed so; he generously ordered burial rites.
translations.idiomatic: They dug and found him, then laid the bones to rest with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，遂夢此人來謝。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, thereupon he dreamed this person came to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: That night the figure visited his dreams to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 子捷，字太應，亦有文才。

translations.literal: His son Jie, style Taiying, also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zou Jie, courtesy name Taiying, inherited literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 永康中，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongkang era he was Gentleman of Cavalier Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongkang he served as gentleman of cavalier attendance.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡逆，捷與陸機等俱作禪文。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Sima Lun usurped in rebellion, Jie together with Lu Ji and others jointly composed the abdication document.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne, Zou Jie joined Lu Ji and others in drafting the forced abdication edict.

sentences.zh: 倫誅，坐下廷尉，遇赦免。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, [Jie] sat as defendant before the Commandant of Justice; encountering amnesty he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's execution landed him before the commandant of justice; an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後為太傅參軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Army Adjutant to the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as adjutant on the grand tutor's staff.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the final years of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 棗據

translations.literal: Zao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Ju

sentences.zh: 棗據，字道彥，潁川長社人也。

translations.literal: Zao Ju, style Daoyan, was a man of Changshe in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Ju, courtesy name Daoyan, came from Changshe in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 本姓棘，其先避仇改焉。

translations.literal: Originally the surname was Ji; his ancestors changed it to flee blood-feud.
translations.idiomatic: The clan originally bore the surname Ji but changed it generations ago to escape a vendetta.

sentences.zh: 父叔禕，魏钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His father Shu Yi was governor of Julu in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao Shuwei governed Julu under Wei.

sentences.zh: 據美容貌，善文辭。

translations.literal: Ju had handsome facial appearance and was skilled in literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and eloquent, he cut a striking figure at court.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，辟大將軍府，出為山陽令，有政績。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was summoned to the Grand General's headquarters; he went out as magistrate of Shanyang and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the grand general's bureau, then governed Shanyang county with a solid record.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎，轉右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and transferred to Assistant Director on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of the masters of writing and then assistant director on the right.

sentences.zh: 賈充伐吳，請為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong campaigned against Wu he requested [Ju] as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong drafted him as middle staff officer for the Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍還，徙黃門侍郎、冀州刺史、太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was shifted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Inspector of Ji province, and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops came home he served successively as gentleman at the Yellow Gates, Ji provincial inspector, and junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太康中卒，時年五十餘。

translations.literal: He died in the Taikang era at age over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Taikang in his early fifties.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦論四十五首，遇亂多亡失。

translations.literal: What he composed—poetry, fu, and discourses in forty-five pieces—when encountering turmoil mostly perished and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five poems, rhapsodies, and essays bore his name; most vanished in the wars.

sentences.zh: 子腆，字玄方，亦以文章顯。

translations.literal: His son Tian, style Xuanfang, also by literature showed distinction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zao Tian, courtesy name Xuanfang, likewise won fame as a writer.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中為襄城太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era he was governor of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he governed Xiangcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟嵩，字台產，才藝尤美，為太子中庶子、散騎常侍，為石勒所殺。

translations.literal: Younger brother Song, style Taichan—talent and arts especially fine—was Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; he was killed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zao Song, courtesy name Taichan, combined literary and artistic gifts; he served as junior mentor and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary until Shi Le had him executed.

sentences.zh: 褚陶

translations.literal: Chu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tao

sentences.zh: 褚陶，字季雅，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Chu Tao, style Jiya, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tao, courtesy name Jiya, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 弱不好弄，少而聰慧，清淡閑默，以墳典自娛。

translations.literal: In youth he did not like playing; young he was clever and wise, pure and quiet, leisurely silent, taking the tomb classics as self-amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he shunned rough games; precocious and reflective, he preferred quiet study of the classical corpus.

sentences.zh: 年十三，作《鷗鳥》、《水磑》二賦，見者奇之。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he composed two fu, "Gulls" and "Water Mill"; those who saw them deemed them marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he wrote the rhapsodies "Gulls" and "The Water Mill," astonishing everyone who read them.

sentences.zh: 陶嘗謂所親曰：「聖賢備在黃卷中，舍此何求！」

translations.literal: Tao once said to those close to him, "Sages and worthies are fully contained in yellow-bound scrolls—apart from this what do we seek!"
translations.idiomatic: He told friends, "Everything worth knowing sits between yellow covers—what else is there to chase?"

sentences.zh: 州郡辟，不就。

translations.literal: The province and commandery summoned him; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial posts came calling; he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 吳平，召補尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified he was summoned to fill Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu surrendered he was appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 張華見之，謂陸機曰：「君兄弟龍躍雲津，顧彥先鳳鳴朝陽，謂東南之寶已盡，不意復見褚生。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua saw him he said to Lu Ji, "Your lordship's brothers leap as dragons at the cloud ford; Gu Yanxian cries as the phoenix at morning sun—I thought the treasures of the southeast were exhausted; I did not expect again to see Master Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua told Lu Ji, "Your clan springs like dragons across the cloudy ford; Gu Yanxian sings like the phoenix at dawn—I assumed the southeast had spent every jewel of talent, then Chu Tao appeared."

sentences.zh: 機曰：「公但未睹不鳴不躍者耳。」

translations.literal: Ji said, "My lord only has not yet seen those who neither cry nor leap."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji replied, "You simply have not met everyone who keeps silent and still."

sentences.zh: 華曰：「故知延州之德不孤，川嶽之寶不匱矣。」

translations.literal: Hua said, "Thus I know the virtue of Yanzhou is not solitary; treasures of rivers and mountains are not exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua answered, "So virtue like Ji Zha's need not stand alone; every river and peak still hides treasure."

sentences.zh: 遷九真太守，轉中尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted governor of Jiuzhen and transferred to Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chu later governed Jiuzhen before becoming metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 年五十五卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-five he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 王沉

translations.literal: Wang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen

sentences.zh: 王沉，字彥伯，高平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, style Yanbo, was a man of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, courtesy name Yanbo, came from Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 少有俊才，出於寒素，不能隨俗沈浮，為時豪所抑。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; he came from humble plain background and could not float or sink with custom—he was suppressed by the powerful of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted but from an obscure house, he refused to curry favor with great families and paid for it in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 仕郡文學掾，鬱鬱不得志，乃作《釋時論》，其辭曰：東野丈人觀時以居，隱耕汙腴之墟。

translations.literal: He served as commandery Instructor Clerk, depressed without realizing his aims—thereupon he composed "Discourse on Discerning the Times," its words saying: East-field Elder observed the age to dwell, hiding himself to plow fertile muddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: He held the minor post of commandery literary instructor, bitter and thwarted, and wrote "Discourse on Discerning the Times," which begins: East-field Elder watched the times and made his home, living in hidden tillage on rich muddy ground.

sentences.zh: 有冰氏之子者，出自冱寒之谷，過而問塗。

translations.literal: There was a son of the Ice clan who came forth from a valley of freezing cold, passed by and asked the way.
translations.idiomatic: A youth of the Ice clan came from a valley of bitter cold and, passing by, asked directions.

sentences.zh: 丈人曰：「子奚自？」

translations.literal: The elder said, "From where do you come?"
translations.idiomatic: The elder asked, "Where do you come from?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「自涸陰之鄉。」

translations.literal: He said, "From the land of dried shade."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "From the land of frozen shade."

sentences.zh: 「奚適？」

translations.literal: "Where are you going?"
translations.idiomatic: "And where are you bound?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「欲適煌煌之堂。」

translations.literal: He said, "I wish to go to the resplendent hall."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I wish to reach the resplendent hall."

sentences.zh: 丈人曰：「入煌煌之堂者，必有赫赫之光。

translations.literal: The elder said, "Those who enter the resplendent hall must have blazing brilliant light.
translations.idiomatic: The elder said, "Those who enter the resplendent hall must carry blazing brilliance.

sentences.zh: 今子困於寒而欲求諸熱，無得熱之方。」

translations.literal: Now you are trapped in cold yet seek heat from without—you have no means to obtain heat."
translations.idiomatic: You are trapped in cold yet seek warmth from without—you have no way to gain it."

sentences.zh: 冰子瞿然曰：「胡為其然也？」

translations.literal: Ice-son started and said, "Why is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: Ice-son started in alarm and asked, "Why should that be so?"

sentences.zh: 丈人曰：「融融者皆趣熱之士，其得爐冶之門者，惟挾炭之子。

translations.literal: The elder said, "Those who glow warm are all men hurrying toward heat; those who gain entry to the furnace and forge are only sons who carry charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: The elder said, "Those who bask in warmth are all men rushing toward heat; only those who carry charcoal may pass through the furnace gate.

sentences.zh: 苟非斯人，不如其已。」

translations.literal: If one is not such a man, better to stop."
translations.idiomatic: If you are not such a man, you had better turn back."

sentences.zh: 冰子曰：「吾聞宗廟之器不要華林之木，四門之賓何必冠蓋之族。

translations.literal: Ice-son said, "I have heard that vessels of the ancestral temple need not be of ornamental-forest wood; guests at the four gates need not be of cap-and-canopy clans.
translations.idiomatic: Ice-son said, "I have heard that temple vessels need not come from ornamental groves, and guests at the four gates need not be of noble houses.

sentences.zh: 前賢有解韋索而佩硃韍舍徒擔而乘丹轂。

translations.literal: Former worthies there were who loosed hemp cords and wore vermillion knee-guards, cast aside the porter's pole and rode vermillion carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Worthies of old cast off hemp ropes to wear vermillion knee-guards, abandoned the porter's pole to ride vermillion carriages.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，何恤而無祿！

translations.literal: From this it is said—why worry that there will be no salary!
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, why fear that office and salary will not come!

sentences.zh: 惟先生告我塗之速也。」

translations.literal: Only, sir, tell me the swift road."
translations.idiomatic: Only tell me, sir, the quickest road."

sentences.zh: 丈人曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: The elder said, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The elder cried, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 子聞得之若是，不知時之在彼。

translations.literal: You have heard attainment like this, yet do not know that the age lies over there.
translations.idiomatic: You have heard that success can come this way, but you do not see that the times have changed.

sentences.zh: 吾將釋子。

translations.literal: I will explain to you.
translations.idiomatic: Let me explain it to you.

sentences.zh: 夫道有安危，時有險易，才有所應，行有所適。

translations.literal: The Way has safety and danger; the age has hardship and ease; talent has what it answers to; conduct has what it suits.
translations.idiomatic: The Way has its safe and perilous courses; the times have their hard and easy seasons; talent meets what it is fitted for; action suits what the moment requires.

sentences.zh: 英奇奮於從橫之世，賢智顯于霸王之初，當厄難則騁權譎以良圖，值製作則展儒道以暢攄，是則袞龍出於縕褐，卿相起於匹夫，故有朝賤而夕貴，先卷而後舒。

translations.literal: Heroes and marvels exerted themselves in the age of vertical and horizontal alliances; worthies and sages showed themselves at the beginning of hegemons and kings; meeting hardship they unleashed stratagem for good plans; meeting creation they spread Ruist Way to pour forth freely—thus dragon robes came from coarse hemp, ministers and chancellors rose from common men; hence morning low and evening noble, first rolled up then unrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes flourished in the age of warring alliances; worthies shone at the rise of hegemons and kings. In hardship they deployed stratagem; in eras of creation they unfolded Confucian teaching. Dragon robes emerged from coarse cloth; ministers rose from common men. Men were low at dawn and noble by evening; fortune first curled tight, then opened wide.

sentences.zh: 當斯時也，豈計門資之高卑，論勢位之輕重乎！

translations.literal: In such a time, who would reckon the high or low of family standing, or debate the light or heavy of power and rank!
translations.idiomatic: In such times, who weighed family pedigree or debated the heft of rank and power!

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise.

sentences.zh: 上聖下明，時隆道寧，群後逸豫，宴安守平。

translations.literal: Above, the sage; below, the enlightened; the age lofty, the Way tranquil; the host of lords at ease, feasting in peace and guarding stability.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign above is sage; ministers below are enlightened; the age is prosperous and the Way at peace; lords live at ease, feasting in security and guarding stability.

sentences.zh: 百辟君子，奕世相生，公門有公，卿門有卿。

translations.literal: The hundred ministers and gentlemen beget one another generation after generation; the duke's gate has dukes, the minister's gate has ministers.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers beget high ministers generation after generation; duke's houses produce dukes, minister's houses produce ministers.

sentences.zh: 指禿腐骨，不簡蚩儜。

translations.literal: Pointing at bald rotten bones, they do not select the ignorant and clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: They point to withered bones and never choose the ignorant and crude.

sentences.zh: 多士豐于貴族，爵命不出閨庭。

translations.literal: Many scholars abound among noble clans; titles and commands do not leave the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men cluster among noble houses; offices and honors never leave the inner court.

sentences.zh: 四門穆穆，綺襦是盈，仍叔之子，皆為老成。

translations.literal: The four gates are solemn; silk jackets fill them; sons of Chief of Music are all called seasoned elders.
translations.idiomatic: The four gates stand solemn; brocade coats fill them; sons of hereditary musicians pass for seasoned elders.

sentences.zh: 賤有常辱，貴有常榮，肉食繼踵于華屋，疏飯襲跡於耨耕。

translations.literal: The lowly have constant disgrace; the noble have constant glory; meat-eaters follow in succession in splendid houses, plain rice follows in traces upon harrowed fields.
translations.idiomatic: The lowly suffer constant shame; the noble enjoy constant honor. Meat-eaters crowd splendid houses in endless succession; plain rice trails behind the plow.

sentences.zh: 談名位者以諂媚附勢，舉高譽者因資而隨形。

translations.literal: Those who speak of fame and rank use flattery to cling to power; those who raise lofty praise follow resources and shift with form.
translations.idiomatic: Men who talk of rank flatter and cling to power; men who win high praise shape themselves to their patrons' resources.

sentences.zh: 至乃空囂者以泓噌為雅量，瑣慧者以淺利為槍槍，脢胎者以無檢為弘曠，僂垢者以守意為堅貞。

translations.literal: So much so that empty boasters take deep resonance as elegant breadth; petty clever ones take shallow profit as sharpness; timid ones in the womb take lack of restraint as vast openness; hunchbacked filth takes guarding one's intent as steadfast constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Empty boasters take bombast for breadth of spirit; petty clever men take small gain for sharp wit; the timid take license for magnanimity; the squalid take stubbornness for constancy.

sentences.zh: 嘲哮者以粗發為高亮，韞蠢者以色厚為篤誠，痷婪者以博納為通濟，眂々者以難入為凝清，拉答者有沈重之譽，嗛閃者得清剿之聲，嗆啍怯畏于謙讓，闒茸勇敢於饕諍。

translations.literal: Mock-shouters take coarse outburst as high brilliance; hidden stupidity takes thick coloration as deep sincerity; gluttonous greed takes broad acceptance as universal passage; squinting eyes take difficulty of entry as austere clarity; fumblers gain reputation for weightiness; modest flashers gain voice for clear cutting; choking stammerers appear timid in humility and yielding; shabby muddle appears brave in greedy quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Mockers take coarse shouting for noble brilliance; concealed fools take thick flattery for deep sincerity; gluttons take broad indulgence for worldly mastery; squinting men take aloofness for austere purity; fumblers win praise for gravity; false modesty wins renown for sharp clarity; stammering cowards pass for humility; shabby mediocrities pass for bold disputants.

sentences.zh: 斯皆寒素之死病，榮達之嘉名。

translations.literal: These are all fatal illnesses of the humble and plain, and fine names of glory and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: These are the mortal sickness of poor scholars—and the honored names of worldly success.

sentences.zh: 凡茲流也，視其用心，察其所安，責人必急，於己恆寬。

translations.literal: All such types, viewing their use of heart and inspecting where they rest—demanding of others they are always harsh; toward themselves always lenient.
translations.idiomatic: All such men, judged by their motives and their comforts, are harsh toward others and lenient toward themselves.

sentences.zh: 德無厚而自貴，位未高而自尊，眼罔向而遠視，鼻𪖷𪖐而刺天。

translations.literal: Virtue not thick yet they prize themselves; rank not yet high yet they esteem themselves; eyes not turned yet gaze far; noses snorting upward pierce the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Without deep virtue they hold themselves dear; without high rank they esteem themselves high; their eyes stare into the distance without looking straight; their nostrils flare toward heaven.

sentences.zh: 忌惡君子，悅媚小人，敖蔑道素，懾籲權門。

translations.literal: They hate and loathe gentlemen, delight in flattering petty men, disdain the plain Way, and cower and plead at power's gates.
translations.idiomatic: They hate true gentlemen and delight in flattering petty men; they scorn plain integrity and cringe before the gates of power.

sentences.zh: 心以利傾，智以勢惛，姻黨相扇，毀譽交紛。

translations.literal: Hearts tilt by profit; wisdom dims by power; marriage cliques fan one another; slander and praise tangle together.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts bend to profit; minds grow dull before power; kin and faction stir one another; slander and praise swirl together.

sentences.zh: 當局迷於所受，聽采惑于所聞。

translations.literal: Those in office are confused by what they receive; in listening and gathering they are deluded by what they hear.
translations.idiomatic: Men in office are blinded by what they receive; in judgment they are misled by what they hear.

sentences.zh: 京邑翼翼，群士千億，奔集勢門，求官買職，童僕窺其車乘，閽寺相其服飾，親客陰參於靖室，疏賓徙倚於門側。

translations.literal: The capital stands in array; gentlemen by the billions; they rush and gather at power's gates, seeking office and buying posts; boy servants peer at their carriages and teams; gatekeepers inspect their dress and ornaments; intimate guests secretly wait in quiet rooms; distant guests linger leaning at the gate side.
translations.idiomatic: The capital teems with arrayed splendor; thousands upon thousands of scholars rush to powerful gates, seeking office and buying posts. Servants study their carriages; gatekeepers appraise their dress; favored guests wait in private rooms; humble visitors linger at the gate.

sentences.zh: 時因接見，矜曆容色，心懷內荏，外詐剛直，譚道義謂之俗生，論政刑以為鄙極。

translations.literal: Occasionally received in audience, they display proud bearing and color; hearts hold inner weakness, outwardly feigning uprightness; speaking of the Way and righteousness they call it vulgar living; discussing government and punishment they deem it the depth of baseness.
translations.idiomatic: When occasionally received in audience they put on proud looks, weak within yet feigning stern integrity; they call talk of the Way and righteousness vulgar, and treat discussion of government and law as the depth of baseness.

sentences.zh: 高會曲宴，惟言遷除消息，官無大小，問是誰力。

translations.literal: At lofty gatherings and private banquets they speak only of promotion and removal news; office great or small—they ask whose power it was.
translations.idiomatic: At grand feasts and private banquets they speak only of promotions and dismissals; for every office, high or low, they ask whose influence secured it.

sentences.zh: 今以子孤寒，懷真抱素，志陵雲霄，偶景獨步，直順常道，關津難渡，欲騁韓盧，時無狡兔，眾塗圮塞，投足何錯！」

translations.literal: Now because you are solitary and cold, embracing truth and holding plainness, ambition vaulting the clouds, walking alone with your shadow, going straight along the common Way—passes and fords are hard to cross; you wish to unleash Han Lu, yet the time has no cunning hare; the many roads are ruined and blocked—where can you set foot without error!"
translations.idiomatic: You are solitary and poor, holding truth and plain integrity; your ambition towers to the clouds, yet you walk alone with your shadow, keeping to the straight path. The passes are hard to cross. You would unleash a swift hound, but there is no cunning hare; every road is blocked—where can you set foot without stumbling!"

sentences.zh: 於是冰子釋然乃悟曰：「富貴人之所欲，貧賤人之所惡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ice-son, released and enlightened, said, "Wealth and honor are what people desire; poverty and baseness are what people hate.
translations.idiomatic: Then Ice-son, suddenly enlightened, said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; poverty and low estate are what men hate.

sentences.zh: 僕少長於孔顏之門，久處於清寒之路，不謂熱勢自共遮錮。

translations.literal: I from youth grew up at the gate of Confucius and Yan, long dwelt on the road of pure cold—I did not suppose that hot power would together block and bind me.
translations.idiomatic: I was raised from youth in the school of Confucius and Yan Hui and have long walked the road of clean poverty—I never thought the heat of power would shut me in.

sentences.zh: 敬承明誨，服我初素，彈琴詠典，以保年祚。

translations.literal: Respectfully I receive your clear instruction, return to my original plainness, pluck the zither and chant the classics, to preserve my years.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully accept your teaching, return to my original plainness, play the zither and chant the classics, and so preserve my years.

sentences.zh: 伯成、延陵，高節可慕。

translations.literal: Bo Cheng and Yanling—lofty integrity worthy of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Cheng and Ji Zha of Yanling—lofty integrity worthy of admiration.

sentences.zh: 丹轂滅族，呂霍哀吟，朝榮夕滅，旦飛暮沈。

translations.literal: Vermillion carriages destroy clans; Lü and Huo mourn in lament; morning glory, evening extinction; dawn flying, dusk sinking.
translations.idiomatic: Vermillion carriages bring clan destruction; the houses of Lü and Huo ended in lament; glory at dawn dies by dusk; flight at morning sinks by evening.

sentences.zh: 聃周道師，巢由德林。

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi were teachers of the Way; Chao Fu and Xu You were groves of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi and Zhuangzi were masters of the Way; Chao Fu and Xu You were forests of virtue.

sentences.zh: 豐屋蔀家，《易》著明箴。

translations.literal: A grand house shadows the family—the "Changes" sets forth a clear admonition.
translations.idiomatic: A grand house casts shadow over the family—the "Book of Changes" gives clear warning.

sentences.zh: 人薄位尊，積罰難任，三郤屍晉，宋華咎深，投扃正幅，實獲我心。」

translations.literal: Men slight yet rank honored; accumulated punishment hard to bear; the Three Xi left corpses in Jin; Song Hua's blame was deep—casting the bolt and straightening the hem truly obtained my heart."
translations.idiomatic: When worth is slight yet rank is high, accumulated guilt becomes unbearable; the Three Xi families left corpses in Jin; Song Hua's fault ran deep. To bolt the door and straighten one's robe—that truly wins my heart."

sentences.zh: 是時王政陵遲，官才失實，君子多退而窮處，遂終於里閭。

translations.literal: At this time royal administration declined; official talent lost substance; gentlemen mostly withdrew and dwelt in hardship—thereupon they ended in hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Royal government had slackened; offices went to mediocrities; men of worth withdrew to rustic lanes and died unheard.

sentences.zh: 元康初，松滋令吳郡蔡洪字叔開，有才名，作《孤奮論》，與《釋時》意同，讀之者莫不歎息焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, Cai Hong of Wu commandery, style Shukai, magistrate of Songzi—had a reputation for talent—composed "Discourse of Lone Exertion"; with "Explaining the Age" the intent was the same—those who read it none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang Cai Hong of Wu—magistrate of Songzi, courtesy name Shukai—won fame for "Discourse on Relentless Effort," echoing Wang's themes and drawing sighs from every reader.

sentences.zh: 張翰

translations.literal: Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han

sentences.zh: 張翰，字季鷹，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Han, style Jiying, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han, courtesy name Jiying, came from Wu county in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父儼，吳大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Grand Herald of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yan had served Wu as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 翰有清才，善屬文，而縱任不拘，時人號為「江東步兵。」

translations.literal: Han had pure talent, skilled in composing texts, yet unrestrained and unbound—people of the time titled him "Infantry Lieutenant east of the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: His prose was lucid and his habits bohemian; contemporaries nicknamed him "Wu Kingdom's Infantry Captain"

sentences.zh: 會稽賀循赴命入洛，經吳閶門，於船中彈琴。

translations.literal: He Xun of Kuaiji answered summons and entered Luoyang; passing Wu's Chang Gate he played the zither in the boat.
translations.idiomatic: —alluding to Ruan Ji. One day He Xun of Kuaiji traveled to Luoyang under summons; mooring at Wu's Chang Gate he played his lute on board.

sentences.zh: 翰初不相識，乃就循言譚，便大相欽悅。

translations.literal: Han at first did not know him; thereupon he approached Xun and conversed—at once they greatly admired each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang did not know him at first but stepped aboard to talk and found an instant soulmate.

sentences.zh: 問循，知其入洛，翰曰：「吾亦有事北京。」

translations.literal: He asked Xun; learning that he was entering Luoyang, Han said, "I too have business in the northern capital."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that He was bound for the capital, Zhang said, "I have errands in the north as well."

sentences.zh: 便同載即去，而不告家人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they rode in the same carriage and left immediately, without telling family members.
translations.idiomatic: They shared a carriage and vanished without a word to kin.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏辟為大司馬東曹掾。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, summoned him as Clerk of the East Bureau under the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, appointed him clerk in the grand marshal's eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 冏時執權，翰謂同郡顧榮曰：「天下紛紛，禍難未已。

translations.literal: When Jiong held power Han said to Gu Rong of the same commandery, "All under heaven is tumultuous; disasters are not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Jiong dominated court, Zhang warned fellow Wu native Gu Rong, "The realm boils and the killing is not over.

sentences.zh: 夫有四海之名者，求退良難。

translations.literal: For one who has fame within the four seas, seeking withdrawal is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Renown across the empire makes retreat almost impossible.

sentences.zh: 吾本山林間人，無望于時。

translations.literal: I am originally a man among mountains and forests—I have no expectation in this age.
translations.idiomatic: I belong among hills and streams, not this court.

sentences.zh: 子善以明防前，以智慮後。」

translations.literal: You, sir, are good at guarding what lies ahead with clarity and pondering what follows with wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: You read trouble coming and plan what follows—skills I lack."

sentences.zh: 榮執其手，愴然曰：「吾亦與子采南山蕨，飲三江水耳。」

translations.literal: Rong grasped his hand and mournfully said, "I too with you would gather bracken on South Mountain and drink the Three Rivers' water, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Gu seized his hand and said sadly, "I would gladly pick ferns on South Mountain with you and drink only river water."

sentences.zh: 翰因見秋風起，乃思吳中菰菜、蓴羹、鱸魚膾，曰：「人生貴得適志，何能羈宦數千里以要名爵乎！」

translations.literal: Han because he saw the autumn wind arise then thought of wild rice shoots, water-shield soup, and perch sashimi in Wu—he said, "In human life what is prized is obtaining one's mind's ease—how can one be tied to office thousands of li to seek rank and title!"
translations.idiomatic: When autumn wind rose he craved Wu water-shield soup, wild rice, and sliced perch. "Life is too short to chain yourself a thousand miles from home for a hollow title!"

sentences.zh: 遂命駕而歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered carriage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his carriage and rode east that same day.

sentences.zh: 著《首丘賦》，文多不載。

translations.literal: He composed the "Fu on Longing for the Burrow Mound"; much of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Rhapsody on the Hill of Home" (largely omitted here).

sentences.zh: 俄而冏敗，人皆謂之見機。

translations.literal: Soon Jiong was defeated; people all called him one who saw the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong fell soon afterward everyone called Zhang prescient.

sentences.zh: 然府以其輒去，除吏名。

translations.literal: Yet the bureau because he abruptly left struck his name from the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry nevertheless struck him from the rolls for desertion.

sentences.zh: 翰任心自適，不求當世。

translations.literal: Han followed his heart and suited himself, not seeking validation from his age.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his mood and cared nothing for reputation among his peers.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「卿乃可縱適一時，獨不為身後名邪？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "You indeed may indulge ease for a moment—do you alone not act for posthumous fame?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "You indulge the moment—have you no thought for how posterity will judge you?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「使我有身後名，不如即時一杯酒。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Let me have posthumous fame—better an immediate cup of wine."
translations.idiomatic: "I'd trade any posthumous fame for another cup of wine tonight."

sentences.zh: 時人貴其曠達。

translations.literal: People of the time prized his broad openness.
translations.idiomatic: His candor passed for profundity in that cynical age.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was supremely filial; encountering mourning for his mother he sorrowed and wasted beyond ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he mourned his mother past what ritual allowed.

sentences.zh: 年五十七卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-seven he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其文筆數十篇行於世。

translations.literal: His literary brushings several tens of pieces circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen essays and poems survived him.

sentences.zh: 庾闡

translations.literal: Yu Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan

sentences.zh: 庾闡，字仲初，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chan, style Zhongchu, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan, courtesy name Zhongchu, hailed from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖輝，安北長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was chief clerk to the General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Hui had served as chief clerk on the staff of the general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 父東，以勇力聞。

translations.literal: His father Dong was famed for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Dong was famed for raw strength.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，有西域健胡趫捷無敵，晉人莫敢與校。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time there was a stalwart Hu from the Western Regions, agile and unmatched—people of Jin none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu a Western Regions wrestler appeared whom no Jin challenger could best.

sentences.zh: 帝募勇士，惟東應選，遂撲殺之，名震殊俗。

translations.literal: The emperor recruited brave warriors—only Dong answered selection—thereupon he threw and killed him; his name shook foreign customs.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sought brawlers; Yu Dong alone volunteered and threw the man dead—his fame echoed beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 闡好學，九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Chan loved learning; at age nine he could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan loved books and composed polished essays at nine.

sentences.zh: 少隨舅孫氏過江。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his maternal uncle's Sun clan in crossing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he crossed the Yangzi with his mother's Sun kin.

sentences.zh: 母隨兄肇為樂安長史，在項城。

translations.literal: His mother followed elder brother Zhao who was chief clerk to Le'an—at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived with her brother in Xiangcheng while he served as chief clerk in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，為石勒所陷，闡母亦沒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia [the city] was seized by Shi Le—Chan's mother also perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le stormed the city at the close of Yongjia, Yu's mother died in the sack.

sentences.zh: 闡不櫛沐，不婚宦，絕酒肉，垂二十年，鄉親稱之。

translations.literal: Chan did not comb or wash, did not marry or take office, cut off wine and meat—for nearly twenty years village kin praised him.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he neither groomed nor married, touched neither meat nor wine—neighbors admired his devotion.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，元帝為晉王，辟之，皆不行。

translations.literal: The province nominated him cultivated talent; when Yuan-di was Prince of Jin he summoned him—both times he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The province ranked him as elite scholar and Prince Yuan-di twice offered posts—Yu refused each summons.

sentences.zh: 後為太宰、西陽王羕掾，累遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Later he was aide to the Grand Marshal and Prince of Xiyang, Sima Yi—by stages he was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the staff of Sima Yi, Prince of Xiyang and grand marshal, and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之難，闡出奔郗鑒，為司空參軍。

translations.literal: During Su Jun's rebellion Chan fled out to Xi Jian and became Army Adjutant to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun seized the capital Yu fled to Xi Jian and served as adjutant on the minister of works' staff.

sentences.zh: 峻平，以功賜爵吉陽縣男，拜彭城內史。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, by merit he was granted noble rank as Baron of Jiyang county and appointed Internal Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell Yu earned a barony at Jiyang and appointment as governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 鑒復請為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Jian again requested him as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian again named him middle staff officer.

sentences.zh: 尋召為散騎侍郎，領大著作。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Gentleman of Cavalier Attendance and concurrently supervised grand compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became cavalier gentleman-attendant and headed the imperial editorial office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出補零陵太守，入湘川，吊賈誼。

translations.literal: Shortly he went out to fill governor of Lingling; entering the Xiang river region he mourned Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted out as prefect of Lingling and traveled the Xiang lands to mourn Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：中興二十三載，余忝守衡南，鼓栧三江，路次巴陵，望君山而過洞庭，涉湘川而觀汨水，臨賈生投書之川，慨以永懷矣。

translations.literal: Its words said: in the twenty-third year of the Restoration, I am honored to guard south of Heng, beating oars on the three rivers; on the road I passed Baling, gazed at Jun Mountain and crossed Dongting, forded the Xiang and viewed the Miluo, and stood by the river where Jia Yi cast his letter into the water, stirred to lasting remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: The piece begins: in the twenty-third year of the Restoration, while I held office south of Mount Heng and rowed the three rivers, my route took me through Baling; I looked toward Jun Mountain and crossed Lake Dongting, traveled the Xiang and came to the Miluo, and stood by the stream where Jia Yi had cast his letter into the water, filled with enduring sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及造長沙，觀其遺象，喟然有感，乃吊之云：偉哉蘭生而芳，玉產而潔，陽葩熙冰，寒松負雪，莫邪挺鍔，天驥汗血，苟云其雋，誰與比傑！

translations.literal: When I reached Changsha and beheld his surviving image, I sighed with deep feeling and mourned him, saying: how great—orchid born and fragrant, jade produced and pure; sunny blossoms thrive upon ice, cold pine bears snow; Mo Ye draws its blade, the heavenly steed sweats blood; if one calls such talent outstanding, who could be matched as his peer!
translations.idiomatic: When I came to Changsha and saw what remained of him, I sighed with deep emotion and composed this lament: how splendid—the orchid born fragrant, jade mined pure; blossoms warm the ice, the pine shoulders snow; Mo Ye unsheathes its edge, the heavenly courser sweats blood—if such genius is called supreme, who could stand beside him as an equal!

sentences.zh: 是以高明倬茂，獨發奇秀，道率天真，不議世疚，煥乎若望舒耀景而焯群星，矯乎若翔鸞拊翼而逸宇宙也。

translations.literal: Thus lofty and brilliantly abundant, he alone brought forth singular excellence; the Way followed native truth and did not debate worldly afflictions; radiant as Wang Shu shining upon the scene and illuminating the host of stars, soaring as a flying phoenix beating its wings and escaping the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Thus eminent and splendid, he alone unfolded rare brilliance; the Way in him followed innate truth and he did not wrangle over worldly woes; he shone like the moon-charioteer brightening the sky and outshining the stars, and soared like a phoenix beating its wings and fleeing beyond the world.

sentences.zh: 飛榮洛汭，擢穎山東，質清浮磬，聲若孤桐，琅琅其璞，岩岩其峰，通道居正，而以天下為公，方駕逸步，不以曲路期通。

translations.literal: Glory flew at the bend of the Luo, and distinguished talent rose in Shandong; his substance was clear as a floating stone chime, his voice like a solitary paulownia; lustrous was his uncut jade, towering his peak; he opened the Way and dwelt in rectitude, taking all under Heaven as public, matching lofty paces and not expecting passage by crooked paths.
translations.idiomatic: Fame rose at Luoyang, and his brilliance emerged in the east; his character was clear as a resonant stone, his voice like a lone paulownia tree; his jade gleamed uncut, his peak stood sheer; he held the Way in rectitude and treated the realm as common ground, keeping pace with the great and never seeking advancement by devious means.

sentences.zh: 是以張高弘悲，聲激柱落，清唱未和，而桑濮代作，雖有惠音，莫過《韶》《濩》；

translations.literal: Thus he raised high and spread his grief; his voice was so intense that pillars fell; his clear song had not yet found harmony when licentious music of Sang and Pu took its place; though there was gracious sound, none surpassed the Shao and Hu;
translations.idiomatic: So he lifted his voice in vast sorrow until the sound shook pillars from their bases; his pure song had not yet found harmony when the wanton tunes of Sang and Pu replaced it; though gracious music existed, none surpassed the Shao and Hu;

sentences.zh: 雖有騰鱗，終僕一壑。

translations.literal: Though there were leaping scales, in the end they served only one gully.
translations.idiomatic: Though talent leapt like fish in flood, in the end it was confined to a single ravine.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 大庭既邈，玄風悠緬，皇道不以智隆，上德不以仁顯。

translations.literal: The age of the Great Hall is already remote, the dark wind far and withdrawn; the imperial Way is not exalted by intelligence alone, and highest virtue is not displayed by benevolence alone.
translations.idiomatic: The age of Great Harmony is already distant, and the subtle Way lies far behind; the royal path is not raised by wit alone, nor is supreme virtue shown by kindness alone.

sentences.zh: 三五親譽，其輒可仰而標；

translations.literal: The intimate praise of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—their tracks can be looked up to and taken as standards;
translations.idiomatic: The close renown of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors offers tracks one may look up to and take as models;

sentences.zh: 霸功雖逸，其塗可翼而闡，悲矣先生，何命之蹇！

translations.literal: Hegemonic achievements though transcendent—their paths can be winged and expounded; how sad, Master—how obstructed your fate!
translations.idiomatic: Though hegemonic merit may be sublime, its path can still be traced and explained; how pitiable, sir—how harsh was your fate!

sentences.zh: 懷寶如玉，而生運之淺！

translations.literal: He treasured talent like jade, yet life and fortune were shallow!
translations.idiomatic: He bore talent like jade in his breast, yet his life and his times were too brief!

sentences.zh: 昔咎繇謨虞，呂尚歸昌，德協充符，乃應帝王。

translations.literal: In old times Gao Yao counseled at Yu's court, and Lü Shang returned to Chang; virtue matched the fullness of the mandate and thus answered to emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Gao Yao advised Shun, and Lü Shang came home to the house of Chang; when virtue matched Heaven's fullness, men answered to emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 夷吾相桓，漢登蕭張；

translations.literal: Guan Zhong served Duke Huan, and Han elevated Xiao and Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yiwu served Duke Huan of Qi, and the Han raised Xiao He and Zhang Liang;

sentences.zh: 草廬三顧，臭若蘭芳。

translations.literal: Three visits were paid to the thatched hut, fragrant as orchid.
translations.idiomatic: Three visits were made to the thatched cottage, sweet as orchid fragrance.

sentences.zh: 是以道隱則蠖屈，數感則鳳睹，若棲不擇木，翔非九五，雖曰玉折，雋才何補！

translations.literal: Thus when the Way is hidden the inchworm curls up, and when fate responds the phoenix appears; if one perches without choosing the tree and soars not at the ninth and fifth positions, though it is called jade broken, what use is brilliant talent!
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Way lies hidden the inchworm curls, and when the times respond the phoenix appears; if one roosts without choosing the right tree and flies not at the sovereign height, though jade may break, what good is transcendent talent!

sentences.zh: 夫心非死灰，智必存形，形托神用，故能全生。

translations.literal: The heart is not dead ash, wisdom must preserve form, and form is entrusted to the spirit's function—thus one can preserve life whole.
translations.idiomatic: The heart is not dead ashes, wisdom must keep its form, and form relies on the spirit's use—by this a man may preserve his life entire.

sentences.zh: 奈何蘭膏，揚芳漢庭，摧景飆風，獨喪厥明。

translations.literal: Alas for orchid ointment spreading fragrance in the Han court—scattered glory in a whirlwind, alone it lost its brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for orchid balm that spread its fragrance in the Han court, only to have its radiance torn away by a sudden gale and lose its light alone.

sentences.zh: 悠悠太素，存亡一指，道來斯通，世往斯圮。

translations.literal: Far, far primordial simplicity—existence and extinction in one finger's span; when the Way comes, thus it connects, and when the age passes, thus it collapses.
translations.idiomatic: Remote primordial simplicity holds life and death in a single moment; when the Way arrives, all opens, and when the age departs, all falls to ruin.

sentences.zh: 吾哀其生，未見其死，敢不敬吊，寄之淥水。

translations.literal: I mourn his life and have not seen his death; how dare I not reverently mourn him—I send this to the clear waters.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for his life though I did not witness his death; how could I fail to offer this reverent lament and commit it to the clear stream?

sentences.zh: 後以疾，徵拜給事中，復領著作。

translations.literal: Later because of illness he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant Within the Yellow Gates—again heading compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health later brought him back to court as palace attendant while he again directed the history office.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史虞潭為太伯立碑，闡制其文。

translations.literal: Wu Internal Administrator Yu Tan erected a stele for Taibo—Chan composed its text.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Tan, interior governor of Wu, raised a monument to Taibo, Yu Chan drafted the inscription.

sentences.zh: 又作《揚都賦》，為世所重。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Fu on the Yang Capital"—it was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Yang Capital" enjoyed enormous esteem.

sentences.zh: 年五十四卒，諡曰貞，所著詩賦銘頌十卷行於世。

translations.literal: At age fifty-four he died; posthumous title was Zhen (Steadfast); what he composed—poetry, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies in ten fascicles—circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four with the posthumous epithet "Steadfast"; ten fascicles of verse, rhapsodies, and commemorative prose survive.

sentences.zh: 子肅之，亦有文藻著稱，歷給事中、相府記室、湘東太守。

translations.literal: His son Suzhi also had literary ornament and was famed—he passed through Palace Attendant, Recorder of the Minister's headquarters, and governor of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Suzhi inherited literary fame, serving as palace attendant, chief recorder on the minister's staff, and governor of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 太元中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Taiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Taiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 曹毗

translations.literal: Cao Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 曹毗，字輔佐，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Cao Pi, style Fuzuo, was a man of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi, courtesy name Fuzuo, came from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖休，魏大司馬。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Xiu was Grand Marshal of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Cao Xiu had been Wei grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 父識，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shi was General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao Shi commanded the right army.

sentences.zh: 毗少好文籍，善屬詞賦。

translations.literal: In youth Pi loved literary records and was skilled at composing ci and fu.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful bookworm and polished rhapsodist, he excelled at verse.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，除郎中，蔡謨舉為佐著作郎。

translations.literal: The commandery investigated him as filial and incorrupt; he was appointed Court Gentleman; Cai Mo nominated him as Assistant Gentleman Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His commandery nominated him as filial and honest; after appointment as court gentleman Cai Mo sponsored him as assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職。

translations.literal: Father mourning caused him to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷句章令，徵拜太學博士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted magistrate of Gouzhang and summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he governed Gouzhang county and was summoned as erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時桂陽張碩為神女杜蘭香所降，毗因以二篇詩嘲之，並續蘭香歌詩十篇，甚有文彩。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shuo of Guiyang was visited by the goddess Du Lanxiang—thereupon Pi by means of two poems ridiculed him, and also continued Lanxiang song-poems in ten pieces—very rich in literary color.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo of Guiyang claimed trysts with the goddess Du Lanxiang, Cao answered with two satirical poems and ten sequels to her songs—all dazzlingly wrought.

sentences.zh: 又著《揚都賦》，亞於庾闡。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Fu on the Yang Capital," second only to Yu Chan.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Yang Capital" ranked just below Yu Chan's celebrated version.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎、鎮軍大將軍從事中郎、下邳太守。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Staff Officer on the Army-General Who Garrisoned the Army, and governor of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through gentleman of the masters of writing, staff officer to the garrisoning general, and governor of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 以名位不至，著《對儒》以自釋。

translations.literal: Because fame and rank did not arrive, he composed "Response to the Ru" to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated at stalled promotion he wrote "Reply to the Scholars" to justify his choices.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：或問曹子曰：「夫寶以含珍為貴，士以藏器為峻，麟以絕跡標奇，松以負霜稱雋，是以蘭生幽澗，玉輝於仞。

translations.literal: Its words said: Someone asked Master Cao, "Treasure is prized for holding gems within; the gentleman is lofty for concealing his vessel; the qilin is marked extraordinary by leaving no tracks; the pine is called surpassing for bearing frost—thus orchids grow in secluded ravines, jade gleams from a thousand-foot cliff.
translations.idiomatic: The piece opens with a question put to Master Cao: "A treasure is valued for the gem it holds; a gentleman is esteemed for the talent he keeps within; the qilin is famed for leaving no trace; the pine is praised for standing through frost. Orchids flourish in hidden streams; jade shines from towering cliffs.

sentences.zh: 故子州浮滄瀾而龍蟠，吳季忽萬乘以解印，虞公潛崇岩以頤神，梁生適南越以保慎，固能全真養和，夷跡洞潤，陵冬揚芳，披雪獨振也。」

translations.literal: Thus Zizhou floated on the blue waves and coiled like a dragon; Wu Jihu suddenly cast off ten thousand chariots and surrendered his seal; Duke Yu hid on lofty cliffs to nourish his spirit; Liang Sheng went to southern Yue to preserve caution—indeed they could preserve the whole and nourish harmony, level their tracks and suffuse with moisture, spread fragrance through winter, and alone flourish amid snow."
translations.idiomatic: Zizhou drifted the blue sea and coiled like a dragon; Wu Jihu abruptly renounced imperial power; Duke Yu withdrew to high cliffs to nourish his spirit; Liang Sheng went south to Yue and kept himself whole. All of them preserved their true selves, lived in quiet obscurity, sent forth fragrance in winter, and flourished alone through snow."

sentences.zh: 今少子睎冥風，弱挺秀容，奇以幼齡，翰披孺童。

translations.literal: Now you, young sir, gaze toward the dark wind, in youth already upright and of fine countenance, extraordinary from tender years, your brush surpassing mere boys.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, young sir, aspire to the reclusive way even in youth—handsome of bearing, precocious in talent, your writing already outshining other lads.

sentences.zh: 吐辭則藻落楊班，抗心則志擬高鴻，味道則理貫莊肆，研妙則穎奪豪鋒。

translations.literal: When you speak, ornament falls before Yang and Ban; when you brace your heart, ambition rivals the high wild goose; when you savor the Way, principle runs through Zhuangzi; when you probe subtlety, keenness seizes the bold edge.
translations.idiomatic: Your words outshine Yang Xiong and Ban Gu; your spirit aspires as high as wild geese in flight; your grasp of the Way matches Zhuangzi; your subtle insight rivals the sharpest masters.

sentences.zh: 固以騰廣莫而萋蒨，排素薄而青蔥者矣，何必以刑禮為己任，申韓為宏通！

translations.literal: Already you soar through the vast void in lush splendor, thrusting aside plain thinness for verdant richness—why must punishments and ritual be your charge, Shen and Han your broad mastery!
translations.idiomatic: You already rise through boundless space in full brilliance, casting off the pale and thin for rich green life—why burden yourself with penal law and ritual, or take Shen Buhai and Han Fei as your grand achievement!

sentences.zh: 既登東觀，染史筆；

translations.literal: You have already ascended the Eastern Pavilion and stained the historian's brush;
translations.idiomatic: You have entered the Eastern Pavilion and taken up the historian's brush;

sentences.zh: 又據太學，理儒功。

translations.literal: again you occupy the Imperial Academy and order Ruist achievement.
translations.idiomatic: and you hold post at the Imperial Academy, managing Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 曾無玄韻淡泊，逸氣虛洞，養采幽翳，晦明蒙籠。

translations.literal: Yet never the dark resonance of quiet detachment, the drifting breath of empty depth, nurturing luster in hidden shade, mingling dark and bright in misted obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you show none of the dark serenity of detachment, the free breath of empty depth, the cultivation of grace in hidden shade, the mingling of light and shadow in misted obscurity.

sentences.zh: 不追林棲之跡，不希抱鱗之龍，不營練真之術，不慕內聽之聰。

translations.literal: You do not pursue the tracks of forest dwelling, do not hope for the dragon embracing scales, do not practice the arts of refining truth, do not admire the inner hearing of keen perception.
translations.idiomatic: You do not follow the path of forest reclusion, do not seek the hidden dragon, do not cultivate arts of refining the true self, do not cherish the inner clarity of deep listening.

sentences.zh: 而處泛位以核物，扇塵教以自濛，負鹽車以顯能，飾一己以求恭。

translations.literal: Instead you occupy a floating post to examine things, fan dusty teaching to cloud yourself, bear the salt cart to display ability, adorn your single self to seek respectability.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you hold an empty office to judge affairs, stir dusty doctrine to blind yourself, bear the salt-laden cart to show off talent, and polish your private self to win approval.

sentences.zh: 退不居漆園之場，出不躡曾城之沖，遊不踐綽約之室，諆不希騄駬之蹤；

translations.literal: In retirement you do not dwell in Zhuangzi's domain, going out you do not tread Zengcheng's heights, in wandering you do not enter rooms of graceful restraint, in planning you do not hope for traces of fine steeds;
translations.idiomatic: In retreat you do not dwell in Zhuangzi's realm; abroad you do not climb immortal heights; in leisure you do not enter chambers of pure refinement; in ambition you do not seek the tracks of noble steeds;

sentences.zh: 徒以區區之懷而整名目之典，覆蕢之量而塞北川之洪，檢名實於俄頃之間，定得失乎一管之鋒。」

translations.literal: you merely use a petty heart to arrange the canons of names and categories, a basket-cover's measure to block the northern river's flood, inspect name and reality in a fleeting moment, and fix gain and loss at the tip of a single brush."
translations.idiomatic: you merely apply a narrow mind to codify names and categories, a cup's measure to dam a northern flood, judge name and reality in an instant, and settle right and wrong at the point of a single brush."

sentences.zh: 子若謂我果是邪？

translations.literal: If you say I am truly right,
translations.idiomatic: If you hold that I am truly in the right,

sentences.zh: 則是不必以合俗。

translations.literal: then one need not conform to custom.
translations.idiomatic: then there is no need to conform to custom.

sentences.zh: 子若云俗果非邪？

translations.literal: If you say custom is truly wrong,
translations.idiomatic: If you say custom is truly wrong,

sentences.zh: 則俗非不可以苟從。

translations.literal: then custom is not something one cannot casually follow.
translations.idiomatic: then custom is not something one may never follow at all.

sentences.zh: 俗我紛以交爭，利害渾而彌重，何異執朽轡以禦逸駟，承勁風以握秋蓬，役恬性以充勞府，對群物以耦怨雙者乎？

translations.literal: Custom and I tangle in mutual strife; gain and harm merge and grow heavier—how is this different from grasping rotten reins to rein in galloping teams, facing strong wind while clutching autumn tumbleweed, pressing tranquil nature to fill the laboring heart, and facing all things as paired resentment doubled?
translations.idiomatic: Custom and self clash in endless dispute; profit and harm blur together and weigh ever heavier—what is this but holding rotten reins against a runaway team, gripping autumn tumbleweed in a gale, forcing a tranquil nature into ceaseless toil, and meeting the world only as doubled resentment?

sentences.zh: 子不聞乎終軍之穎，賈生之才，拔奇山東，玉映漢台，可謂響播六合，聲駭嬰孩，而見毀絳灌之口，身離狼狽之災。

translations.literal: Have you not heard of Zhong Jun's keenness and Jia Yi's talent—raised as marvel east of the mountains, jade reflecting on the Han terrace, one might say their fame resounded through the six directions and their voices startled infants—yet they were slandered by the mouths of Zhou Bo and Guan Ying and personally met the disaster of disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard of Zhong Jun's brilliance and Jia Yi's genius—outstanding talents of Shandong, jade gleaming at the Han court, their fame echoing through the realm and their names startling even children—yet destroyed by the tongues of Zhou Bo and Guan Ying and brought to ruin and disgrace?

sentences.zh: 由此言之，名為實賓，福萌禍胎，朝敷榮華，夕歸塵埃，未若澄虛心于玄圃，廕瑤林于蓬萊，絕世事而雋黃綺，鼓滄川而浪龍鰓者矣。

translations.literal: From this it is said: fame is the guest of reality; fortune sprouts the embryo of disaster; morning spreads glory and splendor, evening returns to dust—better to clarify the empty heart in the dark garden, shelter in jade groves at Penglai, cut off worldly affairs and join Huang and Qi in excellence, and drum the blue river into waves for dragon gills.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see: fame is but the shadow of substance; fortune breeds disaster; glory at dawn turns to dust by dusk. Far better to clear the heart in the mystic garden, rest beneath jade trees on Penglai, leave the world behind like Huang and Qi, and let the blue river surge for the dragon's gills.

sentences.zh: 蒙竊惑焉。」

translations.literal: I am privately puzzled by this."
translations.idiomatic: This is what puzzles me."

sentences.zh: 主人煥耳而笑，欣然而言曰：「夫兩儀既辟，陰陽汗浩，五才迭用，化生紛擾，萬類云云，孰測其兆！

translations.literal: The host, ears brightening, laughed and spoke with pleasure, saying, "When the two principles were already opened, yin and yang flowed vast, the five talents rotated in use, birth and transformation churned in turmoil, the myriad kinds teemed on—who could fathom their signs!
translations.idiomatic: The host laughed with bright delight, then spoke with pleasure: "Once heaven and earth were formed, yin and yang poured forth in vast motion; the five elements succeeded one another; life churned in endless change; the myriad creatures multiplied—who could read their omens!

sentences.zh: 故不登閬風，安以瞻殊目之形？

translations.literal: Thus if one does not ascend Langfeng, how may one behold forms of strange eyes?
translations.idiomatic: Without climbing Mount Langfeng, how can one behold forms beyond ordinary sight?

sentences.zh: 不步景宿，何以觀恢廓之表？

translations.literal: If one does not tread Jingsu, how may one view the broad expanse's surface?
translations.idiomatic: Without walking among the constellations, how can one see the vast reaches of the cosmos?

sentences.zh: 是以迷粗者循一往之智，狷介者守一方之矯，豈知火林之蔚炎柯，冰津之擢陽草！

translations.literal: Thus the crude in confusion follow a single course of wisdom; the narrow and rigid guard one corner's perversity—how could they know the fire forest's lush blazing branches, or ice ford's sprouting yang grass!
translations.idiomatic: The coarse in spirit cling to one fixed wisdom; the rigid guard one narrow orthodoxy—how could they know the blazing branches of the fire forest, or yang grass springing from an icy ford!

sentences.zh: 故大人達觀，任化昏曉，出不極勞，處不巢皓，在儒亦儒，在道亦道，運屈則紆其清暉，時申則散其龍藻，此蓋員動之用舍，非尋常之所寶也。」

translations.literal: Thus the great man sees broadly, entrusting himself to transformation through dusk and dawn; going out he does not exhaust labor, dwelling he does not nest like the white-haired recluse; in Ruism he is Ruist, in the Way he is of the Way; when fortune bends he coils his clear radiance, when the time extends he spreads his dragon ornament—this is the use and release of rounded movement, not what the ordinary prize."
translations.idiomatic: The great man sees far and yields to transformation through night and day; active, he does not exhaust himself; at rest, he does not burrow away like a hermit. Among scholars he is a scholar; among Daoists he is a Daoist. When fortune falters he gathers his clear light; when the time opens he spreads his dragon brilliance. This is the flexible use and release of the rounded way—not the treasure of ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 今三明互照，二氣載宣，玄教夕凝，朗風晨鮮，道以才暢，化隨理全。

translations.literal: Now the three illuminations shine upon one another, the two breaths bear and proclaim; dark teaching congeals at evening, clear wind is fresh at dawn; the Way flows through talent, transformation follows principle to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Now the three lights shine together; yin and yang bear full sway; sacred teaching settles at dusk and clear winds freshen at dawn; the Way advances through talent, and transformation completes through principle.

sentences.zh: 故五典克明於百揆，虞音齊響於五弦，安期解褐于秀林，漁父擺鉤于長川。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Canons are clearly achieved among the hundred duties; Yao's music harmonizes on the five strings; Anqi doffs coarse cloth in the elegant grove; the fisherman casts aside his hook on the long river.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Five Canons govern all affairs; Yao's music sounds on the five strings; Anqi lays aside common dress in a fair grove; the fisherman casts off his hook on the long river.

sentences.zh: 如斯則化無不融，道無不延，風澄於俗，波清於川。

translations.literal: Like this, then transformation has nothing it does not blend, the Way has nothing it does not extend; wind clears over custom, waves clarify upon the stream.
translations.idiomatic: When it is so, transformation leaves nothing unblended and the Way reaches everywhere; winds clear over custom and waves grow calm upon the stream.

sentences.zh: 方將舞黃虯于慶雲，招儀鳳於靈山，流玉醴乎華闥，秀硃草於庭前。

translations.literal: About to dance with yellow hornless dragons amid auspicious clouds, summon the ceremonial phoenix on the spirit mountain, pour jade nectar in the splendid gate, and show vermillion grass flourishing before the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow hornless dragons will dance in auspicious clouds; the ceremonial phoenix will be summoned on the sacred mountain; jade nectar will flow through splendid halls; vermillion grass will flourish before the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 何有違理之患，累真之嫌！

translations.literal: What worry of violating principle, what taint of burdening truth!
translations.idiomatic: What fear then of violating principle, or of staining the true self!

sentences.zh: 子徒知辯其說而未測其源，明朝菌不可逾晦朔，蟪蛄無以觀大年，固非管翰之所述，聊敬對以終篇。」

translations.literal: You merely know to debate the argument yet have not fathomed its source; the morning mushroom cannot cross from new moon to full moon, the summer cicada has no means to behold the great year—this is truly not what brush and pipe would record; I respectfully reply only to close the piece.
translations.idiomatic: You know how to argue the words but have not traced their source. A morning mushroom cannot span from new moon to full; a summer cicada cannot know the great year. This is no matter for petty chroniclers to record—I offer this respectful reply only to close the piece.

sentences.zh: 累遷至光祿勳，卒。

translations.literal: By stages he reached Guangluxun—he died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of the imperial household and died in office.

sentences.zh: 凡所著文筆十五卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: In all what he composed—literary brushings in fifteen fascicles—was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen fascicles of prose and verse circulated after him.

sentences.zh: 李充

translations.literal: Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong

sentences.zh: 李充，字弘度，江夏人。

translations.literal: Li Chong, style Hongdu, was a man of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, courtesy name Hongdu, was a native of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 父矩，江州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ju was Inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Ju governed Jiang province as inspector.

sentences.zh: 充少孤，其父墓中柏樹嘗為盜賊所斫，充手刃之，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chong in youth was orphaned; the cypress trees at his father's tomb were once damaged by robbers—Chong personally killed the robbers with his own hand—by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he tracked down the bandits who had vandalized his father's tomb and slew them with his own blade—news that spread his reputation.

sentences.zh: 善楷書，妙參鐘索，世咸重之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at regular script, subtly referring to Zhong and Suo—the age all prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His regular script rivaled Zhong Yao and Suo Jing—calligraphers everywhere prized his hand.

sentences.zh: 辟丞相王導掾，轉記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as aide to Chancellor Wang Dao and transferred to Recorder Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao brought him onto the chancellor's staff; he then became recorder-adjutant.

sentences.zh: 幼好刑名之學，深抑虛浮之士，嘗著《學箴》，稱：《老子》云：「絕仁棄義，家復孝慈。」

translations.literal: In youth he loved the learning of punishment and names; he deeply suppressed empty floating gentlemen—once he composed "Admonition on Learning," saying: The Laozi says: "Cut off benevolence, discard righteousness, and the family again has filial piety and kindness."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied legalist doctrine and scorned fashionable emptiness; in his "Admonition on Learning" he writes: Laozi says, "Abandon benevolence and discard righteousness, and the household will again know filial piety and kindness."

sentences.zh: 豈仁義之道絕，然後李慈乃生哉？

translations.literal: Could it be that only when the Way of benevolence and righteousness is cut off does filial kindness then arise?
translations.idiomatic: Does filial kindness arise only after benevolence and righteousness have been abolished?

sentences.zh: 蓋患乎情仁義者寡而利仁義者眾也。

translations.literal: It is rather that those who feel benevolence and righteousness are few, while those who profit from benevolence and righteousness are many.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is that few feel benevolence and righteousness in their hearts, while many profit from them.

sentences.zh: 道德喪而仁義彰，仁義彰而名利作，禮教之弊，直在茲也。

translations.literal: When the Way and virtue are lost, benevolence and righteousness are displayed; when benevolence and righteousness are displayed, fame and profit arise—the defect of ritual teaching lies directly in this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way and virtue decline, benevolence and righteousness are proclaimed; when those are proclaimed, fame and profit follow—the flaw of ritual teaching lies here.

sentences.zh: 先王以道德之不行，故以仁義化之，行仁義之不篤，故以禮律檢之；

translations.literal: Former kings, because the Way and virtue did not prevail, therefore used benevolence and righteousness to transform; because practicing benevolence and righteousness was not sincere, therefore used ritual and law to examine;
translations.idiomatic: When the Way and virtue failed to prevail, the ancient kings taught through benevolence and righteousness; when practice grew insincere, they restrained conduct with ritual and law;

sentences.zh: 檢之彌繁，而偽亦愈廣，老莊是乃明無為之益，塞爭欲之門。

translations.literal: the more examination, the broader also hypocrisy—Laozi and Zhuangzi therefore clarified the benefit of non-action and blocked the gate of contentious desire.
translations.idiomatic: yet the more rules multiplied, the wider hypocrisy spread—hence Laozi and Zhuangzi showed the good of non-action and closed the gate of strife and craving.

sentences.zh: 夫極靈智之妙、總會通之和者，莫尚乎聖人。

translations.literal: Now one who reaches the wonder of spiritual intelligence and gathers the harmony of comprehensive penetration—none is loftier than the sage.
translations.idiomatic: None surpasses the sage in reaching the heights of wisdom and gathering the harmony of universal truth.

sentences.zh: 革一代之弘制，垂千載之遺風，則非聖不立。

translations.literal: Reforming a generation's great institutions, handing down a thousand years' legacy-wind—then without the sage it is not established.
translations.idiomatic: Great institutions are not reformed nor enduring customs handed down except through the sage.

sentences.zh: 然則聖人之在世，吐言則為訓辭，蒞事則為物軌，運通則與時隆，理喪則與世弊矣。

translations.literal: Thus when the sage is in the world, uttering words then becomes instructive diction, presiding over affairs then becomes the track of things; when fortune is penetrating he rises with the age, when principle is lost he declines with the world.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage lives among men, his words become teaching and his conduct a model for all things; in prosperous times he rises with the age, and when principle fails he shares the world's decline.

sentences.zh: 是以大為之論以標其旨。

translations.literal: Therefore I greatly compose this discourse to mark its aim.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I set forth this broad argument to make its purpose clear.

sentences.zh: 物必有宗，事必有主，寄責于聖人而遺累乎陳跡也。

translations.literal: Things must have their origin, affairs must have their master—entrust responsibility to the sage and leave the burden upon stale traces.
translations.idiomatic: All things have their root and all affairs their master; fix responsibility on the sage and leave stale forms behind.

sentences.zh: 故化之以絕聖棄智，鎮之以無名之樸。

translations.literal: Therefore transform them by cutting off sagehood and discarding wisdom, stabilize them by the nameless uncarved block.
translations.idiomatic: Thus teach by setting aside false sagehood and cleverness, and steady the age with the nameless uncarved block.

sentences.zh: 聖教救其末，老莊明其本，本末之塗殊而為教一也。

translations.literal: Sage teaching rescues the branch-tips; Laozi and Zhuangzi clarify the root—the paths of root and branch differ, yet as teaching they are one.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian teaching remedies the branches; Laozi and Zhuangzi illuminate the root—the paths differ, yet the teaching is one.

sentences.zh: 人之迷也，其日久矣！

translations.literal: Men's delusion—its days have been long!
translations.idiomatic: Men have wandered in delusion for ages!

sentences.zh: 見形者眾，及道者鮮，不覿千仞之門而遂適物之跡，逐跡逾篤，離本逾遠，遂使華端與薄俗俱興，妙緒與淳風並絕，所以聖人長潛而跡未嘗滅矣。

translations.literal: Those who see form are many, those who reach the Way are few; not beholding the thousand-ren gate yet thereupon adapting to things' traces—chasing traces ever more ardent, departing from the root ever farther—thus causing flowery branch-tips and shallow custom to rise together, subtle threads and pure wind to perish together; therefore the sage long remains hidden yet his traces have never been extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Many see only appearances; few attain the Way.
