Ignoring the lofty gate, they chase outward traces ever more eagerly and drift ever farther from the root—so ornament and vulgarity flourish together while subtle truth and pure custom die together. That is why the sage often withdraws, yet his traces are never lost.

sentences.zh: 懼後進惑其如此，將越禮棄學而希無為之風，見義教之殺而不觀其隆矣，略言所懷，以補其闕。

translations.literal: Fearing that later comers will be deluded in this way, they will overstep ritual and abandon learning to hope for the wind of non-action, seeing righteous teaching as stifling without observing its elevation—I briefly state what I harbor to mend its lack.
translations.idiomatic: Lest later students be misled into casting off ritual and study to chase idle non-action, seeing moral teaching as mere constraint without noting its uplifting power, I briefly set down my thoughts to fill what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 引道家之弘旨，會世教之適當，義之違本，言不流放，庶以祛困蒙之蔽，悟一往之惑乎！

translations.literal: Drawing the broad aim of the Daoist school, meeting the worldly teaching's fitness—meaning not departing from the root, words not flowing unrestrained—perhaps thereby to remove the obstruction of trapped ignorance and awaken the delusion of one-sided going!
translations.idiomatic: I draw on the great aim of Daoism and align it with what worldly teaching requires—keeping meaning true to the root and language from wandering free—in hope of lifting the blinders of confusion and awakening those trapped in one-sided views!

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：芒芒太初，悠悠鴻荒，蚩蚩萬類，與道兼忘。

translations.literal: Its words say: Vast vast primal beginning, far far great wilds, simple simple ten thousand kinds, with the Way together forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: The text runs: In vast primordial chaos, in boundless antiquity, all creatures lived in simple innocence and forgot even the Way.

sentences.zh: 聖跡未顯，賢名不彰，怡此鼓腹，率我倡狂。

translations.literal: Sage traces not yet displayed, worthy names not yet shown—content with this drum-belly, leading us to sing wildly.
translations.idiomatic: No sage's traces yet appeared, no worthy name was known—bellies full, hearts content, all sang in untamed ease.

sentences.zh: 資生既廣，群塗思通，暗實師明，匪予求蒙，遺己濟物而天下為公。

translations.literal: Sustaining life already broad, the many paths thought to penetrate; the dark in truth took the bright as teacher—not I seeking obscurity—forgetting self to aid things and all under heaven was common.
translations.idiomatic: As livelihoods broadened, every path sought mastery; the benighted took the enlightened as teacher—not to seek ignorance, but to forget self, aid others, and make the realm common to all.

sentences.zh: 大庭唱基，義農宏贊，六位元時成，離暉大觀，澤洽雨濡，化流風散，比屋同塵而人罔僭亂。

translations.literal: Great Court sang the foundation, righteous farmers broadly praised; the six positions at the primal time were completed, Li radiance great observation—favor soaking like rain, transformation flowing like wind's dispersal—house by house same dust and men had no usurpation and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Sovereign laid the foundation; the righteous farmers exalted his reign. The six offices were set, the great radiance shone forth; grace soaked like rain, transformation spread like wind, every household shared one dust, and none usurped or rebelled.

sentences.zh: 爰暨中古，哲王胥承，質文代作，禮統迭興，事藉用以繁，化因阻而凝，動非性擾，靜豈神澄！

translations.literal: Then reaching middle antiquity, wise kings all inherited; substance and ornament alternately arose, ritual systems repeatedly rose; affairs relied on use and became complex, transformation because of obstruction became congealed—movement was not nature disturbed, stillness how could spirit be clear!
translations.idiomatic: Then in middle antiquity sage kings succeeded one another; culture and ornament alternated, ritual systems rose in turn. Affairs grew complex through utility, transformation stiffened through obstruction—movement no longer sprang from nature, stillness no longer cleared the spirit!

sentences.zh: 名之攸彰，道之攸廢，乃損所隆，乃崇所替，刑作由於德衰，三辟興乎叔世，既敦既誘，乃矯乃厲。

translations.literal: Where names were displayed, there the Way was abandoned—then reducing what was exalted, then honoring what was replaced; punishments arose from virtue's decline, three penal codes rose in the declining age—both earnest instruction and both correction and severity.
translations.idiomatic: As names were exalted, the Way was cast aside—what had been honored was cut back, what had been discarded was raised up. Punishments arose as virtue waned; three penal codes appeared in a decadent age—through teaching and warning, correction and severity.

sentences.zh: 敦亦既備，矯亦既深，雕琢生文，抑揚成音，群能騁技，眾巧竭心，野無陸馬，山無散林。

translations.literal: Earnest instruction also already complete, correction also already deep—carving and polishing produced ornament, restraint and release made tones; the many talents displayed skill, the crowd of craft exhausted mind; fields had no land-roaming horses, mountains had no scattered groves.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction was complete, correction ran deep—carving produced ornament, modulation shaped music; talents vied in skill, ingenuity exhausted every mind; no horse roamed the plain, no tree stood scattered on the hill.

sentences.zh: 風罔不動，化罔不移，人之失德，反正作奇。

translations.literal: Wind none did not move, transformation none did not shift—men lost virtue, turned from the correct and made the strange.
translations.idiomatic: No wind stirred, no change moved—yet men lost virtue, turned from the straight path, and pursued the bizarre.

sentences.zh: 乃放欲以越禮，不知希競之為病，違彼夷塗而遵此險徑。

translations.literal: Then they released desire to overstep ritual, not knowing that hoping to compete is sickness—violating that level path and following this perilous track.
translations.idiomatic: They indulged desire to breach ritual, never seeing that craving rivalry is a sickness—leaving the level road for this treacherous path.

sentences.zh: 狡兔陵岡，游魚遁川，至賾深妙，大象幽玄，棄餌收罝而責功蹄筌，先統喪歸而寄旨忘言。

translations.literal: Crafty hare mounts the hillock, roaming fish escapes the stream—the utmost subtlety deep and wondrous, the great image dark and abstruse; casting bait and gathering nets yet demanding achievement of hoof and fish-trap, first the lineage lost in return yet entrusting aim to forgetting words.
translations.idiomatic: The crafty hare climbs the hill, the roaming fish flees the stream—the deepest mystery is profound, the great image dark and abstruse. They cast aside bait and nets yet demand results like hoofprints and fish-traps; having lost the original unity, they rest their meaning on wordless teaching.

sentences.zh: 政異征辭，拔本塞源，遁跡永日，尋響窮年，刻意離性而失其自然。

translations.literal: Governance differed and proof-words arose; uprooting the root and blocking the source, hiding traces for endless days, seeking echoes for exhausted years—deliberately departing from nature and losing its spontaneity.
translations.idiomatic: Policies diverged and disputations multiplied—uprooting the source, blocking the spring, hiding away day after day, chasing echoes year after year—forcing nature aside and losing what is spontaneous.

sentences.zh: 世有險夷，運有通圮，損益適時，升降惟理。

translations.literal: The age has peril and ease, fortune has penetration and ruin—increase and decrease fit the time, rising and falling follow principle alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ages bring peril and ease, fortune brings rise and fall—increase and decrease must suit the time, ascent and decline follow reason alone.

sentences.zh: 道不可以一日廢，亦不可以一朝擬，禮不可以千載制，亦不可以當年止。

translations.literal: The Way cannot for one day be abandoned, nor can it in one morning be drafted; ritual cannot for a thousand years be fixed, nor can it in the present year be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The Way may not be abandoned for a single day, nor seized in a single morning; ritual may not be fixed for a thousand years, nor halted in the present year.

sentences.zh: 非仁無以長物，非義無以齊恥，仁義固不可遠，去其害仁義者而己。

translations.literal: Without benevolence there is no means to nurture things, without righteousness there is no means to align shame—benevolence and righteousness truly cannot be kept far; remove only those who harm benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Without benevolence nothing can flourish; without righteousness shame cannot be ordered. Benevolence and righteousness must not be cast away—only remove what harms them.

sentences.zh: 力行猶懼不逮，希企邈以遠矣。

translations.literal: Forceful practice still fears not reaching—hoping to attain the remote is far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Even strenuous effort fears falling short; to hope for the distant ideal is harder still.

sentences.zh: 室有善言，應在千里，況乎行止復禮克己。

translations.literal: When the house has good words, response should be at a thousand li—how much more conduct and stopping returning to ritual and restraining self.
translations.idiomatic: Good words in one's household should resound a thousand leagues away—how much more when conduct and restraint return to ritual and self-mastery.

sentences.zh: 風人司箴，敬貽君子。

translations.literal: The wind-man oversees admonition—respectfully bequeathed to the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The poet charged with admonition respectfully offers this to gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒又引為參軍，充以家貧，苦求外出，裒將許之為縣，試問之，充曰：「窮猿投林，豈暇擇木！」

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou again pulled him in as Army Adjutant; Chong because family was poor bitterly sought to go out—Pou was about to consent to him as county magistrate and tried asking him; Chong said, "A destitute ape casts into forest—how leisure to choose the tree!"
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou of the northern expedition force tried to keep him as adjutant; desperate household finances drove Li to beg a provincial post. When Chu offered a county and asked which he preferred, Li replied, "A hunted ape dives into the forest—there is no leisure to pick the tree!"

sentences.zh: 乃除縣令，遭母憂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed county magistrate—he encountered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Chu named him county magistrate; his mother died soon after.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為大著作郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Chief Gentleman Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he directed the imperial library as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 于時典籍混亂，充刪除煩重，以類相從，分作四部，甚有條貫，秘閣以為永制。

translations.literal: At that time canonical writings were chaotic; Chong deleted annoyance and redundancy, following category to category, dividing into four departments—very orderly—the secret pavilion took it as perpetual regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Court archives were chaos until Li pruned duplicates, grouped texts by subject, and established the four divisions still used in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，卒官。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Palace Secretariat Gentleman—he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of the palace secretariat and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 充注《尚書》及《周易旨》六篇、《釋莊論》上下二篇、詩賦表頌等雜文二百四十首，行於世。

translations.literal: Chong annotated the Documents and six chapters of "Pointers on the Zhou Changes," upper and lower two chapters of "Explaining Zhuangzi," and miscellaneous writings such as poetry, fu, memorials, and eulogies in two hundred forty pieces—circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His corpus includes commentary on the Documents, six essays on the Changes, two treatises on Zhuangzi, and two hundred forty poems, rhapsodies, and state papers.

sentences.zh: 子顒，亦有文義，多所述作，郡舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His son Yong also had literary meaning—many writings—the commandery nominated him filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Yong inherited literary gifts and won nomination as filial and honest.

sentences.zh: 充從兄式，以平隱著稱，善楷隸。

translations.literal: Chong's elder cousin Shi was famed for calm reclusion and was skilled at regular and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Li Shi was noted for quiet integrity and mastery of clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 中興初，仕至侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration he served to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Jin revival he rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 袁宏

translations.literal: Yuan Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong

sentences.zh: 袁宏，字彥伯，侍中猷之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong, style Yanbo, was grandson of Palace Attendant You.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong, courtesy name Yanbo, was grandson of the palace attendant Yuan You.

sentences.zh: 父勖，臨汝令。

translations.literal: His father Xu was magistrate of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Xu governed Linru county.

sentences.zh: 宏有逸才，文章絕美，曾為詠史詩，是其風情所寄。

translations.literal: Hong had roaming talent; his writings were supremely beautiful—once he composed poems chanting history—these were where his mood and feeling lodged.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant and restless, his prose gleamed; his poems on historical themes caught his deepest moods.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，以運租自業。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he took transporting rent grain as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and destitute, he earned his rice ferrying tax grain.

sentences.zh: 謝尚時鎮牛渚，秋夜乘月，率爾與左右微服泛江。

translations.literal: When Xie Shang was garrisoning Niuzhu, on an autumn night riding the moon he casually with attendants in plain clothes floated on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: While Xie Shang commanded Niuzhu he slipped onto the river one moonlit autumn night with a handful of companions in disguise.

sentences.zh: 會宏在舫中諷詠，聲既清會，辭又藻拔，遂駐聽久之，遣問焉。

translations.literal: It happened Hong was in a boat chanting aloud—the voice was both clear and harmonious, phrasing also patterned and outstanding—thereupon [Shang] halted and listened long and sent to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's boat drifted past; his voice rang clear and his lines gleamed—Xie ordered the boat stopped and sent men to learn who sang.

sentences.zh: 答云：「是袁臨汝郎誦詩。」

translations.literal: Reply said: "It is the Young Gentleman of Linru Yuan reciting poetry."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The magistrate of Linru's son is chanting verse."

sentences.zh: 即其詠史之作也。

translations.literal: That is his composition chanting history.
translations.idiomatic: Those were his poems on history.

sentences.zh: 尚傾率有勝致，即迎升舟，與之譚論，申旦不寐，自此名譽日茂。

translations.literal: Shang was unconstrained and had surpassing atmosphere—thereupon he welcomed him to ascend the boat and with him conversed and debated—until dawn without sleeping—from this fame and reputation daily flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by Yuan's spontaneity, Xie invited him aboard and talked until dawn—overnight Yuan's reputation bloomed.

sentences.zh: 尚為安西將軍、豫州刺史，引宏參其軍事。

translations.literal: When Shang was General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yu province he drew Hong to join his military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie became general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yu he named Yuan military adviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷大司馬桓溫府記室。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Recorder of Grand Marshal Huan Wen's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief recorder on Grand Marshal Huan Wen's staff.

sentences.zh: 溫重其文筆，專綜書記。

translations.literal: Wen prized his literary brushings and exclusively supervised correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan prized his pen and gave him sole charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 後為《東征賦》，賦末列稱過江諸名德，而獨不載桓彝。

translations.literal: Later he composed the "Eastern Expedition Fu"; at the fu's end he listed and praised the various famed worthies who crossed the Yangzi—but alone did not record Huan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Eastern Expedition" praised every eminent migrant minister—but omitted Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 時伏滔先在溫府，又與宏善，苦諫之。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Tao was earlier in Wen's headquarters and was also good friends with Hong—he bitterly remonstrated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao, already on Huan's staff and friendly with Yuan, pleaded with him to add Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 宏笑而不答。

translations.literal: Hong smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 溫知之甚忿，而憚宏一時文宗，不欲令人顯問。

translations.literal: When Wen learned it he was very resentful, yet feared Hong as the age's literary patriarch—he did not wish to cause someone openly to question.
translations.idiomatic: Huan seethed yet hesitated to confront the era's literary arbiter openly.

sentences.zh: 後游青山飲歸，命宏同載，眾為之懼。

translations.literal: Later roaming Green Mountain drinking returning, he ordered Hong to ride in the same carriage—the crowd for this feared.
translations.idiomatic: Later, riding home drunk from Green Mountain, Huan insisted Yuan share his carriage—onlookers trembled for him.

sentences.zh: 行數里，問宏云：「聞君作《東征賦》，多稱先賢，何故不及家君？」

translations.literal: Traveling several li he asked Hong saying: "I hear you composed the 'Eastern Expedition Fu,' much praising former worthies—why did you not reach my father?"
translations.idiomatic: After a few miles Huan asked, "Your rhapsody praises every worthy—why omit my father?"

sentences.zh: 宏答曰：「尊公稱謂非下官敢專，既未遑啟，不敢顯之耳。」

translations.literal: Hong replied saying: "Your honored father's title and reference—this lower official does not dare monopolize; since I had not yet leisure to consult, I did not dare display him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan answered, "Addressing so exalted a patronage is not mine to decide lightly—without your instruction I dared not presume."

sentences.zh: 溫疑不實，乃曰：「君欲為何辭？」

translations.literal: Wen doubted it was not true—thereupon said: "What phrasing do you wish to make?"
translations.idiomatic: Unconvinced, Huan snapped, "Supply the line now."

sentences.zh: 宏即答云：「風鑒散朗，或搜或引，身雖可亡，道不可隕，宣城之節，信義為允也。」

translations.literal: Hong immediately replied saying: "Wind mirror scattered bright—sometimes gathering sometimes drawing—though body may perish, the Way cannot fall—integrity of Xuancheng—faith and righteousness as harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan improvised: "Far-sighted and forthright, now recruiting now guiding—life may end yet principle endures; Xuancheng's steadfast honor rings true as justice."

sentences.zh: 溫泫然而止。

translations.literal: Wen wept and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's eyes filled; he said no more.

sentences.zh: 宏賦又不及陶侃，侃子胡奴嘗于曲室抽刃問宏曰：「家君勳跡如此，君賦云何相忽？」

translations.literal: Hong's fu also did not reach Tao Kan; Kan's son Hunu once in a secluded chamber drew blade and asked Hong saying: "My lord father's merit traces are thus—why does your fu so neglect him?"
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsody also snubbed Tao Kan—whose son Hunu cornered Yuan in a side room with a knife: "My father's deeds tower—why erase him?"

sentences.zh: 宏窘急，答曰：「我已盛述尊公，何乃言無？」

translations.literal: Hong embarrassed and hurried replied saying: "I have already greatly narrated your honored father—how then say there is none?"
translations.idiomatic: Flustered, Yuan protested, "I praised him lavishly—how can you say he is missing?"

sentences.zh: 因曰：「精金百汰，在割能斷，功以濟時，職思靜亂，長沙之勳，為史所贊。」

translations.literal: Thereupon said: "Refined gold hundred washings—in cutting able to sever—merit thereby aids the age—office thinks quelling chaos—merit of Changsha—is praised by historians."
translations.idiomatic: He extemporized: "Metal refined through countless heats cuts clean—his service steadied the age and stilled rebellion; historians hymn the Duke of Changsha's feats."

sentences.zh: 胡奴乃止。

translations.literal: Hunu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hunu lowered the blade.

sentences.zh: 後為《三國名臣頌》曰：夫百姓不能自牧，故立君以治之；

translations.literal: Later he composed the 'Panegyric on Eminent Ministers of the Three Kingdoms,' saying: The common people cannot govern themselves, so a ruler is established to govern them;
translations.idiomatic: He later wrote the Panegyric on Eminent Ministers of the Three Kingdoms, which begins: The people cannot govern themselves, and so a ruler is set up to rule them;

sentences.zh: 明君不能獨治，則為臣以佐之。

translations.literal: a bright ruler cannot govern alone, so ministers are appointed to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: a wise ruler cannot rule alone, and ministers are appointed to aid him.

sentences.zh: 然則三五迭隆，歷代承基，揖讓之與干戈，文德之與武功，莫不宗匠陶鈞而群才緝熙，元首經略而股肱肆力。

translations.literal: Thus the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rose in turn, each age inheriting the foundation; whether by abdication or by arms, by civil virtue or martial achievement, none failed to have a master craftsman shape and mold while many talents gathered in splendor, the head planning strategy while arms and legs exerted their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Thus through the ages of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, each dynasty inherited the throne; whether by peaceful succession or by war, by civil culture or martial prowess, a master craftsman always shaped the age while many talents flourished together, the sovereign laying plans and his ministers giving their full strength.

sentences.zh: 雖遭罹不同，跡有優劣，至於體分冥固，道契不墜，風美所扇，訓革千載，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Though their sufferings differed and their tracks had better and worse, as to the substance of their roles being obscurely firm, their accord with the Way not falling, the beauty they fanned abroad, and their teaching reforming a thousand years—their measure was one.
translations.idiomatic: Though their fortunes differed and their records were unequal, in the firmness of their roles, the steadfastness of their bond with the Way, the moral beauty they spread, and the lessons that reformed the ages, their standard was the same.

sentences.zh: 故二八升而唐朝盛，伊呂用而湯武寧，三賢進而小白興，五臣顯而重耳霸。

translations.literal: Hence when the Eight and the Twenty rose, the Tang dynasty flourished; when Yi and Lü were employed, Tang and Wu were pacified; when three worthies advanced, Duke Huan of Qi rose; when five ministers appeared, Duke Wen of Jin became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Eight and the Twenty took office, the house of Tang prospered; when Yi Yin and Lü Shang were used, Tang and Wu knew peace; when three worthies advanced, Duke Huan rose; when five ministers stood forth, Duke Wen of Jin achieved hegemony.

sentences.zh: 中古陵遲，斯道替矣。

translations.literal: In middle antiquity decline set in, and this Way fell away.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle ages the age declined, and this principle was lost.

sentences.zh: 居上者不以至公理物，為下者必以私路期榮，禦員者不以信誠率眾，執方者必以權謀自顯。

translations.literal: Those above did not use utmost fairness to order things; those below were sure to seek glory by private paths; those steering the course did not lead the masses with trust and sincerity; those holding the compass were sure to display themselves through schemes for power.
translations.idiomatic: Those in high place no longer governed all things with perfect fairness; those below sought advancement by private means; those at the helm did not lead the people with sincerity; those who held authority displayed themselves through intrigue.

sentences.zh: 於是君臣離而名教薄，世多亂而時不治，故蘧寧以之卷舒，柳下以之三黜，接輿以之行歌，魯連以之赴海。

translations.literal: Then ruler and minister parted and name-and-teaching grew thin; the age had much disorder and the times were not governed; hence Qu Ning by it drew in and spread out, Liu Xia Hui by it suffered three dismissals, Jie Yu by it went singing, and Lu Zhonglian by it went to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Then lord and minister were estranged and moral teaching grew thin; the age was chaotic and order failed; and so Qu Ning withdrew and returned, Liu Xia Hui was thrice dismissed, Jie Yu went about singing, and Lu Zhonglian threw himself into the sea.

sentences.zh: 衰世之中，保持名節，君臣相體，若合符契，則燕昭、樂毅古之流矣。

translations.literal: In a declining age, to preserve name and integrity, ruler and minister mutually embodying each other as if matching tallies—such were the ancient stream of King Zhao of Yan and Yue Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In a decadent age, to preserve integrity and have ruler and minister embody one another as though joined by a tally—that was the ancient pattern of King Zhao of Yan and Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 夫未遇伯樂，則千載無一驥；

translations.literal: If one has not met a Bo Le, then in a thousand years there is not one swift steed;
translations.idiomatic: Without meeting a Bo Le, a thousand years may pass without a single swift steed;

sentences.zh: 時值龍顏，則當年控三傑，漢之得賢，於斯為貴。

translations.literal: when the time met a dragon countenance, then in that very year three heroes were reined in—the Han's gaining worthies was precious in this respect.
translations.idiomatic: but when the age met a dragon countenance, three heroes were harnessed in a single generation; in this lay the Han's true treasure of worthy men.

sentences.zh: 高祖雖不以道勝禦物，群下得盡其忠；

translations.literal: Though Emperor Gaozu did not overcome things by the Way in ruling, the host below could exhaust their loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Gaozu did not rule by triumph of the Way over things, his followers could give their full loyalty;

sentences.zh: 蕭曹雖不以三代事主，百姓不失其業。

translations.literal: though Xiao and Cao did not serve lords of the Three Dynasties, the common people did not lose their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: and though Xiao He and Cao Shen did not serve lords of the Three Dynasties, the people did not lose their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 靜亂庇人，抑亦其次。

translations.literal: Pacifying disorder and sheltering the people—this too was secondary.
translations.idiomatic: To still chaos and shelter the people was, after all, a lesser matter.

sentences.zh: 夫時方顛沛，則顯不如隱；

translations.literal: When the time was in turmoil, then showing oneself was not as good as hiding;
translations.idiomatic: When the age was in turmoil, to stand forth was inferior to withdrawal;

sentences.zh: 萬物思治，則默不如語。

translations.literal: when all things longed for order, then silence was not as good as speech.
translations.idiomatic: when all things yearned for order, silence was inferior to speaking out.

sentences.zh: 是以古之君子不患弘道難，患遭時難；

translations.literal: Thus the gentlemen of old did not worry that spreading the Way was hard; they worried that meeting the time was hard;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gentlemen of old did not fear that spreading the Way was difficult; they feared that the times were difficult;

sentences.zh: 遭時匪難，遇君難。

translations.literal: if meeting the time was not hard, meeting the ruler was hard.
translations.idiomatic: and if the times were not hard, meeting the right ruler was hard.

sentences.zh: 故有道無時，孟子所以咨嗟；

translations.literal: Hence having the Way but not the time is why Mencius sighed;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Mencius sighed because he had the Way but not the time;

sentences.zh: 有時無君，賈生所以垂泣。

translations.literal: having the time but not the ruler is why Master Jia shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: and Jia Yi wept because he had the time but not the ruler.

sentences.zh: 夫萬歲一期，有生之通塗；

translations.literal: Ten thousand years make one term—the common path of life;
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand years form one span—the common road of life;

sentences.zh: 千載一遇，賢智之嘉會。

translations.literal: a thousand years bring one meeting—the fine assembly of the worthy and wise.
translations.idiomatic: a meeting once in a thousand years—the splendid occasion of the worthy and wise.

sentences.zh: 遇之不能無欣，喪之何能無慨。

translations.literal: To meet it one cannot be without joy; to lose it how can one be without sighing?
translations.idiomatic: To meet such a moment brings joy; to lose it brings sighs—how could it be otherwise?

sentences.zh: 古人之言，信有情哉！

translations.literal: The words of the ancients—truly full of feeling!
translations.idiomatic: The words of the ancients are truly charged with feeling!

sentences.zh: 余以暇日常覽《國志》，考其君臣，比其行事，雖道謝先代，亦異世一時也。

translations.literal: I in my leisure days often perused the Records of the Three Kingdoms, examined its rulers and ministers, and compared their conduct; though the Way fell short of earlier ages, it was still one moment in another age.
translations.idiomatic: In my leisure I often read the Records of the Three Kingdoms, studying its rulers and ministers and comparing their deeds; though their Way fell short of earlier ages, they were nonetheless a moment unto themselves.

sentences.zh: 文若懷獨見之照，而有救世之心，論時則人方塗炭，計能則莫出魏武，故委圖霸朝，豫謀世事。

translations.literal: Wenruo bore the illumination of unique insight and had a heart to save the age; considering the time, men were just in charcoal and paste; reckoning ability, none surpassed Wei Wu—hence he entrusted his plans to the hegemonic court and foresaw affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu possessed the light of singular insight and a heart set on saving the age; the people were in misery, and in ability none surpassed Cao Cao; so he entrusted his designs to the hegemonic court and planned ahead for the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 舉才不以標鑒，故人亡而後顯；

translations.literal: In raising talent he did not use labels and mirrors, so men became illustrious only after death;
translations.idiomatic: He recommended talent without keeping score, so men became famous only after they died;

sentences.zh: 籌畫不以要功，故事至而後定。

translations.literal: in planning he did not demand merit, so affairs were settled only when they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: he planned without demanding credit, so affairs were settled only when they came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 雖亡身明順，識亦高矣。

translations.literal: Though he lost his life in clarifying submission, his discernment was also lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lost his life in making clear his submission, his insight was lofty indeed.

sentences.zh: 董卓之亂，神器遷逼，公達慨然，志在致命。

translations.literal: In Dong Zhuo's rebellion, the sacred vessel was forced to move; Gongda sighed deeply, his aim set on giving his life.
translations.idiomatic: In Dong Zhuo's rebellion, when the imperial regalia was seized, Sima Yi was stirred with resolve to give his life.

sentences.zh: 由斯而譚，故以大存名節。

translations.literal: From this to speak of it, he thereby preserved name and integrity on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, he preserved his integrity on the grandest scale.

sentences.zh: 至如身為漢隸而跡入魏幕，源流趣舍，抑亦文若之謂。

translations.literal: As for being in body a subject of Han while one's tracks entered Wei's tent—the source and flow, inclination and choice—this too may be said of Wenruo.
translations.idiomatic: As for serving in body as a subject of Han while one's path entered Wei's camp—in source, course, and choice, this may also be said of Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 所以存亡殊致，始終不同，將以文若既明且哲，名教有寄乎！

translations.literal: The reason survival and destruction had different ends and beginning and end were not the same must be that Wenruo was both bright and wise, and that name-and-teaching had a lodging in him!
translations.idiomatic: That survival and destruction took different courses and beginnings and ends diverged must be because Xun Yu was bright and wise, and moral teaching found its lodging in him!

sentences.zh: 夫仁義不可不明，時宗舉其致；

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness cannot go unclarified; the age's exemplars raised up their attainment;
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness must be made clear; the age's exemplars displayed their fulfillment;

sentences.zh: 生理不可不全，故達識攝其契。

translations.literal: the principle of life cannot go unfulfilled; hence the far-seeing took up its bond.
translations.idiomatic: the principle of preserving life must be kept whole; hence the far-seeing grasped its inner bond.

sentences.zh: 相與弘道，豈不遠哉！

translations.literal: Together to spread the Way—is it not far-reaching!
translations.idiomatic: Together to spread the Way—was that not a far-reaching aim!

sentences.zh: 崔生高朗，折而不撓，所以策名魏武、執笏霸朝者，蓋以漢主當陽，魏後北面者哉！

translations.literal: Master Cui was lofty and bright, broken yet unbending; the reason he inscribed his name with Wei Wu and held the tablet in the hegemonic court was surely that the Han lord faced the sun and the Wei ruler stood to the north!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan was lofty and bright, broken yet unbending; the reason he took office under Cao Cao and held court at the hegemon's side was surely that the Han sovereign still faced the south while the Wei ruler stood to the north!

sentences.zh: 若乃一旦進璽，君臣易位，則崔生所以不與，魏氏所以不容。

translations.literal: If in a single day the seal were advanced and ruler and minister exchanged places, then that is why Master Cui would not join in and why the house of Wei could not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: But had the imperial seal been offered in a day and ruler and minister changed places, that is why Cui Yan would not have joined in, and why Wei could not tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 夫江湖所以濟舟，亦所以覆舟；

translations.literal: Rivers and lakes can ferry a boat, and can also overturn a boat;
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes can carry a boat, and they can also overturn one;

sentences.zh: 仁義所以全身，亦所以亡身。

translations.literal: benevolence and righteousness can preserve the body, and can also destroy the body.
translations.idiomatic: benevolence and righteousness can preserve the body, and they can also destroy it.

sentences.zh: 然而先賢玉摧于前，來哲攘袂於後，豈天懷發中，而名教束物者乎！

translations.literal: Yet former worthies were jade-shattered before, and later sages rolled up their sleeves after—was it not Heaven's intent issuing from within, and name-and-teaching binding things!
translations.idiomatic: Yet former worthies were shattered like jade before, and later sages rolled up their sleeves after—was this not Heaven's intent welling from within, and moral teaching binding men to their duty!

sentences.zh: 孔明盤桓，俟時而動，遐想管樂，遠明風流，治國以禮，人無怨聲，刑罰不濫，沒有餘泣，雖古之遺愛，何以加茲！

translations.literal: Kongming lingered and turned, waiting for the time to act; he looked far to Guan and Yue and illumined elegance from afar; he governed the state by ritual, men had no sounds of complaint, punishments were not excessive, and at death there were no leftover tears—though the cherished love of antiquity, how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang lingered in seclusion, waiting for the right moment; he looked back to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi and carried their elegance far forward; he governed by ritual, the people murmured no complaint, punishments were not abused, and at death none wept in vain—what ancient beloved minister could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 及其臨終顧托，受遺作相，劉後授之無疑心，武侯受之無懼色，繼體納之無貳情，百姓信之無異辭，君臣之際，良可詠矣！

translations.literal: When at his end he looked back in entrustment, received the testament and became chief minister—the Later Lord entrusted him without doubting heart, the Martial Lord received it without fearful countenance, the heir accepted it without divided feeling, the common people trusted it without differing words; the juncture of ruler and minister—truly fit for song!
translations.idiomatic: At his deathbed he entrusted the realm and became chief minister; Empress Liu entrusted him without doubt, Zhuge Liang received the charge without fear, the heir accepted it without disloyalty, and the people believed without dissent—the bond between ruler and minister is truly worth celebrating in song!

sentences.zh: 公瑾卓爾，逸志不群，總角料主，則素契于伯符；

translations.literal: Gongjin stood out alone, his free ambition unmatched; from boyhood he gauged his lord, and was long in accord with Bofu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu stood apart in excellence, his free spirit unmatched; from youth he judged his lord and was long bound to Sun Ce;

sentences.zh: 晚節曜奇，則三分於赤壁。

translations.literal: in his later years his brilliance was wondrous, and the realm was divided threefold at Red Cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: in his later years his brilliance flared, and at Red Cliffs the realm was divided threefold.

sentences.zh: 惜其齡促，志未可量。

translations.literal: Pity that his years were short; his ambition could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Alas that his years were brief; his ambition cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 子布佐策，致延譽之美，輟哭止哀，有翼戴之功，神情所涉，豈徒謇諤而已哉！

translations.literal: Zibu assisted in planning, achieving the beauty of prolonged praise; he ceased weeping and stopped mourning, and had the merit of winging and upholding; what his spirit and bearing touched—was it only blunt remonstrance!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su aided in planning and won lasting renown; he stopped the mourning and had the merit of supporting the throne; what his spirit and bearing touched went far beyond mere blunt remonstrance!

sentences.zh: 然杜門不用，登壇受譏。

translations.literal: Yet he shut his gates and was not employed, and mounting the altar he received ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was shut behind closed doors and unused, and when he mounted the altar he met with ridicule.

sentences.zh: 夫一人之身所照未異，而用舍之間俄有不同，況沈跡溝壑，遇與不遇者乎！

translations.literal: One man's body—the light it casts is not different, yet between use and rejection there suddenly are differences; how much more for those sunk in ditches and gullies, the met and the unmet!
translations.idiomatic: The same man's light does not change, yet between employment and rejection there may suddenly be a difference—how much more for those sunk in obscurity, the favored and the overlooked!

sentences.zh: 夫詩頌之作，有自來矣。

translations.literal: The making of odes and panegyrics has had its origin from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The writing of odes and panegyrics is an ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 或以吟詠情性，或以紀德顯功，雖大指同歸，所托或乖。

translations.literal: Some use them to chant and sing one's nature and feelings, some to record virtue and display merit; though the great aim returns to one, what they rest upon may differ.
translations.idiomatic: Some sing to give voice to feeling, others record virtue and display merit; though the broad aim is one, what they rest upon may differ.

sentences.zh: 若夫出處有道，名體不滯，風軌德音，為世作範，不可廢也。

translations.literal: As for advancing and withdrawing having a Way, name and substance not stagnating, model conduct and virtuous repute making a pattern for the age—these cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When advancement and withdrawal follow the Way, when name and substance are not fixed in place, when conduct and reputation serve as models for the age—these cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 復綴序所懷，以為之贊曰：火德既微，運纏大過。

translations.literal: Again I string together what I harbor in the preface and make for it a praise, saying: The fire virtue was already faint; fortune was entangled in Great Excess.
translations.idiomatic: I now gather what I expressed in the preface and offer this praise: The fire virtue had waned; fate was wound in Great Excess.

sentences.zh: 洪飆扇海，二溟揚波。

translations.literal: Great gales fanned the sea; the two oceans raised their waves.
translations.idiomatic: Mighty winds lashed the sea; both oceans heaved their waves.

sentences.zh: 虯獸雖驚，風雲未和。

translations.literal: Horned beasts were startled, yet wind and cloud were not yet in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Horned beasts were alarmed, yet wind and cloud had not yet joined in harmony.

sentences.zh: 潛魚擇川，高鳥候柯。

translations.literal: Hidden fish chose their streams; high birds awaited their branches.
translations.idiomatic: Fish in the depths chose their streams; birds on high awaited their branches.

sentences.zh: 赫赫三雄，並回乾軸。

translations.literal: Brilliant, brilliant—the three heroes together turned the axis of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Resplendent, the three heroes together turned the axis of heaven.

sentences.zh: 競收杞梓，爭采松竹。

translations.literal: They vied to gather catalpa and cedar; they strove to pluck pine and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: They raced to gather fine timber; they strove to harvest pine and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 鳳不及棲，龍不暇伏。

translations.literal: The phoenix had no time to perch; the dragon no leisure to crouch.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix had no branch left to perch on; the dragon no moment to lie low.

sentences.zh: 谷無幽蘭，嶺無停菊。

translations.literal: In valleys there was no hidden orchid; on ridges no resting chrysanthemum.
translations.idiomatic: No hidden orchids remained in the valleys; no chrysanthemums lingered on the ridges.

sentences.zh: 英英文若，靈鑒洞照。

translations.literal: Illustrious, illustrious Wenruo—spiritual mirror penetrating in illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Xun Yu—his discerning mirror pierced all things.

sentences.zh: 應變知微，頤奇賞要。

translations.literal: Responding to change he knew the subtle; he nourished the wondrous and prized the essential.
translations.idiomatic: He met change and knew the subtle; he cherished the rare and valued the essential.

sentences.zh: 日月在躬，隱之彌曜。

translations.literal: Sun and moon were in his person; the more he hid, the brighter he shone.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon seemed embodied in him; the more he withdrew, the brighter he shone.

sentences.zh: 文明暎心，贊之愈妙。

translations.literal: Civil brilliance mirrored his heart; the more one praised, the finer it grew.
translations.idiomatic: Civil brilliance lit his heart; the more one praised him, the finer he seemed.

sentences.zh: 滄海橫流，玉石俱碎。

translations.literal: The blue sea flowed crosswise; jade and stone were shattered together.
translations.idiomatic: As the dark sea flowed awry, jade and common stone were shattered alike.

sentences.zh: 達人兼善，廢己存愛。

translations.literal: The accomplished man was doubly good; he set himself aside and preserved love.
translations.idiomatic: The far-seeing man embraced all in goodness; he set himself aside and kept love alive.

sentences.zh: 謀解時紛，功濟宇內。

translations.literal: His plans untied the age's tangles; his merit aided all within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel unraveled the age's turmoil; his merit aided all within the realm.

sentences.zh: 始救生靈，終明風概。

translations.literal: At first he saved the living masses; at the end he clarified wind and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: At first he saved the people; at the end he made his moral bearing clear.

sentences.zh: 公達潛朗，思同蓍蔡。

translations.literal: Gongda was hidden yet bright; his thought matched tortoise and milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was reserved yet luminous; his thought matched the oracle tortoise and milfoil.

sentences.zh: 運用無方，動攝群會。

translations.literal: In deployment he had no fixed method; in movement he gathered all assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed without fixed method; in action he commanded every assembly.

sentences.zh: 爰初發跡，遘此顛沛。

translations.literal: When first he set out on his path, he met this turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When first he rose to prominence, he met this age of turmoil.

sentences.zh: 神情玄定，處之彌泰。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were darkly settled; the more he dwelt in it, the more at peace he was.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit was serenely fixed; the more he faced turmoil, the more at ease he grew.

sentences.zh: 愔愔幕裹，算無不經亹癖通韻，跡不暫停。

translations.literal: Quiet, quiet within the tent-wrap; in calculation nothing went unthreaded, diligently penetrating in resonance, his tracks never briefly halted.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet within the tent, in counsel nothing went unconsidered; diligent and penetrating in design, his course never briefly paused.

sentences.zh: 雖懷尺璧，顧哂連城。

translations.literal: Though he held a foot-long jade disk, he looked back with a smile at cities linked in worth.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held a foot of jade, he smiled at cities worth a thousand.

sentences.zh: 智能極物，愚足全生。

translations.literal: Wisdom can exhaust things; folly is enough to preserve life.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom may master all things; folly is enough to preserve one's life.

sentences.zh: 郎中溫雅，器識純素。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant was mild and elegant; vessel and insight pure and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was mild and refined; his character and insight were pure and plain.

sentences.zh: 貞而不諒，通而能固。

translations.literal: Upright yet not narrow; penetrating yet able to be firm.
translations.idiomatic: Upright yet not rigid; penetrating yet steadfast.

sentences.zh: 恂恂德心，汪汪軌度。

translations.literal: Deferential, deferential in moral heart; vast, vast in model measure.
translations.idiomatic: Deferential in moral heart; vast in standard and measure.

sentences.zh: 仁者必勇，德亦有言。

translations.literal: The benevolent man is sure to be brave; virtue also has its saying.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent are surely brave; virtue too has its word.

sentences.zh: 雖遇履尾，神氣恬然。

translations.literal: Though he met treading the tail, his spirit and bearing were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Though he trod the tiger's tail, his spirit remained serene.

sentences.zh: 行不修飾，名節無愆。

translations.literal: In conduct he did not adorn himself; in name and integrity there was no fault.
translations.idiomatic: He did not adorn his conduct; his integrity knew no fault.

sentences.zh: 操不激切，素風愈鮮。

translations.literal: His bearing was not sharp and urgent; his plain wind grew fresher.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was not harsh; his plain integrity grew ever fresher.

sentences.zh: 邈哉崔生，體正心直。

translations.literal: Remote, Master Cui—substance upright, heart straight.
translations.idiomatic: Far-seeing Cui Yan—upright in body, straight in heart.

sentences.zh: 天骨疏朗，牆岸高嶷。

translations.literal: Heaven's bones were open and bright; his wall-bank was high and steep.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's bone-structure was open and bright; his bearing stood high and steep as a wall.

sentences.zh: 忠存軌跡，義形風色。

translations.literal: Loyalty lodged in his tracks; righteousness took form in his wind and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty lived in his every step; righteousness showed in his bearing and face.

sentences.zh: 思樹芳蘭，翦除荊棘。

translations.literal: He thought to plant fragrant orchids and cut away brambles and thorns.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to plant fragrant orchids and cut away thorns.

sentences.zh: 人惡其上，世不容哲。

translations.literal: Men hated one above them; the age could not tolerate the wise.
translations.idiomatic: Men resented his uprightness; the age could not tolerate the wise.

sentences.zh: 琅琅先生，雅杖名節。

translations.literal: Clear-ringing, the Master—elegantly he leaned on name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-voiced Master Chen—he nobly upheld integrity.

sentences.zh: 雖遇塵務，猶震霜雪。

translations.literal: Though he met dusty affairs, he still quaked like frost and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Though he met the dust of office, he still stood firm as frost and snow.

sentences.zh: 運極道消，碎此明月。

translations.literal: Fortune reached its limit and the Way faded; this bright moon was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune peaked the Way waned; this bright moon was shattered.

sentences.zh: 景山恢誕，韻與道合。

translations.literal: Jingshan was broad and far-reaching; his resonance joined with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui was broad and far-reaching; his tone harmonized with the Way.

sentences.zh: 形器不存，方寸海納。

translations.literal: Form and vessel did not remain; within a square inch the sea was received.
translations.idiomatic: Form and vessel did not confine him; within a square inch he held the sea.

sentences.zh: 和而不同，通而不雜。

translations.literal: Harmonious yet not the same; penetrating yet not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious yet not uniform; penetrating yet not confused.

sentences.zh: 遇醉忘辭，在醒貽答。

translations.literal: Meeting drunkenness he forgot words; when sober he left answers behind.
translations.idiomatic: In drink he forgot fine speech; sober, he left counsel behind.

sentences.zh: 長文通雅，義格終始。

translations.literal: Changwen was penetrating and refined; righteousness framed beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun was penetrating and refined; righteousness shaped his whole course.

sentences.zh: 思戴元首，擬伊同恥。

translations.literal: He thought to uphold the chief; he matched Yi in shared shame.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to uphold the sovereign; he shared Yi Yin's sense of shame.

sentences.zh: 人未知德，懼若在己。

translations.literal: When men did not yet know virtue, his fear was as if in himself.
translations.idiomatic: When others failed to know virtue, he feared as though the fault were his own.

sentences.zh: 嘉謀肆庭，讜言盈耳。

translations.literal: Fine plans filled the court; forthright words filled the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Fine counsel filled the court; forthright words filled the ears.

sentences.zh: 玉生雖麗，光不逾把。

translations.literal: Though jade born is beautiful, its light does not exceed a handful.
translations.idiomatic: Though jade newly born is fair, its light does not pass a hand's breadth.

sentences.zh: 德積雖微，道暎天下。

translations.literal: Though virtue accumulated is slight, the Way illumines all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Though virtue gathered may be slight, the Way illumines all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 邈哉太初，宇量高雅。

translations.literal: Remote, Tai Chu—his universe-measure was lofty and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Far-seeing Xi Zheng—his breadth of mind was lofty and refined.

sentences.zh: 器范自然。

translations.literal: Vessel and model were natural.
translations.idiomatic: His character and model were wholly natural.

sentences.zh: 標準無假。

translations.literal: Standard and rule had no falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: His standard was without pretense.

sentences.zh: 全身由直，跡洿必偽。

translations.literal: Preserving the body comes through uprightness; tracks stained must be false.
translations.idiomatic: Preserving the body comes through uprightness; a stained path must be false.

sentences.zh: 處死匪難，理存則易。

translations.literal: Facing death is not hard; where principle exists it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death is not hard; where principle stands, it is easy.

sentences.zh: 萬物波蕩，孰任其累！

translations.literal: All things billow and surge—who can bear their burden!
translations.idiomatic: All things surge and toss—who can bear their burden!

sentences.zh: 六合徒廣，容身靡寄。

translations.literal: The six directions are only vast; a place for the body has nowhere to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The six directions are vast indeed, yet nowhere could his body find rest.

sentences.zh: 君親自然，匪由名教。

translations.literal: Lord and parent are natural; they are not from name-and-teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and parent are natural bonds, not mere products of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 愛敬既同，情禮兼到。

translations.literal: Love and reverence being alike, feeling and ritual both arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Love and reverence were one; feeling and ritual both were fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 烈烈王生，知死不撓。

translations.literal: Fierce, fierce Master Wang—knowing death, he did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce Wang Xiang—knowing death, he did not bend.

sentences.zh: 求仁不遠，期在忠存。

translations.literal: To seek benevolence is not far; the expectation lies in loyalty preserved.
translations.idiomatic: To seek benevolence is not far; it rests in keeping loyalty alive.

sentences.zh: 玄伯剛簡，大存名體。

translations.literal: Xuanbo was firm and plain; on a great scale he preserved name and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiao was firm and plain; on the grand scale he preserved name and substance.

sentences.zh: 端委獸門，正言彌啟。

translations.literal: With correct robe at the beast gate, upright words ever more opened forth.
translations.idiomatic: Robed in dignity at the court gate, his upright words ever opened wider.

sentences.zh: 臨危致命，盡其心禮。

translations.literal: Facing peril he gave his life; he exhausted his heart's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Facing peril he gave his life, fulfilling his heart's duty to the end.

sentences.zh: 堂堂孔明，基宇宏邈。

translations.literal: Grand, grand Kongming—foundation and structure vast and far.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Zhuge Liang—his foundation and structure were vast and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 器同生靈，獨稟先覺。

translations.literal: His vessel matched living spirits; alone he received prior awakening.
translations.idiomatic: His capacity matched the living masses; alone he received prior awakening.

sentences.zh: 標榜風流，遠明管樂。

translations.literal: He set up elegance as a banner; from afar he illumined Guan and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He held up elegance as his banner; from afar he illumined Guan Zhong and Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 初九龍盤，雅志彌確。

translations.literal: At first the nine dragons coiled; his elegant ambition grew ever more sure.
translations.idiomatic: At first the dragon coiled on the ninth day; his noble ambition grew ever firmer.

sentences.zh: 百六道喪，干戈迭用。

translations.literal: The hundred six ways were lost; shields and spears were used in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred ways were lost; arms were taken up in turn.

sentences.zh: 苟非命世，孰掃雰雺！

translations.literal: If not one fated for the age, who could sweep the murky haze!
translations.idiomatic: If not a man fated for the age, who could sweep away the murky haze!

sentences.zh: 宗子思甯，薄言解控。

translations.literal: The imperial scion thought of peace; in brief words he released control.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei thought of peace; in few words he loosened restraint.

sentences.zh: 釋褐中林，郁為時棟。

translations.literal: Leaving plain cloth in the central grove, he flourished as the age's pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving common dress in the central grove, he flourished as the pillar of the age.

sentences.zh: 士元弘長，雅性內融。

translations.literal: Shiyuan was broad and long; elegant nature inwardly fused.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tong was broad and far-reaching; his refined nature fused within.

sentences.zh: 崇善愛物，觀始知終。

translations.literal: He honored goodness and loved things; viewing the start he knew the end.
translations.idiomatic: He honored goodness and cherished things; seeing the beginning, he knew the end.

sentences.zh: 喪亂備矣。

translations.literal: Disorder and chaos were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Disorder and chaos were complete.

sentences.zh: 勝塗未隆。

translations.literal: The path to victory was not yet raised.
translations.idiomatic: The road to victory was not yet raised.

sentences.zh: 先生標之，振起清風。

translations.literal: The Master marked it out and roused a clear wind.
translations.idiomatic: Master Xu marked the way and roused a clear wind.

sentences.zh: 綢繆哲後，無妄惟時。

translations.literal: He was careful toward the wise successor; without rashness, only with the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful toward the wise heir; without rashness, only as the time required.

sentences.zh: 夙夜匪懈，義在緝熙。

translations.literal: From early night he was not slack; righteousness lay in gathering splendor.
translations.idiomatic: From early to late he did not slacken; his duty lay in gathering splendor.

sentences.zh: 三略既陳，霸業已基。

translations.literal: The three strategies were already set forth; the hegemonic enterprise already had its base.
translations.idiomatic: The three strategies were set forth; the hegemonic enterprise already had its foundation.

sentences.zh: 公琰殖根，不忘中正。

translations.literal: Gongyan planted his root, not forgetting central correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi planted his root, never forgetting central correctness.

sentences.zh: 豈曰模擬，實在雅性。

translations.literal: How could one say it was imitation? It truly lay in elegant nature.
translations.idiomatic: This was no mere imitation; it truly lay in his refined nature.

sentences.zh: 亦既羈勒，負荷時命。

translations.literal: Already bridled and reined, he bore the burden of the age's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Already bridled to office, he bore the burden of the age's mandate.

sentences.zh: 推賢恭己，久而可敬。

translations.literal: He pushed forward the worthy and was respectful to himself; over time he became worthy of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted the worthy and was humble before others; in time he won deep respect.

sentences.zh: 公衡沖達，秉志淵塞。

translations.literal: Gongheng was even and penetrating; he held his aim deep and blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi was even and penetrating; he held his resolve deep and firm.

sentences.zh: 媚茲一人，臨難不惑。

translations.literal: He was gracious to this one man; facing hardship he was not confused.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his sovereign; facing hardship he was not confused.

sentences.zh: 疇昔不造，假翮鄰國。

translations.literal: In former days he did not succeed; he borrowed wings in a neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: In former days he did not succeed; he borrowed wings in a neighboring state.

sentences.zh: 進能徽音，退不失德。

translations.literal: Advancing he could send forth fine repute; withdrawing he did not lose virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing he could send forth fine repute; withdrawing he did not lose virtue.

sentences.zh: 六合紛紜，人心將變。

translations.literal: The six directions were tangled and confused; men's hearts were about to change.
translations.idiomatic: The six directions were in turmoil; men's hearts were about to change.

sentences.zh: 鳥擇高梧，臣須顧眄。

translations.literal: Birds choose high parasol trees; ministers must look back and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Birds choose tall parasol trees; ministers must look about with care.

sentences.zh: 公瑾英達，朗心獨見。

translations.literal: Gongjin was heroic and penetrating; bright of heart, he saw alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu was heroic and penetrating; bright of heart, he saw alone.

sentences.zh: 披草求君，定交一面。

translations.literal: Parting the grass he sought his lord; he fixed friendship in a single meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Parting the grass he sought his lord; he sealed friendship in a single meeting.

sentences.zh: 桓桓魏武，外托霸跡。

translations.literal: Mighty, mighty Wei Wu outwardly relied on hegemonic tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Mighty Cao Cao outwardly relied on the path of hegemony.

sentences.zh: 卓卓若人，曜奇赤壁。

translations.literal: Outstanding, such a man—his wonder blazed at Red Cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding such a man—his wonder blazed at Red Cliffs.

sentences.zh: 三光參分，宇宙暫隔。

translations.literal: The three lights were divided threefold; the universe for a time was parted.
translations.idiomatic: The three luminaries were divided threefold; for a time the universe was parted.

sentences.zh: 子布擅名，遭世方擾。

translations.literal: Zibu monopolized fame; he met an age just in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao won great renown; he met an age still in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 撫翼桑梓，息肩江表。

translations.literal: He soothed wings in his native mulberry land; he rested shoulders beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: He spread his wings in his homeland; he rested his shoulders south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 王略威夷，吳魏同寶。

translations.literal: The king's strategy made might level; Wu and Wei shared the same treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The royal strategy leveled threats; Wu and Wei held a shared treasure.

sentences.zh: 遂贊宏謨，匡此霸道。

translations.literal: Then he praised the great design and rectified this hegemonic Way.
translations.idiomatic: Then he aided the great design and upheld this hegemonic course.

sentences.zh: 桓王之薨，大業未純。

translations.literal: When Lord Huan died, the great enterprise was not yet pure.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce died, the great enterprise was not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 把臂托孤，惟賢與親。

translations.literal: Clasping arms he entrusted the orphan—only the worthy and the kin.
translations.idiomatic: Clasping arms he entrusted the orphan—only the worthy and the kin.

sentences.zh: 轟哭止哀，臨難忘身。

translations.literal: With a great cry he stopped mourning; facing hardship he forgot himself.
translations.idiomatic: With a great cry he stopped the mourning; facing hardship he forgot himself.

sentences.zh: 成此南面，實由老臣。

translations.literal: To accomplish this facing south truly came through the old minister.
translations.idiomatic: To accomplish this facing south truly came through the old minister.

sentences.zh: 才為世生，世亦須才。

translations.literal: Talent is born for the age; the age also needs talent.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is born for the age; the age also needs talent.

sentences.zh: 得而能任，貴在無猜。

translations.literal: To obtain and be able to employ—what is precious lies in being without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: To gain talent and employ it—what matters is freedom from suspicion.

sentences.zh: 昂昂子敬，拔跡草萊。

translations.literal: High-lifting, Zijing—he pulled his tracks from grass and weeds.
translations.idiomatic: Uplifted Lu Su rose from the common fields.

sentences.zh: 荷簷吐奇，乃構雲臺。

translations.literal: Bearing the eaves he spat forth wonder; thus he built the Cloud Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the roofbeam he brought forth wonders; thus he built the Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 子瑜都長，體性純懿。

translations.literal: Ziyu was capital chief; his substance and nature pure and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin was chief of the capital; his character was pure and fine.

sentences.zh: 諫而不犯，正而不毅。

translations.literal: In remonstrance he did not offend; upright yet not harsh.
translations.idiomatic: In remonstrance he gave no offense; upright yet not harsh.

sentences.zh: 將命公庭，退忘私位。

translations.literal: Bearing mandate in the public court, in withdrawal he forgot private position.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing mandate in the public court, in private he forgot personal rank.

sentences.zh: 豈無鶺鴒，固慎名器。

translations.literal: Were there not wagtail birds? He firmly was careful of name and vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Though kin were near as wagtails, he was careful of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 伯言謇謇，以道佐世。

translations.literal: Boyan was blunt and blunt; with the Way he aided the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun was forthright and firm; with the Way he aided the age.

sentences.zh: 出能勤功，入亦獻替。

translations.literal: Going out he could toil in merit; entering he also offered correction.
translations.idiomatic: Going forth he labored in service; returning he offered correction.

sentences.zh: 謀寧社稷，妥紛挫銳。

translations.literal: His plans settled the altars of soil and grain; he soothed tangles and blunted sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: His plans settled the state; he soothed turmoil and blunted sharpness.

sentences.zh: 正以招疑，忠而獲戾。

translations.literal: Uprightness thereby drew suspicion; loyalty yet received offense.
translations.idiomatic: Uprightness drew suspicion; loyalty yet met with blame.

sentences.zh: 元歎邈遠，神和形檢。

translations.literal: Yuantan was remote and far; spirit harmonious, form restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong was remote and far-reaching; harmonious in spirit, restrained in form.

sentences.zh: 如彼白珪，質無塵點。

translations.literal: Like that white jade tablet—substance without a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Like a white jade tablet—his substance bore no speck of dust.

sentences.zh: 立行以恆，匡主以漸。

translations.literal: He established conduct through constancy; he rectified his lord through gradualness.
translations.idiomatic: He established conduct through constancy; he corrected his lord by degrees.

sentences.zh: 清不增潔，濁不加染。

translations.literal: In purity he did not add cleanliness; in turbidity he did not add stain.
translations.idiomatic: In purity he did not grow cleaner; in foulness he took no stain.

sentences.zh: 仲翔高亮，性不和物。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang was lofty and bright; by nature he did not harmonize with things.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi was lofty and bright; by nature he did not blend with the crowd.

sentences.zh: 好是不群，折而不屈。

translations.literal: He loved what was not of the herd; broken yet not bent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved what set him apart; broken yet unbent.

sentences.zh: 屢摧逆鱗，直道受黜。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he crushed the reverse scales; the straight Way received dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he touched the dragon's scales; the straight path brought dismissal.

sentences.zh: 歎過孫陽，放同賈屈。

translations.literal: He sighed passing Sun Yang; released, he was the same as Jia Qu.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed for lack of a Sun Yang; cast aside, he shared Jia Yi's fate.

sentences.zh: 莘莘眾賢，千載一遇。

translations.literal: Numerous, numerous—the host of worthies; a thousand years bring one meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Numerous worthies all—once in a thousand years such a meeting.

sentences.zh: 整轡高衢，驤首天路。

translations.literal: They adjusted reins on the high thoroughfare; they raised heads on heaven's road.
translations.idiomatic: They adjusted reins on the high road; they raised their heads on heaven's path.

sentences.zh: 仰揖玄流，俯弘時務。

translations.literal: Looking up they bowed to the dark stream; looking down they spread the age's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up they bowed to the lofty tradition; looking down they advanced the affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 名節殊塗，雅致同趣。

translations.literal: Name and integrity had different paths; elegant aim shared the same bent.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity took different paths; elegant purpose shared one aim.

sentences.zh: 日月麗天，瞻之不墜。

translations.literal: Sun and moon beautify heaven; gazing upon them, they do not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon adorn the sky; gazing upon them, they do not fall.

sentences.zh: 仁義在躬，用之不匱。

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness were in their persons; using them, they did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness were in their persons; employed, they never failed.

sentences.zh: 尚想遐風，載揖載味。

translations.literal: Still thinking of the far wind, they bow again and savor again.
translations.idiomatic: Still I think of that far wind, bowing again and savoring again.

sentences.zh: 後生擊節，懦夫增氣。

translations.literal: Later generations beat the measure; cowards increase their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations beat the measure; even cowards take heart.

sentences.zh: 從桓溫北征，作《北征賦》，皆其文之高者。

translations.literal: Following Huan Wen on northern expedition he composed the "Northern Expedition Fu"—both are among the heights of his writings.
translations.idiomatic: His northern campaign with Huan Wen produced the "Northern Expedition Rhapsody"—among his loftiest pieces.

sentences.zh: 嘗與王珣、伏滔同在溫坐，溫令滔讀其《北征賦》，至「聞所傳于相傳，雲獲麟於此野，誕靈物以瑞德，奚授體于虞者！

translations.literal: Once together with Wang Xun and Fu Tao they sat in Wen's presence; Wen ordered Tao to read his "Northern Expedition Fu," reaching "I hear what is transmitted from transmission—clouds caught the unicorn in this wilderness—birth spiritual thing by auspicious virtue—why grant body to the Yu ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Xun, Fu Tao, and Yuan joined Huan Wen; Huan had Fu read the "Northern Expedition" aloud until the passage: "Tradition upon tradition tells how the unicorn was taken in this field—the spirit beast appeared as an omen of virtue—why should Heaven lend its form to the house of Yu?

sentences.zh: 疚尼父之洞泣，似實慟而非假。

translations.literal: Affliction for Ni Father's deep weeping—seems truly grief and not false.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius wept from the marrow—it was grief unfeigned, not theater.

sentences.zh: 豈一性之足傷，乃致傷於天下」，其本至此便改韻。

translations.literal: How could one nature suffice for sorrow—thereby causing sorrow in All under Heaven"—its root reaching here then changed rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Not one man's fate alone was mourned—Heaven itself seemed to grieve"; at that turn Yuan shifted rhyme."

sentences.zh: 珣云：「此賦方傳千載，無容率耳。

translations.literal: Xun said: "This fu is about to transmit a thousand ages—it cannot tolerate rashness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun said, "This piece must endure centuries—you cannot shift rhyme carelessly.

sentences.zh: 今於'天下'之後，移韻徙事，然於寫送之致，似為未盡。」

translations.literal: Now after 'All under Heaven,' shifting rhyme and moving topic—yet as to the mood of describing send-off, seems not yet exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Moving the rhyme after 'All under Heaven' breaks the emotional arc—the closure still feels abrupt."

sentences.zh: 滔云：「得益寫韻一句，或為小勝。」

translations.literal: Tao said: "If one obtains benefit by writing one rhyme line—or may be a slight improvement."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao added, "One extra bridging couplet might salvage the transition."

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「卿思益之。」

translations.literal: Wen said: "You think to augment it."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Then improve it."

sentences.zh: 宏應聲答曰：「感不絕于餘心，愬流風而獨寫。」

translations.literal: Hong answering voice replied saying: "Feeling does not cease in my surplus heart—complaining flowing wind and alone writing."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan shot back, "Gratitude lingers in the heart—I chase that lingering breeze and set it down alone."

sentences.zh: 珣誦味久之，謂滔曰：「當今文章之美，故當共推此生。」

translations.literal: Xun chanted and tasted long—said to Tao: "Today's literary beauty—indeed ought jointly to push this youth."
translations.idiomatic: Wang savored the new lines and told Fu Tao, "Among living stylists we must rank him first."

sentences.zh: 性強正亮直，雖被溫禮遇，至於辯論，每不阿屈，故榮任不至。

translations.literal: By nature strong, upright, bright, and straight—although receiving Wen's courteous treatment—as for debate and disputation—often he did not flatter or bend—therefore honored appointment did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright, he never flattered Huan in debate—so he never won high office.

sentences.zh: 與伏滔同在溫府，府中呼為「袁伏」。

translations.literal: Together with Fu Tao in Wen's headquarters—in the headquarters they were called "Yuan-Fu."
translations.idiomatic: Staff paired him with Fu Tao as "Yuan and Fu."

sentences.zh: 宏心恥之，每歎曰：「公之厚恩未優國士，而與滔比肩，何辱之甚。」

translations.literal: Hong in heart was ashamed of it—often sighed saying: "My lord's thick grace has not treated me as country knight—yet together with Tao shoulder to shoulder—how extreme the insult."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan burned with shame: "Huan honors me no higher than a confidant yet pairs me with Fu Tao—insufferable."

sentences.zh: 謝安常賞其機對辯速。

translations.literal: Xie An often prized his alert responses and debate speed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An loved his quick wit in debate.

sentences.zh: 後安為揚州刺史，宏自吏部郎出為東陽郡，乃祖道於冶亭。

translations.literal: Later when An was Inspector of Yang province Hong from Gentleman of the Personnel Bureau went out as Dongyang commandery—thereupon they performed road sacrifice at Smelting Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie An governed Yangzhou, Yuan left the personnel ministry for Dongyang; friends saw him off at the Smelting Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時賢皆集，安欲以卒迫試之，臨別執其手，顧就左右取一扇而授之曰：「聊以贈行。」

translations.literal: Worthy men of the time all gathered; An wished by pressing urgency to test him—at parting grasped his hand—looked to attendants to take a fan and handed it saying: "Briefly to present for journey."
translations.idiomatic: Notables gathered; Xie meant to test Yuan under pressure—at farewell he pressed a fan into Yuan's hand as a parting gift."

sentences.zh: 宏應聲答曰：「輒當奉揚仁風，慰彼黎庶。」

translations.literal: Hong answering voice replied saying: "Then shall uphold and spread humane wind—comfort those black-haired commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan answered instantly, "I shall fan benevolent breeze over the common folk."

sentences.zh: 時人歎其率而能要焉。

translations.literal: People of the time sighed at his spontaneity yet ability to capture essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners marveled that wit so quick could stay apt.

sentences.zh: 宏見漢時傅毅作《顯宗頌》，辭甚典雅，乃作頌九章，頌簡文之德，上之于孝武。

translations.literal: Hong saw that in Han times Fu Yi composed "Eulogy on Manifest Ancestor"—phrasing very canonical elegant—thereupon he composed eulogies in nine chapters praising Jianwen's virtue—presented them to Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling Fu Yi's stately "Hymn for Emperor Ming," Yuan composed nine chapters honoring Emperor Jianwen and presented them to Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 太元初，卒于東陽，時年四十九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyuan he died in Dongyang—at that time age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Dongyang early in Taiyuan, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 撰《後漢紀》三十卷及《竹林名士傳》三卷、詩賦誄表等雜文凡三百首，傳於世。

translations.literal: He compiled thirty fascicles of "Annals of Later Han" and three fascicles of "Traditions of Bamboo Grove Famous Men"—poetry, fu, dirges, memorials and other miscellaneous writings in all three hundred pieces—transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left thirty rolls of Later Han annals, three of Bamboo Grove worthies, and three hundred assorted poems, rhapsodies, and state papers.

sentences.zh: 三子：長超子，次成子，次明子。

translations.literal: Three sons: eldest Chaozi, next Chengzi, next Mingzi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yuan Chaozi, Yuan Chengzi, and Yuan Mingzi.

sentences.zh: 明子有父風，最知名，官至臨賀太守。

translations.literal: Mingzi had father's air—most famed—office reached governor of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mingzi alone matched his father's fame, rising to governor of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 伏滔

translations.literal: Fu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao

sentences.zh: 伏滔，字玄度，平昌安丘人也。

translations.literal: Fu Tao, style Xuandu, was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao, courtesy name Xuandu, came from Anqiu in Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 有才學，少知名。

translations.literal: He had talent and learning—in youth was known.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and learned, he won notice while young.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，辟別駕，皆不就。

translations.literal: The province nominated him cultivated talent; he was summoned as adjunct commander—both times he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The province ranked him as elite scholar and summoned him as adjunct administrator—he declined both offers.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫引為參軍，深加禮接，每宴集之所，必命滔同遊。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen drew him in as Army Adjutant and deeply added courteous reception—wherever feasts gathered he always ordered Tao to roam together.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen named him adjutant and showered him with favor—every banquet required Fu Tao at his side.

sentences.zh: 從溫伐袁真，至壽陽，以淮南屢叛，著論二篇，名曰《正淮》。

translations.literal: Following Wen he campaigned against Yuan Zhen; arriving at Shouyang—because Huainan repeatedly rebelled—he composed two treatises titled "Correcting Huainan."
translations.idiomatic: During the expedition against Yuan Zhen he penned two essays called "Setting Huainan Right" after repeated rebellion south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 其上篇曰：淮南者，三代揚州之分也。

translations.literal: Its upper chapter says: Huainan is the allotment of Yangzhou in the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The upper essay begins: the Huainan region was the Yangzhou domain of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 當春秋時，吳、楚、陳、蔡之與地。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period, it was territory shared with Wu, Chu, Chen, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Spring and Autumn era it lay among the lands of Wu, Chu, Chen, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 戰國之末，楚全有之，而考烈王都焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Warring States, Chu wholly possessed it, and King Kaolie made it his capital there.
translations.idiomatic: By the close of the Warring States Chu held it entirely, and King Kaolie established his capital there.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，建立郡縣，是為九江。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, established commanderies and counties, and this became Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin unified the empire and instituted the commandery-county system, the area became Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉項之際，號曰東楚。

translations.literal: In the age of Liu and Xiang, it was called Eastern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the struggle between the Liu and Xiang houses it was known as Eastern Chu.

sentences.zh: 爰自戰國至於晉之中興，六百有餘年，保淮南者九姓，稱兵者十一人，皆亡不旋踵，禍溢於世，而終莫戒焉。

translations.literal: From the Warring States down to the restoration of Jin, more than six hundred years—nine houses held Huainan, eleven men raised arms; all perished without turning heel, calamity overflowed the age, and in the end none took warning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Warring States through the Jin restoration, a span of more than six centuries, nine lineages held the Huainan region and eleven men took up arms; every one perished almost at once, disaster spread through the age, and still no one heeded the lesson.

sentences.zh: 其天時歟，地勢歟，人事歟？

translations.literal: Was it celestial timing, terrain and momentum, or human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Was the cause celestial timing, geographical advantage, or human conduct?

sentences.zh: 何喪亂之若是也！

translations.literal: Why was disorder and ruin thus!
translations.idiomatic: Why has turmoil been so relentless!

sentences.zh: 試商較而論之。

translations.literal: Let us compare and weigh the matter and discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Let us weigh the evidence and examine the question.

sentences.zh: 夫懸象著明，而休征表於列宿；

translations.literal: Heaven's suspended images are made manifest, and auspicious signs appear among the constellations;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven displays its signs clearly, and favorable or ominous portents appear among the stars;

sentences.zh: 山河衿帶，而地險彰於丘陵；

translations.literal: rivers and mountains form collar and belt, and the land's peril is shown in hills and mounds;
translations.idiomatic: rivers and mountains gird the land like collar and sash, and strategic danger is revealed in its hills;

sentences.zh: 治亂推移，而興亡見於人事。

translations.literal: order and disorder shift in turn, and rise and fall are seen in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: order and chaos alternate, and the rise and fall of states are disclosed in human affairs.

sentences.zh: 由此而觀，則兼也必矣。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, then all three together is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, all three factors must operate together.

sentences.zh: 昔妖星出於東南而弱楚以亡，飛孛橫於天漢而劉安誅絕，近則火星晨見而王淩首謀，長彗宵暎而毋丘襲亂。

translations.literal: Formerly a demon star appeared in the southeast and weak Chu thereby perished; a flying comet stretched across the Heavenly River and Liu An was executed to extinction; recently Mars appeared at dawn and Wang Ling first plotted rebellion; a long comet shone through the night and Guanqiu Jian launched disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a baleful star rose in the southeast and enfeebled Chu was destroyed; a comet swept across the Milky Way and Liu An was put to death with his house; in recent times Mars appeared at dawn as Wang Ling first conspired, and a long comet blazed by night when Guanqiu Jian rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 斯則表乎天時也。

translations.literal: This then is displayed in celestial timing.
translations.idiomatic: These are manifestations of Heaven's timing.

sentences.zh: 彼壽陽者，南引荊汝之利，東連三吳之富；

translations.literal: That Shouyang—southward draws the profit of Jing and Ru; eastward links the wealth of the Three Wu regions;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang draws southern profit from the Jing and Ru corridor and eastern wealth from the Three Wu lands;

sentences.zh: 北接梁宋，平塗不過七日；

translations.literal: northward adjoins Liang and Song, and level roads require no more than seven days;
translations.idiomatic: to the north it meets Liang and Song, reachable over level roads in no more than seven days;

sentences.zh: 西援陳許，水陸不出千里；

translations.literal: westward supports Chen and Xu, and by water or land it is not beyond a thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: to the west it links Chen and Xu, within a thousand li by river or road;

sentences.zh: 外有江湖之阻，內保淮肥之固。

translations.literal: outside it has the barrier of rivers and lakes; inside it preserves the solidity of the Huai and Fei.
translations.idiomatic: rivers and lakes guard it without, while the Huai and Fei basins secure it within.

sentences.zh: 龍泉之陂，良疇萬頃，舒六之貢，利盡蠻越，金石皮革之具萃焉，苞木箭竹之族生焉，山湖藪澤之隈，水旱之所不害，土產草滋之實，荒年之所取給。
