translations.literal: The Longquan reservoir, fine fields by the myriad mu; tribute from Shu and Liu, profit extending to the Man and Yue; implements of metal, stone, leather, and hide gather there; clans of wrapped timber and arrow bamboo grow there; recesses of mountains, lakes, marshes, and swamps where flood and drought do not harm; native products and nourishing grasses and fruits, supplies drawn upon in lean years.
translations.idiomatic: The Longquan reservoir and ten thousand mu of fertile fields; tribute from Shu and Liu channels profit as far as the southern barbarian lands; metal, stone, leather, and harness are gathered there, and timber and arrow bamboo abound; in the sheltered margins of hills, lakes, and marshes drought and flood do little harm, while native grains, herbs, and fruits sustain the people in years of famine.

sentences.zh: 此則系乎地利乎也。

translations.literal: This then is tied to geographical advantage.
translations.idiomatic: This, then, depends on geographical advantage.

sentences.zh: 其俗尚氣力而多勇悍，其人習戰爭而貴詐偽，豪右並兼之門，十室而七；

translations.literal: Its customs honor physical force and produce many fierce and bold men; its people are practiced in warfare and prize deceit and falsehood; among powerful houses that annex and merge, seven in ten dwellings;
translations.idiomatic: Local custom esteems brute strength and breeds fierce warriors; the people are seasoned in war and prize cunning stratagem; in seven of every ten households powerful families annex their neighbors;

sentences.zh: 藏甲挾劍之家，比屋而發。

translations.literal: houses that store armor and carry swords rise house by house.
translations.idiomatic: homes that hoard armor and bear swords appear in nearly every dwelling.

sentences.zh: 然而仁義之化不漸，刑法之令不及，所以屢多亡國也。

translations.literal: Yet the transforming influence of benevolence and righteousness does not gradually reach them, and the commands of penal law do not extend to them—therefore states here have repeatedly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the civilizing force of benevolence and righteousness never takes root, and penal statutes never reach them—hence the repeated ruin of states in this region.

sentences.zh: 昔考烈以衰弱之楚屢遷其都，外迫強秦之威，內遘陽申之禍，逃死劫殺，三世而滅。

translations.literal: Formerly Kaolie, with a weakened Chu, repeatedly moved his capital; outwardly pressed by mighty Qin's might, inwardly meeting Lord Yang Shen's calamity; fleeing death and suffering robbery and murder, in three generations it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: King Kaolie of a declining Chu moved his capital again and again, threatened without by Qin's power and torn within by the disaster of Lord Chunshen; amid flight, slaughter, and plunder, his line was extinguished in three generations.

sentences.zh: 黥布以三雄之選，功成垓下，淮陰既囚，梁越受戮，嫌結震主之威，慮生同體之禍，遂謀圖全之計，庶幾後亡之福，眾潰于一戰，身脂於漢斧。

translations.literal: Ying Bu, chosen among the three heroes, achieved merit at Gaixia; once Huaiyin was imprisoned and Liang and Yue were executed, suspicion formed over the awe of a ruler who trembled before his subjects, fear arose of the calamity of shared flesh and blood; then he plotted a plan to preserve himself whole, hoping perhaps for the fortune of dying later—his host collapsed in one battle, and his body greased the Han axe.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Bu, one of the three great champions, had won glory at Gaixia; after Han Xin was imprisoned and Peng Yue of Liang was executed, he brooded on the peril of a lord who fears his own ministers and on the doom that visits those of one flesh and blood; he devised a scheme to save himself and delay his end, but his army broke in a single battle and he was cut down by Han axes.

sentences.zh: 劉長支庶，奄王大國，承喪亂之餘，禦新化之俗，無德而寵，欲極禍發。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, a collateral branch, suddenly ruled a great state; inheriting the aftermath of disorder and tumult, facing a newly transformed custom—without virtue yet favored, desire reached its limit and disaster erupted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, a cadet of the imperial house, suddenly held a great kingdom; inheriting a realm still raw from chaos and confronting a newly imposed order, he enjoyed favor without virtue until desire ran to excess and ruin broke out.

sentences.zh: 王安內懷先父之憾，外眩奸臣之說，招引賓客，沈溺數術，藉二世之資，恃戈甲之盛，屈強江淮之上，西向而圖宗國，言未絕口，身嗣俱滅。

translations.literal: Liu An inwardly harbored his late father's grievance, outwardly dazzled by treacherous ministers' persuasions; he drew in guests and retainers, drowned himself in numerology and occult arts, relied on the resources of two generations, trusted in the abundance of weapons and armor, bent force upon the Yangzi and Huai, turned westward and plotted against the imperial house—his words had not ceased when body and heir alike were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu An nursed his father's old resentment within while beguiled without by crafty advisers; he gathered retainers, immersed himself in numerology and occult arts, drew on the wealth of two reigns, and trusted in vast stores of arms; flexing power along the Yangzi and Huai, he turned west to strike at the imperial domain—and before his design was fully spoken, he and his line were annihilated.

sentences.zh: 李憲因亡新之余，袁術當衰漢之末，負力幸亂，遂生僭逆之計，建號九江，稱制下邑，狼狽奔亡，傾城受戮。

translations.literal: Li Xian rode the remnant of the fallen Xin; Yuan Shu stood at the end of a declining Han; relying on force and trusting disorder, they then produced plans of usurpation and treason, established a title in Jiujiang, and declared rule over lesser towns; in frantic flight and ruin the whole city suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian seized on the wreckage of Wang Mang's Xin dynasty; Yuan Shu rose as Han declined; trusting in brute force and welcoming chaos, they hatched treasonous designs, proclaimed a reign in Jiujiang, and asserted rule over subordinate towns—only to flee in disgrace and see their cities leveled and their people slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 及至彥雲、仲恭、公休之徒，或憑宿名，或怙前功，握兵淮楚，力制東夏，屬當多難之世，仍值廢興之會，謀非所議，相系禍敗。

translations.literal: Down to the likes of Yan Yun, Zhong Gong, and Gong Xiu—some relying on long-standing fame, some presuming on former merit—they grasped armies in Huai and Chu, by force controlled eastern Xia; just when the age was full of hardship, they still met the turning point of ruin and revival; their plots were not what should have been deliberated, and disaster and defeat followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Zhuge Dan, and men of their kind—some trading on old renown, others on past service—who seized armies in the Huai-Chu region and dominated the eastern heartland; in an age already racked by hardship, at the very juncture of dynastic rise and fall, they pursued reckless designs and brought ruin upon one another in succession.

sentences.zh: 祖約助逆，身亡家族。

translations.literal: Zu Yue aided rebellion; his person perished and his clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue abetted rebellion and lost both his life and his entire family.

sentences.zh: 彼十亂者，成乎人事者也。

translations.literal: Those ten disorders were accomplished through human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those ten rebellions were the work of human conduct.

sentences.zh: 然則侵弱昏迷，以至絕滅，亡楚當之。

translations.literal: Thus then invasion, weakening, and delusion leading to utter extinction—declining Chu bore this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus enfeeblement, confusion, and final extinction fell, as they had upon dying Chu.

sentences.zh: 恃強畏逼，遂謀叛亂，黥布有焉。

translations.literal: Trusting in strength yet fearing pressure, then plotting rebellion and disorder—Ying Bu was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on power yet dreading coercion, then turning to rebellion—such was Ying Bu.

sentences.zh: 二王遘逆，寵之之過也。

translations.literal: The two kings encountering treason—this was excess in favor shown them.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes who turned traitor did so because favor had been heaped upon them beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 公路僭偽，乘釁之盜也。

translations.literal: Gonglu's usurpation and false rule was a bandit who seized an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, styled Gonglu, was a usurper who preyed on opportunity.

sentences.zh: 二將以圖功首難，士少以驕矜樂禍。

translations.literal: Two generals, seeking merit, were first to raise difficulty; lesser officers, through arrogance, delighted in calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Two generals courted merit by stirring trouble first; lesser commanders, proud and reckless, welcomed disaster.

sentences.zh: 本其所因，考其成跡，皆寵盛禍淫，福過災生，而制之不漸，積之有由也。

translations.literal: Tracing what they relied upon and examining the tracks of their accomplishment, all were favor overflowing and disaster following excess, fortune passing its measure and calamity arising—and control was not gradual; accumulation had its causes.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing their origins and reviewing the record of their deeds, each case shows favor run to excess and disaster bred by overweening fortune; blessings outran their measure and ruin followed, because restraint was never applied gradually and the seeds had long been sown.

sentences.zh: 其下篇曰：昔高祖之誅黥布也，撮三策之要，馳赦過之書，乘人主之威以除逆節之虜，然猶決戰陳都，暴屍橫野，僅乃克之，害亦深矣！

translations.literal: Its lower chapter says: Formerly, when Gaozu executed Ying Bu, he gathered the essentials of three stratagems, dispatched edicts pardoning past offenses, and rode the sovereign's majesty to remove a rebel of deviant integrity—yet still he fought a decisive battle at the Chen capital, corpses were exposed and strewn across the wilds, and only then was victory achieved; the harm was also deep indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The lower essay begins: when Gaozu moved against Ying Bu, he distilled the essentials of three plans, issued amnesties for past crimes, and wielded imperial authority to crush a rebellious foe—yet still he had to fight a decisive battle at the Chen capital, leaving corpses heaped across the plain before victory came; the cost was grievous indeed.

sentences.zh: 長安之謀，雖兵未交于山東，禍未遍於天下，而馳說之士與闔境之人幽囚誅放者，亦已眾矣。

translations.literal: The Chang'an conspiracy—though troops had not yet clashed east of the mountains and disaster had not yet spread across the realm, envoys and persuaders together with people throughout the borders who were imprisoned, executed, or exiled were already numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Wang Ling's conspiracy, though armies had not yet met east of the mountains and calamity had not engulfed the empire, the persuaders who were sent forth and the people throughout the region who were imprisoned, executed, or banished were already legion.

sentences.zh: 光武連兵于肥舒，魏祖馳馬於蘄苦，而廬九之間流溺兵凶者十而七八焉。

translations.literal: Guangwu linked armies at Fei and Shu; the Wei founder galloped horses at Qi and Ku; yet between Lu and Jiu those swept away, drowned, or harmed by soldiery were seven or eight in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu campaigned repeatedly in Fei and Shu; Cao Cao drove his armies through Qi and Ku; yet between Lujiang and Jiujiang seven or eight of every ten people were drowned, displaced, or destroyed by war.

sentences.zh: 夫王淩面縛，得之于砎石；

translations.literal: Wang Ling bound his own face and was obtained at Fancheng;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling came forward with bound face and was taken at Fancheng;

sentences.zh: 仲恭接刃，成之於後覺也。

translations.literal: Zhong Gong met the blade, and accomplishment came only through belated awareness.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian met the sword, and success came only after rulers awakened too late.

sentences.zh: 而高祖以之宵征，世宗以之發疾，豈不勤哉！

translations.literal: Yet Gaozu for this made night campaigns; Shizong for this fell ill—were they not diligent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozu marched through the night for such ends, and Emperor Wu fell ill from such exertions—were they not tireless!

sentences.zh: 文皇挾萬乘之威，杖伊周之權，內舉京畿之眾，外征四海之銳，雲合雨集，推鋒以臨淮浦，而誕欽晏然，方嬰城自固，憑軾以觀王師。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen wielded the majesty of ten thousand chariots, leaned on the authority of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; inwardly he raised the masses of the capital region, outwardly he summoned the sharp elite of the four seas; clouds gathered and rain converged as he drove his vanguard to the Huai shore—yet Dan and Qin were at ease, just then closing the city to hold firm, leaning on the chariot rail to observe the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen deployed the might of an empire and exercised power like Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou; he mobilized the armies of the capital districts within and the finest troops of the realm without; forces massed like clouds and rain as he pressed the front to the Huai bank—yet Zhuge Dan and Wen Qin remained unruffled, sealing the city and holding fast, leaning on their chariot rails to watch the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 於是築長圍，起棼櫓，高壁連塹，負戈擊柝以守之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they built a long encirclement, raised tangled siege towers, high walls linked with ditches, and bearing weapons and striking watch-clappers they defended it.
translations.idiomatic: Then the besiegers raised a long encirclement, erected siege towers, linked high walls with trenches, and settled in behind arms and watch-drums to hold the lines.

sentences.zh: 自夏及春，而後始知亡焉。

translations.literal: From summer until spring, only afterward did they know destruction.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through spring the siege dragged on before they at last met their ruin.

sentences.zh: 然則屠城之禍，其可極言乎？

translations.literal: Thus then the calamity of slaughtering cities—can it be fully told?
translations.idiomatic: As for the horror of cities put to the sword, can it even be fully described?

sentences.zh: 約之出奔，淮左為墟，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yue's flight into exile—the left bank of the Huai became ruins; alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue fled, the country east of the Huai was reduced to wasteland—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 信哉魯哀之言，夫生乎深宮，長於膏梁，憂懼不切於身，榮辱不交於前，則其仁義之本淺矣。

translations.literal: Trustworthy indeed are Duke Ai of Lu's words: one born in the deep palace, reared amid fine grain and meat—if worry and fear do not cut close to the person, if honor and disgrace do not meet one face to face, then the root of benevolence and righteousness is shallow.
translations.idiomatic: How true were Duke Ai of Lu's words: born deep within the palace and reared on the finest fare, if worry never touches one's person and honor and shame never stand before one's eyes, the roots of benevolence and righteousness must remain shallow.

sentences.zh: 奉以南面之尊，藉以列城之富，宅以制險之居，養以眾強之盛，而無德以臨之，無制以節之，則厭溢樂禍之心生矣。

translations.literal: Given the honor of facing south, lent the wealth of many cities, dwelling in a residence that commands strategic peril, nourished by the abundance of numerous strength—yet without virtue to oversee it, without regulation to restrain it—then a heart sated to overflow and delighting in calamity is born.
translations.idiomatic: Invested with the throne, endowed with wealthy cities, lodged in a fortress of strategic advantage, and sustained by vast armed strength—yet without virtue to govern and without restraint to curb excess—the mind grows surfeited and begins to relish disaster.

sentences.zh: 夫以昏主禦奸臣，利甲資堅城，偽令行于封內，邪惠結于人心，乘間幸濟之說日交於側，猾詐錮咎之群各馳於前，見利如歸，安在其不為亂乎！

translations.literal: For a benighted lord to face treacherous ministers, sharp armor supplied by stout walls, false commands running within the fief, wicked favors binding people's hearts—plots that seize openings and hope for success daily meet at one's side; crafty, deceitful bands that lock in blame each race forward; seeing profit they return like homing—how could disorder not arise!
translations.idiomatic: When a dim ruler confronts crafty ministers, when sharp weapons and stout walls become assets, when false decrees rule within the domain and corrupt favors win men's hearts, when daily counsel urges seizing every chance, when deceitful factions press forward, and when men rush toward profit as toward home—how could rebellion not follow!

sentences.zh: 況乘舊寵，挾前功，畏逼懼亡，以謀圖身之舉者，望其俯首就羈，不亦迂哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, for one who rides old favor, clutches former merit, fears pressure and dreads ruin, and undertakes a plot to preserve himself— to expect that he will bow his head and accept bonds, is that not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: And for men who trade on past favor, brandish old achievements, dread coercion, fear destruction, and scheme for their own survival—to expect them meekly to submit is surely naive.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「履霜堅冰，馴致之道，」蓋言漸也。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Treading frost, solid ice"—the way of gradual arrival—this speaks of gradualness.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Frost underfoot means solid ice to come"—the path of gradual development; it is speaking of slow accumulation.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 斯所以亂臣賊子亡國覆家累世而不絕者歟！

translations.literal: This then is why rebellious ministers and wicked sons destroy states and overturn houses, generation after generation without cease!
translations.idiomatic: This is why traitorous ministers and rebellious sons bring down states and ruin families age after age without end!

sentences.zh: 昔先生之宰天下也，選於有德，訪之三吏，正其分位元，明其等級，畫之封疆，宣之政令，上下有序，無僭差之嫌，四人安業，無並兼之國。

translations.literal: Formerly when the sage-kings governed the realm, they selected the virtuous, consulted the three administrators, rectified allotted positions and primary rank, clarified grades and levels, demarcated borders and frontiers, proclaimed policies and commands; high and low had order, without suspicion of overstepping; the four peoples pursued their occupations in peace, and there were no states of annexation and merger.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the sage rulers governed the realm, they chose the virtuous, sought counsel from the chief officers, fixed ranks and stations, defined grades, drew borders, and proclaimed laws; superior and inferior kept their order without trespass; the people in all quarters pursued their callings in peace, and no lord annexed another's domain.

sentences.zh: 三載考陟，功罪不得逃其跡，九伐時修，刑賞無所謬其實。

translations.literal: Every three years they examined promotion; merit and guilt could not escape their tracks; the nine punitive expeditions were timely maintained; punishments and rewards nowhere missed their true measure.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they reviewed appointments, so merit and guilt left a clear record; the nine punitive campaigns were kept in due repair, and rewards and punishments never missed their mark.

sentences.zh: 令之有漸，軌之有度，寵之有節，權不外授，威不下黷，所以杜其萌際，重其名器，深根固本，傳之百世。

translations.literal: Commands had gradualness, tracks had measure, favor had moderation; authority was not granted outside, majesty was not debased below—thereby to block the first sprouting, to honor titles and regalia, to root deeply and secure the foundation, and to transmit it for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Laws advanced step by step, conduct had its proper bounds, and favor knew its limits; power was not delegated rashly, nor was authority cheapened; thus the first signs of disorder were cut off, titles and honors were held in esteem, foundations were sunk deep and made firm, and the state could be handed down for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 雖時有盛衰，弱者無所懼其亡；

translations.literal: Though times had flourishing and decline, the weak had nothing by which to fear their extinction;
translations.idiomatic: Though fortunes rose and fell, the weak need not fear extinction;

sentences.zh: 道有興廢，強者不得資其弊。

translations.literal: the Way had rise and abandonment, and the strong could not rely on such weakness for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: and though the Way itself might wax or wane, the strong could not exploit disorder for private gain.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，將使天下從風，穆然軌道，慶自一人，惠流萬國，安有向時之患哉！

translations.literal: If it were thus, it would make the realm follow like the wind, solemnly keep to the proper track, felicity arise from one man, grace flow to ten thousand states—how could there be the troubles of former times!
translations.idiomatic: Were it so, the empire would follow as if on the wind, move solemnly along the right path, draw its blessings from a single ruler, and spread his grace to every state—what room would remain for the calamities of ages past!

sentences.zh: 壽陽平，以功封聞喜縣侯，除永世令。

translations.literal: When Shouyang was pacified, by merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Wenxi county and appointed magistrate of Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouyang fell he earned the Wenxi county marquisate and magistracy of Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 溫薨，征西將軍桓豁引為參軍，領華容令。

translations.literal: When Wen died, General Who Conquers the West Huan Huo drew him in as Army Adjutant—concurrently magistrate of Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's death transferred him to General Huan Huo's western headquarters as adjutant and concurrent magistrate of Huarong.

sentences.zh: 太元中，拜著作郎，專掌國史，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era he was appointed Gentleman Compiler—solely managing dynastic history—and concurrently grand rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiyuan he became gentleman compiler in charge of national history while ranking officials for his native province.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝嘗會於西堂，滔豫坐，還，下車先呼子系之謂曰：「百人高會，天子先問伏滔在坐不，此故未易得。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once assembled at the western hall—Tao participated in seating—returning, getting off carriage first called son Xizhi saying: "A hundred-person lofty gathering—the Son of Heaven first asks whether Fu Tao is seated or not—this reason is not easily obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xiaowu held court in the western hall; Fu Tao attended. Home again he shouted for his son Xizhi: "A banquet of a hundred lords—and the emperor asks first whether Fu Tao came: few fathers earn such pride.

sentences.zh: 為人作父如此，定何如也？」

translations.literal: Acting as father for others thus—how indeed?"
translations.idiomatic: What father could wish for more?"

sentences.zh: 遷遊擊將軍，著作如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Roams and Strikes—compilation as before.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of agile strikes while keeping his compiler's duties.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子系之，亦有文才，歷黃門郎、侍中、尚書、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Xizhi also had literary talent—passed through Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Palace Attendant, Masters of Writing, and Imperial Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xizhi inherited literary gifts, rising through gentleman at the Yellow Gates, palace attendant, minister of the masters of writing, and household grandee.

sentences.zh: 羅含

translations.literal: Luo Han.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Han

sentences.zh: 羅含，字君章，桂陽耒陽人也。

translations.literal: Luo Han, style Junzhang, was a man of Leiyang in Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Han, courtesy name Junzhang, came from Leiyang in Guiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彥，臨海太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan was governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather had governed Linhai.

sentences.zh: 父綏，滎陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Sui was governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Sui governed Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 含幼孤，為叔母硃氏所養。

translations.literal: Han in youth was orphaned—was raised by aunt Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his aunt surnamed Zhu.

sentences.zh: 少有志尚，嘗晝臥，夢一鳥文彩異常，飛入口中，因驚起說之。

translations.literal: In youth he had ambition—once sleeping by day he dreamed a bird with pattern-color unusually splendid flew into his mouth—thereupon startled he rose and told it.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious even as a boy, he dreamed a brilliant bird flew into his mouth—he woke breathless and told his aunt.

sentences.zh: 硃氏曰：「鳥有文彩，汝後必有文章。」

translations.literal: Clan Zhu said: "The bird has pattern-color—you afterward must have literary compositions."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Colored feathers mean you will write brilliantly."

sentences.zh: 自此後藻思日新。

translations.literal: From this afterward ornate thought daily renewed.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his lines grew steadily finer.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州三辟，不就。

translations.literal: At the capping age the province thrice summoned—he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty the provincial office summoned him thrice; he refused.

sentences.zh: 含父嘗宰新淦，新淦人楊羨後為含州將，引含為主簿，含傲然不顧，羨招致不已，辭不獲而就焉。

translations.literal: Han's father once governed Xin'gan—Xin'gan man Yang Xian later became Han's provincial general—drew Han as chief clerk—Han proudly did not heed—Xian summoned without cease—declining did not succeed—thereupon took office.
translations.idiomatic: His father had governed Xin'gan; when local commander Yang Xian pressed him into chief clerk, Luo refused until persistence left him no graceful exit.

sentences.zh: 及羨去職，含送之到縣。

translations.literal: When Xian left office Han escorted him to the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang left office Luo escorted him clear to the county seat.

sentences.zh: 新淦人以含舊宰之子，咸致賂遺，含難違而受之。

translations.literal: Xin'gan people because Han was former magistrate's son—all presented bribes and gifts—Han hard to refuse accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Locals showered the former prefect's son with gifts; Luo reluctantly accepted.

sentences.zh: 及歸，悉封置而去。

translations.literal: When returning he entirely sealed and placed them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home he resealed every parcel untouched.

sentences.zh: 由是遠近推服焉。

translations.literal: From this far and near pushed submission to him.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors far and wide applauded his integrity.

sentences.zh: 後為郡功曹，刺史庾亮以為部江夏從事。

translations.literal: Later he was commandery Merit Assessor—Inspector Yu Liang appointed him Jiangxia staff attendant for the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as merit clerk until Inspector Yu Liang named him aide for Jiangxia affairs.

sentences.zh: 太守謝尚與含為方外之好，乃稱曰：「羅君章可謂湘中之琳琅。」

translations.literal: Governor Xie Shang with Han had friendship beyond ranks—thereupon praised saying: "Luo Junzhang can be called among Xiang's fine jades."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xie Shang, fast friends beyond ceremony, called him "the brightest jewel south of the Xiang."

sentences.zh: 尋轉州主簿。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he advanced to provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後桓溫臨州，又補征西參軍。

translations.literal: Later when Huan Wen attended the province he again supplemented West Expedition Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen took the province Luo joined his western headquarters as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 溫嘗使含詣尚，有所檢劾。

translations.literal: Wen once sent Han to visit Shang—there was something to investigate and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Huan once dispatched Luo to audit Xie Shang.

sentences.zh: 含至，不問郡事，與尚累日酣飲而還。

translations.literal: When Han arrived he did not ask about commandery affairs—with Shang for successive days drank heavily and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Luo ignored paperwork and spent days drinking with Xie before heading home.

sentences.zh: 溫問所劾事，含曰：「公謂尚何如人？」

translations.literal: Wen asked about impeachment matters—Han said: "My lord considers Shang what sort of person?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan demanded findings; Luo asked, "What do you think of Xie Shang?"

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「勝我也。」

translations.literal: Wen said: "He surpasses me."
translations.idiomatic: "He surpasses me," said Huan."

sentences.zh: 含曰：「豈有勝公而行非邪！

translations.literal: Han said: "How can there be one who surpasses my lord yet commits wrongdoing!
translations.idiomatic: "Would your better deserve impeachment?

sentences.zh: 故一無所問。」

translations.literal: Therefore altogether nothing was asked."
translations.idiomatic: So I filed nothing."

sentences.zh: 溫奇其意而不責焉。

translations.literal: Wen marveled at his intent and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan admired the wit and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 轉州別駕。

translations.literal: He transferred to provincial adjunct commander.
translations.idiomatic: He became provincial adjunct administrator.

sentences.zh: 以廨舍喧擾，于城西池小洲上立茅屋，伐木為材，織葦為席而居，布衣蔬食，晏如也。

translations.literal: Because official lodging was noisy and disturbed—on a small islet in the western pond he erected a thatched hut—cut wood for materials—wove reed for mats and dwelled—plain clothes vegetable food—serene thus.
translations.idiomatic: Office bustle drove him to a reed hut on an islet west of town—timber frame, woven mats, coarse clothes and greens—yet utterly content.

sentences.zh: 溫嘗與僚屬宴會，含後至。

translations.literal: Wen once feasted with staff members—Han arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan Wen feasted his staff; Luo arrived late.

sentences.zh: 溫問眾坐曰：「此何如人？」

translations.literal: Wen asked the seated assembly saying: "This one—what sort of person?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked the table, "What manner of man is this?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「可謂荊楚之材。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Can be called talent of Jing-Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "Among Jing-Chu's best."

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「此自江左之秀，豈惟荊楚而已。」

translations.literal: Wen said: "This is naturally the elite east of the Yangzi—how only Jing-Chu and that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied, "He stands among the finest east of the Yangzi—not merely Chu."

sentences.zh: 徵為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him as gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 溫雅重其才，又表轉征西戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Wen elegantly prized his talent—again memorialized transferring him to West Expedition Revenue Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen respected his gifts and transferred him to revenue adjutant on the western staff.

sentences.zh: 俄遷宜都太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Yidu commandery.

sentences.zh: 及溫封南郡公，引為郎中令。

translations.literal: When Wen was enfeoffed Duke of Nan commandery—drew him in as palace attendant chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan became Duke of Nanjun Luo served as his palace majordomo.

sentences.zh: 尋征正員郎，累遷散騎常侍、侍中，仍轉廷尉、長沙相。

translations.literal: Soon summoned regular gentleman—by stages promoted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant—still transferred Minister of Justice and minister of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up through regular gentleman, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, palace attendant, minister of justice, and finally chief minister to the Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 年老致仕，加中散大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Old age retired from office—added Grand Master of Palace Leisure—gate installed traveling horses.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring with age, he received the grand master of palace leisure title and the honor of carriage stakes before his gate.

sentences.zh: 初，含在官舍，有一白雀棲集堂宇，及致仕還家，階庭忽蘭菊叢生，以為德行之感焉。

translations.literal: Earlier when Han was in official lodging there was a white sparrow roosting gathered on hall roof—when retiring returning home—steps and courtyard suddenly orchid-chrysanthemum thick growing—thought it virtue conduct's sympathetic response.
translations.idiomatic: A white finch once nested on his office eaves; after retirement orchids and chrysanthemums sprouted unbidden in his courtyard—omens of virtue, people said.

sentences.zh: 年七十七卒，所著文章行於世。

translations.literal: At age seventy-seven he died—what he composed articles circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven; his essays stayed in circulation.

sentences.zh: 顧愷之

translations.literal: Gu Kaizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kaizhi

sentences.zh: 顧愷之，字長康，晉陵無錫人也。

translations.literal: Gu Kaizhi, style Changkang, was a man of Wuxi in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kaizhi, courtesy name Changkang, came from Wuxi in Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父悅之，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Yuezhi was Left Assistant to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu Yuezhi served as left aide to the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 愷之博學有才氣，嘗為《箏賦》成，謂人曰：「吾賦之比嵇康琴，不賞者必以後出相遺，深識者亦當以高奇見貴。」

translations.literal: Kaizhi broadly learned had talent and air—once he completed the "Fu on the Zheng-zither"—said to people: "My fu compared to Ji Kang's qin—those who do not appreciate must because later produced discard them—those deeply discerning also ought because lofty strange deem them precious."
translations.idiomatic: Learned and spirited, he finished his "Rhapsody on the Zither" and declared, "Critics will dismiss it as derivative next to Ji Kang's qin pieces; true judges will prize its strangeness and height."

sentences.zh: 桓溫引為大司馬參軍，甚見親昵。

translations.literal: Huan Wen drew him in as Grand Marshal Army Adjutant—greatly seen intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen named him grand marshal adjutant and treated him almost as family.

sentences.zh: 溫薨後，愷之拜溫墓，賦詩云：「山崩溟海竭，魚鳥將何依！」

translations.literal: After Wen died Kaizhi bowed at Wen's tomb—composed poetry saying: "Mountain collapses dark seas dry up—fish and birds will rely on what!"
translations.idiomatic: At Huan Wen's tomb he mourned in verse: "Mountains fall and seas run dry—where shall fish and birds turn?"

sentences.zh: 或問之曰：「卿憑重桓公乃爾，哭狀其可見乎？」

translations.literal: Someone asked him saying: "You rely on and esteem Duke Huan thus—weeping appearance—can it be seen?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked whether grief for Huan Wen showed on his face."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「聲如震雷破山，淚如傾河注海。」

translations.literal: He replied saying: "Sound like thunder shaking mountains—tears like overturning river pouring into sea."
translations.idiomatic: "Thunder splitting cliffs and a river pouring into the sea," he said."

sentences.zh: 愷之好諧謔，人多愛狎之。

translations.literal: Kaizhi loved jest and banter—people mostly loved to be intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of wit, he was everyone's favorite companion.

sentences.zh: 後為殷仲堪參軍，亦深被眷接。

translations.literal: Later he was Yin Zhongkan's Army Adjutant—also deeply received loving reception.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Zhongkan prized him equally as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 仲堪在荊州，愷之嘗因假還，仲堪特以布帆借之，至破塚，遭風大敗。

translations.literal: When Zhongkan was in Jingzhou Kaizhi once because leave returned—Zhongkan specially lent him cloth sail—arriving at Broken Tomb—encountered wind great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: While Yin governed Jingzhou Gu borrowed cloth sails for leave home; at Broken Tomb a gale shredded them.

sentences.zh: 愷之與仲堪箋曰：「地名破塚，真破塚而出。

translations.literal: Kaizhi wrote Zhongkan a note saying: "Place name Broken Tomb—truly broke tomb and emerged.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Yin, "The place lives up to its name—we smashed through the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 行人安穩，布帆無恙。」

translations.literal: Travelers peaceful stable—cloth sail without illness."
translations.idiomatic: Travelers are safe and your sails intact."

sentences.zh: 還至荊州，人問以會稽山川之狀。

translations.literal: Returning to Jingzhou people asked him about Guiji mountains and rivers' forms.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Jingzhou friends asked him to describe Kuaiji's scenery.

sentences.zh: 愷之云：「千岩競秀，萬壑爭流。

translations.literal: Kaizhi said: "Thousand cliffs vie in splendor—ten thousand ravines contend in flowing.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Cliffs beyond counting vie in splendor; streams without number race downhill.

sentences.zh: 草木蒙籠，若雲興霞蔚。」

translations.literal: Plants and trees mist-shrouded—as clouds rise rosy clouds lush."
translations.idiomatic: Mists braid the foliage like clouds lifting into sunset glow."

sentences.zh: 桓玄時與愷之同在仲堪坐，共作了語。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was together with Kaizhi at Zhongkan's seating—they jointly composed threat phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan Xuan joined Gu and Yin Zhongkan in a word game of perilous lines.

sentences.zh: 愷之先曰：「火燒平原無遺燎。」

translations.literal: Kaizhi first said: "Fire burns plain leaving no remnant blaze."
translations.idiomatic: Gu opened: "Wildfire sweeps the plain—nothing left but ash."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「白布纏根樹旒旐。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "White cloth wraps root tree funeral banners."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan answered, "White hemp wraps the roots—mourning banners flutter."

sentences.zh: 仲堪曰：「投魚深泉放飛鳥。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan said: "Cast fish deep spring release flying bird."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "Fish tossed into deep pools; birds loosed to the sky."

sentences.zh: 復作危語。

translations.literal: Again composed peril phrases.
translations.idiomatic: They turned to deadly riddles.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「矛頭淅米劍頭炊。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Spear tip rinses rice sword tip cooks."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Rinse rice on a spearpoint; boil stew on a sword edge."

sentences.zh: 仲堪曰：「百歲老翁攀枯枝。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan said: "Hundred-year old man climbs withered branch."
translations.idiomatic: Yin answered, "A hundred-year-old climbs a rotten limb."

sentences.zh: 有一參軍云：「盲人騎瞎馬臨深池。」

translations.literal: One army adjutant said: "Blind man rides blind horse facing deep pool."
translations.idiomatic: An aide added, "A blind man on a blind stallion above a deep pool."

sentences.zh: 仲堪眇目，驚曰：「此太逼人！」

translations.literal: Zhongkan had small eye—startled said: "This too presses person!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin—half blind—cried, "That cuts too close!"

sentences.zh: 因罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The game ended.

sentences.zh: 愷之每食甘蔗，恆自尾至本。

translations.literal: Kaizhi whenever ate sugarcane always from tail to root.
translations.idiomatic: Gu always ate sugarcane from the thin tip toward the thick root.

sentences.zh: 人或怪之，云：「漸入佳境。」

translations.literal: People perhaps wondered at it—said: "Gradually entering fine realm."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he smiled, "So sweetness deepens—" entering a finer realm step by step.

sentences.zh: 尤善丹青，圖寫特妙，謝安深重之，以為有蒼生以來未之有也。

translations.literal: Especially skilled at cinnabar-green painting—drawing and writing especially marvelous—Xie An deeply prized him—thought since dark-haired folk arose never been such.
translations.idiomatic: His brushwork was supreme; Xie An deemed him unmatched since civilization began.

sentences.zh: 愷之每畫人成，或數年不點目精。

translations.literal: Kaizhi whenever painted people finished—sometimes several years did not dot eye pupils.
translations.idiomatic: Often he left faces unfinished for years—especially the eyes.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，答曰：「四體妍蚩，本無闕少於妙處，傳神寫照，正在阿堵中。」

translations.literal: People asked its reason—he replied saying: "Four limbs beautiful or ugly—originally without lack in subtle places—transmitting spirit portraying illumination—just right in that very spot."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Limbs matter little for likeness; capturing spirit—that lives in those dots we call eyes."

sentences.zh: 嘗悅一鄰女，挑之弗從，乃圖其形於壁，以棘針釘其心，女遂患心痛。

translations.literal: Once he favored a neighboring girl—teased her—she did not comply—thereupon drew her form on wall—used thorn needle to nail her heart—the girl thereupon suffered heart pain.
translations.idiomatic: Spurned by a neighbor girl, he painted her on a wall and drove thorns into the breast—she doubled over with chest pain.

sentences.zh: 愷之因致其情，女從之，遂密去針而愈。

translations.literal: Kaizhi thereupon conveyed his feeling—the girl followed him—thereupon secretly removed needle and recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When he confessed and she yielded, he pulled out the thorns and she healed.

sentences.zh: 愷之每重嵇康四言詩，因為之圖，恆云：「手揮五弦易，目送歸鴻難。」

translations.literal: Kaizhi always prized Ji Kang's four-character poems—thereupon for them drew pictures—always saying: "Hand strums five strings easy—eyes send returning wild goose hard."
translations.idiomatic: He illustrated Ji Kang's quatrains, sighing, "Strumming the five strings is easy—painting the gaze that follows the wild goose is hard."

sentences.zh: 每寫起人形，妙絕于時。

translations.literal: Whenever wrote raising human forms—marvelous unsurpassed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Portraits from his brush had no peer in his day.

sentences.zh: 嘗圖裴楷象，頰上加三毛，觀者覺神明殊勝。

translations.literal: Once he drew Pei Kai's likeness—on cheeks added three hairs—observers felt spirit illumination surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: Three extra hairs on Pei Kai's cheeks brought the likeness eerily alive.

sentences.zh: 又為謝鯤象，在石岩裏，云：「此子宜置丘壑中。」

translations.literal: Again for Xie Kun's likeness—inside stone cliff—said: "This fellow ought be placed amid hills and valleys."
translations.idiomatic: He set Xie Kun among cliff rocks, noting, "This man belongs in wild hills."

sentences.zh: 欲圖殷仲堪，仲堪有目病，固辭。

translations.literal: Wishing to draw Yin Zhongkan—Zhongkan had eye illness—firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan, ashamed of his eyes, refused to sit.

sentences.zh: 愷之曰：「明府正為眼耳，若明點瞳子，飛白拂上，使如輕雲之蔽月，豈不美乎！」

translations.literal: Kaizhi said: "My enlightened prefect precisely because of eyes—if clearly dot pupils—flying white brush across—make like light clouds veiling moon—how could it not be beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: Gu insisted, "Precisely those eyes—I'll dot the pupils and veil them with dry strokes like thin clouds crossing the moon."

sentences.zh: 仲堪乃從之。

translations.literal: Zhongkan thereupon followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin relented.

sentences.zh: 愷之嘗以一廚畫糊題其前，寄桓玄，皆其深所珍惜者。

translations.literal: Kaizhi once by means of one chest of paintings pasted sealed its front—sent to Huan Xuan—all were what he deeply treasured.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed a chest of his dearest paintings and sent them to Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄乃發其廚後，竊取畫，而緘閉如舊以還之，紿雲未開。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon opened its chest rear—secretly took paintings—yet sealed closed like old to return them—deceived saying not opened.
translations.idiomatic: Huan slit the back, stole the scrolls, resealed the chest, and returned it untouched—or so he claimed.

sentences.zh: 愷之見封題如初，但失其畫，直雲妙畫通靈，變化而去，亦猶人之登仙，了無怪色。

translations.literal: Kaizhi saw seal inscription like first—but lost its paintings—straight said marvelous paintings penetrated spirits—transformed and departed—also like people's ascending immortals—utterly without strange expression.
translations.idiomatic: Finding seals intact but paintings gone, Gu declared spirits had spirited them away—as mortals ascend to immortality—without blinking.

sentences.zh: 愷之矜伐過實，少年因相稱譽以為戲弄。

translations.literal: Kaizhi boasted bragging exceeded reality—young men therefore mutually praised him taking it as jesting.
translations.idiomatic: Youths mocked his boastfulness by showering him with fake praise.

sentences.zh: 又為吟詠，自謂得先賢風制。

translations.literal: Again he did chanting recitation—himself thought he obtained former worthies' wind pattern.
translations.idiomatic: His poems aped ancient masters—or so he believed.

sentences.zh: 或請其作洛生詠，答曰：「何至作老婢聲！」

translations.literal: Someone requested him perform Luoyang scholar chanting—he replied saying: "How reach making old maidservant voice!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked to chant in the Luoyang accent he sneered, "I won't croak like some Luoyang hag!"

sentences.zh: 義熙初，為散騎常侍，與謝瞻連省，夜於月下長詠，瞻每遙贊之，愷之彌自力忘倦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi he was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary—together with Xie Zhan linked province—night under moon long chanting—Zhan each from afar praised him—Kaizhi more exerted himself forgetting weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yixi he served as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary alongside Xie Zhan; moonlit nights he declaimed while Xie cheered from afar until dawn unaware of fatigue.

sentences.zh: 瞻將眠，令人代己，愷之不覺有異，遂申旦而止。

translations.literal: Zhan about to sleep—ordered someone substitute for himself—Kaizhi did not perceive there was difference—thereupon stretched till dawn then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie slipped off to bed he left a stand-in applauding; Gu never noticed and kept reciting until sunrise.

sentences.zh: 尤信小術，以為求之必得。

translations.literal: Especially believed petty arts—thought seeking them must obtain.
translations.idiomatic: He dabbled in petty magic and trusted every charm.

sentences.zh: 桓玄嘗以一柳葉紿之曰：「此蟬所翳葉也，取以自蔽，人不見己。」

translations.literal: Huan Xuan once by means of one willow leaf deceived him saying: "This is the leaf cicadas use for concealment—take it to conceal yourself—people will not see oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan once handed him a willow leaf: "Cicadas hide beneath this—hold it and vanish from sight."

sentences.zh: 愷之喜，引葉自蔽，玄就溺焉，愷之信其不見己也，甚以珍之。

translations.literal: Kaizhi rejoiced—drew leaf concealing himself—Xuan approached urinating there—Kaizhi believed they did not see himself—greatly thereby treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: Gu hid his eyes with it while Huan relieved himself; Gu believed no one could see him and prized the leaf.

sentences.zh: 初，愷之在桓溫府，常云：「愷之體中癡黠各半，合而論之，正得平耳。」

translations.literal: Earlier when Kaizhi was in Huan Wen's headquarters he often said: "Within Kaizhi's substance folly and cleverness each half—combined discussing them—just obtain balance."
translations.idiomatic: Serving Huan Wen he used to say, "Half my nature is foolish, half clever—average them and you get mediocrity."

sentences.zh: 故俗傳愷之有三絕：才絕，畫絕，癡絕。

translations.literal: Therefore vulgar tradition transmits Kaizhi had three unsurpasseds: talent unsurpassed, painting unsurpassed, folly unsurpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence people say Gu Kaizhi had three supreme gifts—genius, brushwork, and glorious folly.

sentences.zh: 年六十二，卒於官，所著文集及《啟䑃記》行於世。

translations.literal: At age sixty-two he died in office—what he composed collected writings and "Record of Qimeng" circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-two; his literary collection and "Notes on Awakening the Veil" circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 郭澄之

translations.literal: Guo Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengshi

sentences.zh: 郭澄之，字仲靜，太原陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Guo Chengshi, style Zhongjing, was a man of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengshi, courtesy name Zhongjing, hailed from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少有才思，機敏兼人。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and thought—alert quickness doubled others.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted from youth, he outpaced peers.

sentences.zh: 調補尚書郎，出為南康相。

translations.literal: Transferred filled Gentleman of the Masters of Writing—went out as minister of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to gentleman of the masters of writing, then became chief minister to the Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 值盧循作逆，流離僅得還都。

translations.literal: Encountering Lu Xun raising rebellion—wandering scattering barely able to return capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's rebellion uprooted him; he barely escaped back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉裕引為相國參軍。

translations.literal: Liu Yu drew him in as Army Adjutant to the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu enlisted him as adjutant to the minister of state.

sentences.zh: 從裕北伐，既克長安，裕意更欲西伐，集僚屬議之，多不同。

translations.literal: Following Yu on northern expedition—already conquered Chang'an—Yu's intent further wished western expedition—gathered staff members to deliberate—many did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: On Liu Yu's northern campaign, after Chang'an fell Liu wished to push west; his staff mostly demurred.

sentences.zh: 次問澄之，澄之不答，西向誦王粲詩曰：「南登霸陵岸，回首望長安。」

translations.literal: Next asked Chengshi—Chengshi did not answer—westward chanted Wang Can's poem saying: "South ascend Overlord Tomb shore—turn head gaze Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Asked next, Guo remained silent, then faced west and recited Wang Can: "Climbing Baling southward I turned toward Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 裕便意定，謂澄之曰：「當與卿共登霸陵岸耳。」

translations.literal: Yu thereupon intent settled—said to Chengshi: "Ought with you jointly ascend Overlord Tomb shore."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu understood: "Then we climb Baling together—no farther west."

sentences.zh: 因還。

translations.literal: Thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the western march.

sentences.zh: 澄之位至裕相國從事中郎，封南豐侯，卒於官，所著文集行於世。

translations.literal: Chengshi's rank reached Yu's minister of state Staff Officer—enfeoffed Marquis of Nanfeng—died in office—what he composed collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to middle staff officer under Liu Yu's ministerate, received the Nanfeng marquisate, died in harness, and left a literary collection.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫賞好生於情，剛柔本於性，情之所適，發乎詠歌，而感召無象，風律殊制。

translations.literal: The historians say: As for appreciation and fondness born from emotion—hard and soft rooted in nature—where emotion suits—it issues forth in chanting song—yet sympathetic resonance has no image—wind and rhythm have distinct patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Taste springs from disposition, tone from temperament; feeling seeks outlet in song, yet resonance follows no fixed image and prosody admits endless forms.

sentences.zh: 至於應貞宴射之文，極形言之美，華林群藻罕或疇之。

translations.literal: As for Ying Zhen's banquet archery writing—it exhausts the beauty of shaped language—Hualin's crowd of literary ornament rarely may equal it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen's verses from the Hualin archery banquet exhaust the splendor of language—few poems from that grove rival them.

sentences.zh: 子安幼標明敏，少蓄清思，懷天地之寥廓，賦辭人之所遺，特構新情，豈常均之所企！

translations.literal: Zi'an in youth displayed bright keenness—in youth stored pure thought—embracing heaven and earth's vast emptiness—composing what literary men abandoned—specially framing new feeling—how could vulgar averages aspire!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui showed brilliance young; brooding on cosmos-wide themes he reclaimed what lesser poets discarded—inventions beyond ordinary ambition.

sentences.zh: 太沖含豪曆載，以賦《三都》，士安見而稱善，平原睹而韜翰，匪惟高步當年，故以騰華終古。

translations.literal: Taichong embraced brush lasting years—to compose the "Three Capitals"—Shian saw and praised good—Pingyuan viewed and sheathed brush—not only high steps in that age—therefore by soaring splendor endures forever.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si nursed his "Three Capitals" for ages; Huangfu Mi praised it and Lu Ji laid down his brush—not merely foremost in his day but luminous for all time.

sentences.zh: 鄒湛之持論，棗據之緣情，實南陽之人傑，蓋潁川之時秀。

translations.literal: Zou Zhan's holding discourse—Zao Ju's following emotion—truly Nanyang's human elite—indeed Yingchuan's timely elite.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan's essays and Zao Ju's lyric passion crown Nanyang and Yingchuan alike.

sentences.zh: 季雅摛屬遒邁，夙備成德，稱為泉岱之珍，固其然矣。

translations.literal: Jiya's unfolding compositions forceful far-reaching—early prepared completed virtue—called springs and Mount Tai's treasures—solidly thus indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tao's prose strides boldly; ripened early in virtue, hailed as treasure beside sacred springs and Taishan—deservedly so.

sentences.zh: 彥伯未能混跡光塵，而屈乎卑位，《釋時》宏論，亦足見其志耳。

translations.literal: Yanbo could not mingle traces in light dust—yet bent to humble station—the "Explaining the Age" grand discourse—also suffices to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen never blended with the powerful yet languished lowly; his "Discourse on Our Times" reveals his mind.

sentences.zh: 季鷹縱誕一時，不邀名爵，《黃花》之什，浚發神府。

translations.literal: Jiying unrestrained wild for one age—not inviting rank titles—the "Yellow Flowers" suite—deeply dredges spirit treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han frolicked outside convention, spurning titles; his "Yellow Blossom" poems unlock the soul.

sentences.zh: 仲初之文，風流可尚，擢秀士林，《揚都》之美，尤重時彥。

translations.literal: Zhongchu's writings—wind flow worthy to esteem—plucking excellence among scholar woods—the "Yang Capital"'s beauty—especially weighted among age's elites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan's polished prose lifts him among writers; his "Yang Capital" rhapsody drew especial praise from contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 曹毗沈研秘笈，踠足下僚，綺靡降神之歌，朗暢《對儒》之論。

translations.literal: Cao Pi sinks studying secret texts—curving foot serving lower staff—luxuriant descending-spirit songs—bright smooth "Response to Ru" discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi plumbed arcane lore despite humble posts; his goddess songs shimmer and his "Reply to the Scholars" rings clear.

sentences.zh: 李充之《學箴》，信清壯也。

translations.literal: Li Chong's "Admonition on Learning"—indeed pure and robust.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong's "Admonition on Learning" is taut and forceful indeed.

sentences.zh: 袁宏《東征》、《名臣》之作，抑潘陸之亞。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong's "Eastern Expedition" and "Famous Ministers" compositions—perhaps Pan and Lu's peers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's Eastern Expedition and famed-minister eulogies rank beside Pan Yue and Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 玄度學藝優瞻，筆削擅奇，降帝問於西堂，故其榮觀也。

translations.literal: Xuandu's learning arts abundant surveying—brush editing monopolizes marvel—descending emperor questioned at western hall—therefore his glorious spectacle.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao's erudition and editorial genius drew the emperor's queries in the western hall—signal honor.

sentences.zh: 君章耀湘中之寶，挺荊楚之材，夢鳥發乎精誠，豈獨日者之蛟鳳！

translations.literal: Junzhang shines Xiang's midst treasure—straightens Jing-Chu's timber—dream bird issues from refined sincerity—how only diviner's horn dragon phoenix!
translations.idiomatic: Luo Han gleams as pearl of the Xiang lands; his bird dream sprang from utter sincerity—not mere augury of dragons and phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 長康矜能過實，譚諧取容，而才多逸氣，故有三絕之目。

translations.literal: Changkang boasts ability exceeding reality—talk harmony seeks acceptance—yet talent much roaming spirit—therefore has three unsurpasseds' label.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kaizhi overstated his gifts yet charmed every circle; genius and eccentricity earned him the "three supremacies."

sentences.zh: 仲靜機思通敏，延譽清流，德輿西伐之計，取定於微指者矣。

translations.literal: Zhongjing plan thought penetrating quick—extending fame clear stream—virtue carriage western expedition plan—decision taken from subtle pointing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengshi's agile counsel won renown among purists; his subtle quotation decided Liu Yu's western campaign.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：爻彖垂法，宮征流音。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Hexagram statements hang down law—palace modes flow sound.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Changes set patterns; pentatonic scales carry tone.

sentences.zh: 美哉群彥，揚蕤翰林。

translations.literal: Beautiful alas crowd of elites—raise flowering Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: How fair these masters, flourishing in literature's grove.

sentences.zh: 俱諧振玉，各擅鏘金。

translations.literal: Together harmonize vibrating jade—each monopolizes ringing gold.
translations.idiomatic: Each voice rings like jade, each stroke clangs like bronze.

sentences.zh: 子安、太沖，遒文綺爛。

translations.literal: Zi'an, Taichong—forceful writings patterned brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui and Zuo Si wield blazing, muscular prose.

sentences.zh: 袁、庾、充、愷，縟藻霞煥。

translations.literal: Yuan, Yu, Chong, Kai—dense ornament rosy clouds radiant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Yu, Li, and Gu weave iridescent, sunset-rich lines.

sentences.zh: 架彼辭人，共超清貫。

translations.literal: Frame those literary men—together transcend pure penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Beside earlier masters they ascend toward lucid perfection.
